title: Tyson Bagent, Case Keenum on first preseason game vs. Browns | Press Conference
text: Guys, how did it feel out there today? First half, assessment? >> Yeah, I think as far as the assessment goes from a personal level, I think it's nowhere close to my standards, especially how we started off. You know, going into this first preseason game, thinking back to the first preseason game last year, we had two three-and-outs, and then I threw a touchdown to Hardman. So, I'm like, "Hey, let's just start a little bit faster than that." And then we had two three-and-outs, and then I threw a touchdown to Hardman. So, hopefully next year when preseason one rolls around, we can change that up a little bit, but I thought we did a great job of staying the course. Second quarter, obviously, there were a lot of explosive plays within that quarter. I thought Cayden Davis did a great job running fast. And I thought some of those young guys up front getting to a lot of meaningful reps with the guy with some of the guys that we have out. So, a lot of good things, but um as far as individually, definitely would like to you know, obviously got to continue to get better this camp and and put a better foot forward starting off next week. >> Tyson, where did you the the hiccups came in those first couple of drives? >> Yeah, it just comes from obviously well, so the first drive they you know, I thought they played good coverage on that first third down. Second third down, you know, the ball just gets high on me. I got to put it right on right in the middle of Rausch's chest plate. And I think that's just the extent of it. You know, the ball went to exactly who it's supposed to go to. Just all about ball placement and being able to move the chains on third down. >> Your coaches and the other quarterbacks in comparison talk you know, talk about how valuable you are to them on the practice field and in the meeting room. But, is it something different when you can show it on the field for the world to see? You know, you've been really good in these preseason settings since you came out of college. >> Yeah, I think that you never know when when a when a moment's going to you know, arise. So, I think being able to attack each rep like it's your last and and really steward it the best that you can is the only way to operate. So, that you know, that's what I try to do. You know, I spend a lot of time on the sideline watching the games the past two years especially, so when my name is called upon being able to you know give confidence to the coaches that I you know I know what I'm doing that I'm able to be a coach out there on the field for these guys. Um and you know be successful and keep the chains moving and put points up on the board. >> We've seen other quarterbacks foreign starters talk about they believe they're one of the 32 guys starters. You're the best quarterbacks walking the earth right now. Do you have that type of belief factor yourself? >> No, 100%. I think that you know in order to be a successful quarterback in this business you have to have an unrealistic confidence about yourself. Um and as far as I'm concerned just like I said I mean there was a lot of success in that first half but there's also a lot of unacceptable things that took place to where if I am going to be one of those 32 guys that you know I got to play at a higher level. Um and you know really just got to start fast. You know, nobody wants to go three and out on the first two drives. Um so obviously got to improve on that if I am going to be one of those guys in the near future. >> I saw the touchdown to Hardman happen and that play through your eyes. >> Yeah, we had a we had a cross concept called little half roll to the left. They went cover two invert on us. Safety didn't do a good enough job taking away the mid cross. Little bit of pressure in my face. So I was able to give Hardman something he could work with and then obviously he was able to do the rest from there but I thought it was a good play call and I thought everybody executed pretty well. You know, obviously got to look at the tape but I thought it was a pretty solid play call. >> I know already with Randall El started calling plays but what was that experience like from your vantage point and even him even sitting in on the quarterback meetings kind of drawing up some plays and talking about some of the bigger >> Yeah, I mean has anybody ever had a better first outing than Antwaan Randle El? When it comes to calling plays I thought he did a great job. Um but you know that's just who he is. He's always prepared. He knows the ins and outs of the playbook. So it was really not surprising for at least us on the sideline to see the amount of success that we were able to have in the second half. >> Kaden Kaden Davis has had a really good camp. Made that big 41-yarder for him today. I was curious, too, on that just not just that play, but your perspective on the block that he laid to then clear the path that you were on the sideline at that point, but to clear the path for Akrum's touchdown. >> Yeah, I think that's just kind of who he is. You know, in the receiver room, um as far as I'm concerned, it's no block, no rock. So, you know, if you're not throwing your hat and getting your face a little bit dirty on the run plays or screens, for that matter, then you know, you're they're going to be less inclined to get you the ball. So, I think that's just who he is, where he's supposed to be, when he's supposed to be there, and just really just playing his heart out, you know, for the man beside him, which was that was really the message going into this game. >> Has there been an >> [clears throat] >> official Has there been an official jersey exchange with with Brent Doyle? >> Oh, yeah. Um No, he does not I don't think he's got my He might, but you know, I don't think he's got mine yet, but yeah, shout out to Brent Doyle. Super stoked to have him in the city of Chicago. So, just Shepherd guys being able to make a name for himself. He's done extremely well for himself, so excited to have him. >> Is this game worn? >> No, no, this is not game worn. Uh that is just me being extremely late. Complete sloppy move on my on my part. uh got to you know, got to be better there. I think one less hitch will get the job done, or you know, just move on. Move on to the next progression, throw it in the dirt, but by all means, do not throw an interception. >> How much emphasis on that Akrum touchdown that Chase threw? He seemed to want to down that regardless of where your yards that was a 49-yard touchdown pass as a quarterback. >> Yeah, I think you go home and you're able to tell your girlfriend, your wife, your kids that [snorts] you threw a 50-yard touchdown. You know, that it all counts as yards for us. Um I thought he did a good job with pressure in his face being able to have a throw a free throw over the guy and um give Savon a chance. So, um I thought it was a great play on his part. >> Were you able to listen back to Al calling plays during that portion? >> Yes. >> Okay, so what was your experience just kind of being a spectator or watching that unfold for you? >> Yeah, I mean I thought it was great. I mean he was reporting to Ben who then was reporting to the quarterback. So, it was still Ben's voice. Um but I thought that, you know, there was no let up at all and you know, like I said before, I don't know if there's ever been somebody that's been that successful their first time calling plays. So, hats off to him and hats off to the execution by those guys in the third and fourth quarter. >> What's up, guys? I'm great. How are y'all? >> I know it rolled in the third quarter there a little bit. What was your advantage point the way the offense flowed there? >> Yeah, it felt good. Um you know, it was really nice. Uh I don't know if coach has said it, but Al got to call call the the second half for me and for my couple of drives and uh I loved it. I I got into immediate rhythm with him. Uh I thought uh I thought the guys up front, uh especially some of the newer guys, you know, some of the young guys that was really getting their first taste of of action played really well. Uh communication was good in the huddle. Uh couple of tight ends and and receivers too that was their first time. Uh and then, you know, like a guy like Ray Ray who I met on, you know, 3 days ago. I thought made some big plays for us today, too. So, uh I enjoyed it. I had a lot of fun. Um I don't care where you are. Throwing touchdowns and and moving the ball down the field is fun. So, >> The screen [clears throat] back man, obviously you can't you know, how that came together and then you did the rest of the end. But what was your sense of just the whole flow of that play? >> Yeah, I I tell uh I tell the QB room those all those count all those passing yards. So, they did all the work. Uh you know, I just managed to get it up and over and guys did a great job of blocking down field. And man, those those cutbacks cross court um, you know, when you have a guy like that with speed and and the eye for vision for that, we work screens all the time and uh you know, it showed on that play uh and a couple of other ones, too. So, I'm excited to see those guys getting space like that. >> Ben was mentioning how you had two penalties all game, how clean it was, especially for preseason opener. How did you guys feel like you performed that way? >> Yeah, like I said, I mean, the communication was really good in the huddle offensively. Um you know, and and when you have a lot of guys in and out of the game young guys, you know, you don't know who's up, who's down at this point to be able to substitute, too. So, communication on the sideline was was very well and when you have guys playing hard, sometimes those penalties happen during the snap, but uh for us to not have those, I thought um, you know helped us keep the ball moving and scoring lots of points. >> What did you see Go ahead. What did you see about Kade Warner? This is a guy that's kind of emerging camp and okay, you brought him to today. >> Yeah, we have a deep receiver room uh and that really helps the quarterback room when it comes to preseason. So uh you know, especially when we had some guys that didn't play today. So yeah, Kade has has the speed down the field. He can threaten um, you know, big strider um, and uh you know, like all those guys today, when we were able to get him in space and make make plays down the field um, and he's played some ball. So, he's experienced. He's a guy we can count on to be in the right place at the right time when we need him to be there. So, uh yeah, I've uh really enjoyed it throwing him the ball. >> Ben mentioned that he thinks he could be an offensive coordinator and a head coach in this league. You know, you talked about him a little bit earlier, but in your time working with him, what maybe gives you that same kind of impression? >> Yeah, I know he's going to be a head coach. Um I think uh his demeanor in front of the team, his leadership qualities are top notch. Uh some of the best I've been around. Uh his relatability to players, man. I mean, the fact that he's been there, done that it just about everything. Um and you know, there's no like >> [sighs] >> you know, for lack of better word, coach speak to him. It's all real. And it's it's uh it's very relatable. Um you know, and his knowledge of ball. Uh you know, he's been a part of a lot of systems and he is a master of Ben's system. Um you know, extension of him in that receiver room. Which in in this system, I would think is probably besides the quarterbacks I don't know. They're all hard rooms to coach cuz cuz Ben's very demanding, but man, to to get those guys detailed up on where to line up you know, when to be in the right spot, when it's man, when it's zone, the rules in different routes and and coverages. Uh Uh I mean, he's on it. And uh it's it was it was fun to be a part of him calling his first time calling plays today. >> So, what was notable about the way he called plays and also maybe just the way you guys prepared knowing that he was going to have the the wheel? >> Yeah, one, he liked to throw it. So, >> [laughter] >> uh and he told us he was, you know, and so that was even when the forecast called for a ton of rain. So, um which I I don't mind. I like it. We know where we're cutting, they don't know where we're cutting. So, but it just it felt comfortable. You know, I felt like I I knew what he was trying to get. You know, we call it play caller's intent and he did a great job of of uh you know, kind of whatever the situation was feeling out and and getting you know, to a play that I thought uh you know, gave us a good chance to make plays. Um you know, we got to go.

title: Ben Johnson on Bears' performance vs. Browns | Press Conference
text: Okay, a few guys that didn't uh didn't finish through there. So, Nico has a right knee, um didn't finish the game. Xavier Woods had a groin, didn't finish. Uh Nephi Sewell had a concussion, so he's in protocol right now. And then Reuben has a shoulder, so we'll keep uh we'll keep looking at at that as we go through the week here. Um man, proud of our guys and how they played. We talked about uh being disciplined in all three phases and and uh we really saw today, I think two penalties on the day from from all three phases. We haven't had a practice yet where we've had that few fouls. So, that was really encouraging to see. They took that to heart. Um I don't know if I've been a part of a preseason one where that's been the case in my career. So, credit to them. Um and then we talked about being physical, being uh fast, being detailed. I I thought our guys were able to cut it loose. We simplified the game plans from what we've been doing in practice and just let them go out there and play. And I thought the the fundamentals, the technique showed up. I thought our defense was tackling for the most part. Uh when they had opportunities offensively, we had some detail there in the passing game. Quarterbacks were fairly accurate with the football. Um but it'll be really good tape for us to look at and it's a it's a good start as we get going. If you notice a difference in terms of offensive execution and uh it looked better in the second half, that's a that's really because of Antoine Randall El calling it there in the second half. I thought he did a phenomenal job, um you know, with Case taking the reins and then transition on over to Miller just to see how he was he was trying to stay in their wheelhouse. He was part of the quarterback meeting last night and you know, we're we're talking about what was on the call sheet and their favorites and all that and uh you know, I I I think it was it was a phenomenal experience for him and and I know our guys really rallied around that as well. So, I open it up from there. >> Why did you end up play calling duties at all? Why him specifically? >> Yeah, well, I think we might might take a look at a couple guys here during uh during the preseason. You know, last year Declan had an opportunity in one of those games to do the second half. Um and so I I wanted I wanted L to get that that chance and he wanted it too. I mean, he I think he's an outstanding coach and I think sometimes when you're put in certain position rooms, you kind of get labeled one thing or another and and here's the thing about L. I think he's got chance to be an offensive coordinator in this league. I think he's got a chance to be a head coach in this league. I think he would do a phenomenal job in both those respects and I I just I don't know if he gets that that type of credit around the league right now. So, it's a good opportunity for him to to get some recognition. >> The screen play that I'm mad that got out of the gate well, what was your vantage point on what made that all click? >> Oh, shoot. You know, we've been harping on those details. We got specific landmarks. We drill them every single day. I think our defense has done a really good job throughout the week of practice to make those hard for so we've had a lot of very difficult looks. Some of our worst plays in practice over the last couple weeks have been have been our screens. And so, um you know, I just think it's a really good job up front executing the timing, the rhythm and then you know, we we always talk about those screen runners when they get the ball in their hands. We're trying to get vertical for a few steps and then turns into a punt return after that and then that's certainly what that one looked like as he was taking it across the field. So, good to see those guys blocking down the field. A guy like Cayden Davis who really is trying to run coverage away from the screen ends up making a key block and and it's good to see things like that. >> How did you feel the rotation at left tackle between Quran and >> Yeah, yeah, I think I that's a hard one for me to assess right now. Um sometimes that trench play you got to you got to go ahead and take a look at the you know, the lens from behind and and really be able to take a look at it, but as a whole, I would say offense line, I felt like our quarterback got hit more than I would like. Tyson certainly did in the first half and second half we still felt some pressures there on on Case and and Miller. So, we'll look at why that was the case and then running game wise was a little bit spotty as well. So, different style of defense certainly attributes to that. Their front is coming off the ball and they make it very difficult for one-on-one blocks. You got to be very specific with your angles and all that and so there there's a back and forth there in the running game as well. So, hard to say a whole lot about left tackle quite yet. >> Setting aside today the first team offense, how ready do you feel like that group is now with less than a month till season starts? >> Yeah, I I I feel really good about where those guys are at. We had a phenomenal throwing session before we got going today and that was by design. I mean we got over 60 plays that we're able to simulate, you know, [clears throat] going in a huddle, calling the play, talking through the coaching points, the footwork, the timing, the rhythm. I thought all those guys that didn't play in the game, they we needed that. I think that's how you get better at the passing game is you got to have days like that. So, it was a good time to do it. We'll assess whether we we need to play in the next couple games as we go through these joint practices here and and we'll see where we're at as a team, but I'm happy with what the the offense looks like right now and yet we're only halfway through this thing and and we got a long ways to go. >> This time last year, even later in the camp, into August last year, you were voiced a lot of frustrations. >> Yeah. >> What do you feel like is bothering you right now? What do you feel like still needs to be cleaned up? >> Well, my concerns last year were a lot with the pre-snap um and I I don't have we don't have those procedure issues to that degree anymore and so um provided we can keep those to a minimum, I think that's where we'll continue to get better. I think our defense is going to continue to get better cuz they're facing a clean unit as well and you know, we'll see what it looks like going against a couple new opponents. I I know like I'm excited to go down to Cincinnati and they've got a lot of new talent on defense that uh uh that we're going to have to be on our P's and Q's if we want to have success against. And so um that to me is going to help help us really shape where we're at as an offense right now. >> What impressed you about Jabari today? >> Oh yeah, I mean it's it's something um you see it in the springtime the new techniques that we're coaching with and he's flashing and yet it's like is this is this the time he's going to turn it on? And you don't know and then you go into a game like this and you see the get-off, you see the relentlessness. Um I mean he you could feel his presence every single snap. And I got I you know I'm standing close to the D-linemen and they're just they're hooting and hollering and cheering for him because they're as excited as he is cuz they're seeing him going out there making plays and making an impact like that. He's such a hard worker. Um I know he's been in the program now for a minute and uh to see him have some success on the field like that that was huge. >> With that being what he's showing you that whether he can be this this running back and and his fit with this offense. >> Yeah, well I mean I think we know we feel good about those top two backs right now and where they're at. So the battle for three, four, five, whatever that looks like uh a lot comes down to special teams, a lot comes down to how do you separate yourself from those top two guys, what's your skill set, how's it different. Um you know he he certainly he's got that slashing mentality where he's hard to hard to bring down in space and uh that showed up again today. It showed up in practice really throughout camp so far. Um we'll continue to challenge him to find a a defined role there on special teams where he can help us out the most there and then you know pass protection, how do we continue to improve? When you're a little bit smaller as a running back, um that's always what I'm looking for is how well how stout are we holding up to a blitzing linebacker as well. So things that we're looking for as we as we continue through this thing. >> Couple more please. Keon Bishop hasn't been here long but he came away with a couple of he's done in college and take away from that. How do you kind of sort through the significance of that in the game with those guys? >> Well, no, I think it's it's a credit to him. Um, you know, he he doesn't say a whole lot. He's just learning and trying to absorb the system right now and uh, you know, I think DA has been pretty clear with how our pass defense it works together. It's the rush up front combined with the coverage in the back end and when you feel that front coming off the ball and affecting the quarterback to the degree that they did, move him off his spot, that's where you get some overthrows and things of that nature and Beanie's in great position and he took advantage of it twice, you know? Um, thought he had a great return afterwards as well. And so, it was it was awesome to see. We'll continue to evaluate him as as we get going. It's also um, where we got to get better as a team is we got to we got to score some touchdowns when we when we get those takeaways. So, there's a lot of good tape from today. I know what the score says and yet we we got a lot to learn from and grow from as well. >> So, just about a year ago you talked about being four or five guys you could trust to be in the offense where where they need to be. What what does that list look like now? I think last year it was like Rome, Ozy, DJ. What does that list look like now going into >> Yeah, I don't know if I could put a number on it, but uh, these guys these guys are they understand what the expectation is and um, I think they study their their tails off and they do I mean, they're professionals and you bring in some new guys, some young guys, like take Zayvian for example, and now you can just say, "Hey, just do what Rome does. Just do what Kalief does." Just, you know, like that's where this thing really takes off and Zayvian is on his stuff because he's just watching them and doing what what they do. And so, um, there's not a number on it, but it there's a lot of confidence right now with where we are, where we're heading, and what we're we can potentially become here as we keep going through this thing. I love the fact that we take all the bells and whistles off uh today and we're more static, not a whole lot of motions and all that, and these guys can just cut it loose and play fast. I thought their play speed showed up today. >> And uh three injured guys I want to check in on really quick. Montez, how soon do you expect to have >> Uh sooner sooner sooner sooner, like within this week. >> And uh Braxton? >> Uh same thing. >> Kyler? >> Uh unknown.

title: Bears postgame locker room | 2026 Preseason Week 1
text: It's not a few for you out there getting your kind of first start, first game action. How did that >> Oh, it was awesome. It wasn't enough. Not enough. >> How much did you end up playing out there? >> I'm not sure exactly, but they they told me I was done, so I was trying to get some more, but they they said no. >> How different was it, you know, getting kind of not that it was real regular season game, but still, you know, NFL game action against you another team? >> Mhm. Uh I mean, it was good. Like every everything matters. All the reps matter. Um so, definitely look at the film, see where I can improve there. But it it was good. Like I like being out there. It was fun. >> Where do you feel like you're at in terms of sort of getting everything down and being ready to start if it was week one of the regular season? >> Uh I think I am ready. Mentally, I think you can just the more reps you get, the better the better it is. So, I mean, the more experience you can get, just um >> [snorts] >> more reps, more times watching film, talking to other guys, so I feel ready, but the more I can get that, it just prepares me more. Mhm. Yeah, I mean, definitely definitely looking forward to that, but taking it just one week at a time, focus on the next opponent. >> Have you talked to Coach Sans? I don't know if we've talked to you since we found out, you know, his injury's going to take a Yeah, he's he's been back in the building, so I've been talking to him. He's been um just reaching out, making sure I'm all good. Like if I had any questions or I needed anything, and uh I've been checking up on him, but uh he's doing great so far. >> You had a couple of good good third down stuff early in the game. You had a stop on 36, I think, in coverage. How important is that, and how did you feel out there? >> I felt good. I felt felt good moving around. Felt healthy. Felt like I could everything was like slowing down for me. Um but obviously there's stuff I can still get better at. A few things I can want to improve. >> Explain how does that like the slow down happen? It seems that's that's pretty bad for it to slow down. You mean from the off-season program up until now? >> Yeah, like going through the practices and then getting out there just felt like felt like I had like everything was just like a step slower. >> Okay. >> I don't know how to explain it. Probably wasn't the best. >> [laughter] >> I'll accept that. You said that there are things that you want to get better at. What what specifically? >> Uh I mean just you can always keep working on your technique, man coverage. Um making sure your eyes are just playing like just all those things. >> What's that process like getting used to playing with Cam and Xavier and just kind of like Uh just communication off rip. So, just getting to know them, uh how they like to play, how they see things. Uh Cam and Xavier both coming from different um backgrounds, different schemes. So, they they have a lot of experience in in uh It's been great playing with them. >> Are you where you thought you'd be or not? >> I mean, it's hard to say that I'm where I thought I'd be seeing as I've started one game in in 3 years and I've been injured multiple times. Uh so, there's obviously that level of frustration. I'm not the player that I want to be yet, obviously. Um but, I'm working towards that. Everybody has a different path to the NFL. And as a competitor, obviously it's it's it's it is frustrating to not be out there, not to not be healthy, but, you know, I'm healthy now and I'm focused on staying on the field as as as long as I can. >> Yeah, given those frustrations, how do you feel you handled this opportunity to compete with them like that? >> Uh I think you know, I handled it with you know, as well as I could. Uh taking it day by day, uh focusing on myself, on what I need to do to get better. Um listening to what Coach O'Shaughnessy is saying in the film room, what he sees from me and trying to apply that on the field daily. >> How'd today go for you? >> I think like I said, it was up and down. Uh I think I was kind of getting my feet underneath me for a second. It's tough to get in a rhythm uh sitting in the second quarter and coming back to the 2-minute drill and and then the third quarter and stuff like that. So, so it's a good learning opportunity obviously just to you know what I need to do to stay ready in those moments if there is another occasion like that. Um but yeah, like I said it's uh it was up and down and um you know, I'll I'll only get better from it. Definitely. I mean, it's where I've played pretty much my whole career since high school. Uh I feel more comfortable at tackle, but you know, I'll play I'll play anywhere. >> The 2-minute drill, to be in there to see what that drive ended with at the at the end of the first half, what did you learn about that operation and what do you think needs to be cleaned up about it? >> Well, I think like I said most of it honestly for me but on a personal level was staying in the game and being you know, being out for the second quarter and then coming back in just for that 2-minute drill. Uh it takes a different level of execution and of and attention to detail, especially up front, you know, D-linemen are going to move a lot more. They're going to run them a lot more games. You're going to get their best move because they're they're trying to get the quarterback in that 2-minute and and kind of end the drive there. So, I think it's you know, it's a lot of things you know, detail, execution, but then also staying within the game and and kind of calming down in that moment. >> What is the most challenging at the nickel position that that you have found so far? >> Uh run fits. I would definitely say run fits, gap schemes, uh knowing where to fit, um knowing once you get inside of the 40 or you get inside of the 20 20 or 30, uh just knowing where your fit is in in in different calls. and then just knowing where your help is, uh knowing the spacing, knowing what what the timing is going to be. but I'll say those are the are are the challenging things. >> How did it feel for you out there today? Obviously, you made a big play blowing up the screen, but just overall what did it kind of feel like? >> Uh I mean, really just getting my feet wet uh playing in front of a crowd again uh in the NFL now. But uh at the end of the day, man, I just tell myself, man, you a rookie, bro. Just go out there and play. Uh you going to make mistakes. Just go out there and fly around and just be you. Play ball. >> And when it comes to like making mistakes or coming, how do you feel like you've been you know, adjusting to life in the NFL? >> Yeah, so that's the thing about me like I don't want to make no mistakes. But uh, now just talking to guys like Jaylen Johnson or Kobe Bryant or even like Josh Blackwell or and some some more of the other guys who've been here for a long time who've been playing in the league for a long time. Uh, they just tell you man, they're getting paid just like you are. Like they didn't get drafted or they didn't they're not on a team for no reason. So you're going to make mistakes, you're going to give up plays. Just make the next play your best play. >> They've been uh, they've been great. Had the opportunity to play for them in Detroit and uh, they've encouraged me a lot to just take it day by day and made it easy. >> Yeah, obviously you made some plays in camp, but what did it feel like to do it in in a game atmosphere today? >> Uh, it feels good anytime you can go out there and make plays in an NFL field. It's a very humbling league, so it feels good to make plays. >> do you think you've shown these guys with this game? >> Um, I think I've shown them speed and that they can trust me and consistency. >> How have you developed your connection with Tyson throughout camp and I'm saying to today? >> Um, yeah, it's been quick. I mean, it's still just football at the end of the day. Um, timing does play a factor, but Tyson's got a great arm and great head on his shoulders and has made it easy for me. I just do my best to get open and he does his part to get me the ball. >> Do you like this schedule you're on where you go spring football to fall football? >> Yeah, I mean, I'm just I'm all about opportunity. Whatever opportunity comes my way, uh, I just want to take full advantage of it. >> You mentioned it just sort of being delayed for you at this point. So how do you feel like you take advantage of this opportunity with no one in front of you? >> Um, I just keep taking it day by day and putting my best foot forward knowing what to do and making the play when the ball comes my way.

title: Gardner Minshew II Press Conference 8.15.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: The owner decided that the best way to describe how well you guys are playing as a group as QB's like a reverse show. Um, I'm curious like how do you kind of analyze the fact that all four of you are seem to be playing lights out. >> Yeah, no, it's quite a visual puts out there. But now it's been great, man. I think the emphasis that coach has put on just operating in the offense, the simplicity in it, it's made our jobs easy and each guy kind of has their own strengths and has been able to lead that group. It's been a lot of fun. >> Did you feel like you were in a rhythm? Like is was there a groove that you were in that like nothing was going to be able to shake that in the last game against the Raiders? >> I don't know, man. It felt good to be out there. It's always good to play ball, man. Sure. >> How do you kind of approach how you're looking at this? I mean, obviously you know, Jacoby's QB1. You said when you first came in, whatever is needed, you've learned that a long time ago. How do you Was that something you had to learn as your career went on? So many rookies come in and they're thinking, I'm trying to make my way in this league. Is there a time when you have to kind of like readjust your thought process? >> Um maybe a little bit. It's a bit of a perspective shift, but not in not in the way you think like I mean, what do we really have? Each day we have the opportunity to show up and get better. And like you can just do that over and over and that's it, you know. Um looking around and wondering who's around you or what's around you like doesn't serve you at all. Doesn't serve the team. Um, so really the best thing you can do is just show up and work and be a good dude to the people around you and you know, try to do that every day. >> You and Jacoby having each been in the league for quite a while. How do you help each other at this point in your careers? I mean, where do you help each other with what and all that stuff? >> Yeah, I think just kind of it's nice to be a sounding board, you know, have somebody else with the experience to kind of you know, talk through stuff, you know, ask you know, what did you see? Even just the example, you know, from each other how you know, we each have different experiences and are bringing those into this offense, you know, seeing how he sees it is like, "Oh, that's you know, that makes a lot of sense. That's nice." Um so, just being able to use each other's experience, watching each other's plays out there. Um I know I've learned a lot from him that way. >> You've played in a lot of offenses in the league. You had a lot of offenses in college as well. Your process of learning an offense, when do you feel like you have it down? Do you have it down yet? >> Uh yeah, no, I feel very comfortable out there. Um it's been great. I was fortunate to have a ton of reps through the spring, through camp so far. Um Coach LaFleur is a great teacher. Um and I think it's very user-friendly. So, all those things kind of uh help make it, you know, and help get us where we are now to where we're able to get out there and execute. >> Jaylen had said trust was a big factor in the back shoulder touchdown throw to him that you trust him on that play. Is is that a tough thing to develop on the fly, especially when you've got different guys entering, coming out of the lineup at this point in the season? >> Uh no, I mean, like anybody that we have out there, you know, you expect them to do the job. If you wait to see do it, like you're going to be late and you're not it's not going to work. Man, I think we got a a long list of guys that can go in there and get the job done. Uh and that's a great feeling as a quarterback. Like, you're not you're not really looking at each play for matchup-dependent. It's really just, hey, where does the coverage tell you to go with the ball and you can trust that they'll be in the right spot. >> That attitude you were mentioning before that you kind of take into it, is that Do you ever try and give that advice to younger quarterbacks or is it something that a guy just has to kind of come to on his own accord? >> Uh I don't know, a little bit of both. Like, if they ask, you know, but I'm not like a preacher or anything, you know. Uh I think the best thing you do for the young guys is just be a great example and be an encouraging to those guys. Uh and then for me, the best like when I was a young guy, it was Nick Foles. Just how encouraging and how much that helped. Um you know, when everything's crazy, um you know, just kind word here or there goes a long way. >> What have you kind of noticed from Carson as he continues to get his feet wet? >> No, man. Carson has a ton of confidence. He can throw the heck out of it. Um it's been awesome to see him uh really grow in the offense through fall camp. Had a great game the other day. Um he's opening up in the quarterback room, which is so fun, you know? Um but now I feel feel great about our group, and it's been a been a good feeling in the quarterback room. >> We've seen at practices you've been wearing the game jersey. Is that something you've done throughout your career or what kind of went into the decision? >> Yeah, kind of um I think it's you know it's a very different fitting jersey, you know? So only doing that on Sunday doesn't really make sense. Um you know, so just it's good to just practice that way all the time, really. >> With Carson, he had a lot of college experience. How do you see that kind of translating early on now? >> Yeah, um I don't know. I mean, he's played a lot of ball, you know? You know, ball's ball. It's you know, you get to the NFL, guys are a little bit faster. Um coaches think they're a little bit smarter, you know? So you're doing more stuff, but like, you know, it's the same game, and it's good to see him trust that and not um you know, think he has to do too much, but he can just be himself. >> I'm sure you've seen a lot of rookies in your career. Does he seem ahead of the curve, if you will, because of all that experience? >> Yeah, I guess, you know, he's old, you know? But uh no, he's he's he's doing great, seriously. >> When when Yeldon left the room, he said the fun guy's coming up, referring to you. What do you >> [laughter] >> What do you like about this group of offensive linemen? Obviously, the O-line is known for having some personalities. What do you What do you think of this group overall in that department? >> No, it's been great, man. I think they do a great job as a unit. They communicate really well. Um all of them take their job very seriously. We got some guys that have played a lot of ball. Um so I think their understanding and ability to communicate and execute um has been really good this camp. And our defense throws a ton of looks out Uh it's kind of, you know, uncharted territory each day with them. Uh, and it's been good to see our guys like kind of figure it out on the fly. I think that's been a big thing. >> Jordan, how different of an athlete are you now than you were as a rookie back in '19? >> Uh, yeah, now um, a good bit. Um, I don't know, just a little more mobile, can, you know, bend a little better. I think I throw a little more on the little better on the run. Got a little more zip on the ball. You know, just getting a little older. Um, yeah, try not to lean on that quite as much as I used to, but uh, yeah. >> You can games and quarterbacks are fine like 50 for 59, close to 500 yards. >> It's pretty good. >> You look at training camp practices and things leading up. Do you say that practices are maybe sometimes tougher than when you guys get out in the game you're so prepared that >> Uh, maybe, yeah, and it should be. Um, you know, we practice hard. Our defense is very challenging and looks that they throw at us. They mix it up a lot. Uh, I think also in the preseason games, you know, everybody tames down a little bit. It's a little more vanilla. you know, so based on what we've been getting in practice like it's, you know, generally simpler looks. Just and that's, you know, nothing on the teams we're playing. That is just the nature of the preseason. Um, but I think what we do in practice has prepared us very well for for games. >> Mike has said he prefers 11 on 11 over seven on seven. Has that How does that translate for you guys into on the field? Does that help you guys in what ways does that help you guys make that much a lot? >> Yeah, it's good. Um, I mean, I like seven on seven just for a fact to get reps, you know, just to get more reps, but obviously there's nothing, you know, nothing like the real thing and getting out there with the, uh, you know, the perspective of having the rush, the timing of that, the having to move and, you know, the lack of vision. Um, I think that's all, you know, obviously more real. I think there's benefits to both, but um, you know, as long as we're getting reps, you know, I think that's a big thing.

title: Hjalte Froholdt Press Conference 8.15.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Mike said he was kind of rushing out of the plane to make sure Chase had a spot up front after he got hurt. He said you had already taken care of it and went back to his seat and I'm just wondering like maybe it's obvious, but just you're making sure that he was okay given everything and trying to be a leader about that whole situation and like what was going through your head? >> Uh well, yeah. I mean, he was wrapped up and I think I had him in a brace or something. So, um I'm lucky enough to be able to have the privilege of sitting in the front. Some nice seats up there. So, try to help him out a little bit. >> How do you I mean, again, we go through this every year. We've talked about this with a lot of people, but for a rookie who's just trying to get started, what's kind of your advice to a guy like that in this situation? >> Um I mean, I was hurt myself my rookie year. Um blew my shoulder and had to sit out. So, >> [sighs] >> it always sucks. I mean, it sucks when everybody gets hurt. It's hard when it's one in your room, you know, it's a and especially young guy like that. I mean, Chase was coming along so well. I mean, he was opening up. You know, it's it takes a little while for young guys to start getting another personality coming out a little bit. So, you're like, all right, here we go. Come on. We're doing good. So, uh but you know, I'm not going to let him just be isolated. So, we'll bring him around. I'll keep getting on his ass, make him do some duties or something like that when he can when he's getting [laughter] I mean, when he gets back. Uh but yeah, no. Um it sucks, man. Um gutted about it. It's part of the game. It's the worst part of the game. Um but you know, needs some time for himself to kind of, you know, get through it and then just, you know, he has a long time like get back on track and take it slow, you know. I think uh sometimes you want to rush things back, but he has a whole year to come back and do as well as he needs to do it. So, worse he can do is force it and then have a setback. So, um main thing I think for some guys that are hurt, especially myself, was only good days. So, I think it's even though you might feel slow and bored, but only good days. You don't want a bad day. Um at least early on. Of course, he wants to push it. You need to push it at some point, but no bad days. >> You're pretty business like for you when the first team is out there on Thursday night. Just kind of take [clears throat] us through that touchdown drive and him what you guys wanted to accomplish today. >> Yeah, I mean, I I messed up on one of them. There's a little bit of procedural stuff there that we need to clean up that I mean, it's not up to our standards. So, that's some stuff that we need to be better at obviously, but uh I mean, yeah. Jacoby threw an absolute dart and um through all the traffic. Marv made a hell of a catch. So, it was really good. I was happy with the first drive. I think we ran the ball really pretty well and got some good stuff on tape and you know, it always feels a little bit different live and against another defense and we don't really do a whole a ton of scouting in preseason. Um, but so it's a little hard sometimes, but just some looks we want back and some things we want to do, but sometimes it's like, oh, we don't really want to run that play versus that look, but it's always good to do cuz then you can talk about it and now you're like, okay, but what if it happens again? Like, you never know. Defense can do whatever the hell they want to do. Uh, but I think it was good. It was good going out there. We had a nice long drive. Uh, guys played really well and hard. So, that was good, but just some of the procedural stuff we need to pick up, but then uh yeah, two guys went out there and made some some pretty good plays out there in the end. So, it was good. >> You know, Andrew Billings was saying the other day, now he's on the defense, so obviously it might be a little bit different, but he's like, because you can't really take down a running back and you definitely can't touch a quarterback, that even when the pads are on in practice, it's you're not he's like, you're not really going all the way like you would in a game. Is it the same for an offensive lineman or is it a little different cuz you can touch the other guys. >> Yeah, I mean, it's a little different. I think some of the feel cuz then you can kind of feel when the D-lineman either pulls up or not cuz I mean, we're trying to take care of each other. So, um obviously game is different. So, but I think uh >> that last bit is is more a personal thing, I think, than something that you really teach like yeah, I mean, you saw you saw what what what Andrew could do. Like when he went in a game and just crushed like, you know, and it's like, yeah, that that's what's in him. And then like, in practice, then he might hold up right here or do something like that, or I might reach the hell out of him or whatever it is, and then like we get good work both ways. So, I think that way it it's good. Um but I think in the end it's like it's up to the individual to be like Coach Farwell [clears throat] talks about it, there's about that 80/20. So, the first 80% it's like, get off the ball, get your feet, run your feet, and then that last 20% of the drive where you don't really know where the back is going, you don't really know where the quarterback is. Like, how do you finish that 20%? It's not really something you can really drill. It's not something you can really teach unless you go live, but that's just too much stuff that can happen with that. But yeah, I think that's that's that's why you do all the scouting to see if it's a guy that, you know, is willing to put in that last 20%. Push through the old lineman to get to the running back, or is he like, I'm good in my gap? Um so, but I think we have a lot of like I think we have a ton of both young guys and old guys. I think there's a lot of experience there that you know, guys play like you can feel it's like, okay, if he had a chance he would have run through there or whatever. So, like they I mean, I still like we've had a really good and tough camp so far, and you can see everybody getting better and better, and and you know, the toughness has showed up on shows up on Sunday, I think, or that was Thursday. But yeah. >> When you are game planning in preseason games, is it more like pick up style, or like what does it challenge you to do? What kind of skills that work on when you don't really know what's coming and kind of you prepare for? >> I mean, generally preseason the looks are generally fairly simple. I also think guys don't want to necessarily show everything you have. Uh but a lot of it's just get fits in a live situation, so uh they had a good little uh delayed TT on delayed interior game on like the first pass pro we had. Um so, it was delayed. I wasn't really ready for it, but he kind of picked me and I fell on the ground and it's like it's good to feel cuz that doesn't really happen in practice. Like if we're happening in practice, a guy wouldn't necessarily knock me on the ground cuz what if? Uh he would I could feel it and I was like, "Oh, okay. He would have knocked me on the ground there." But it's good to feel. So it's like, "Okay, late in the play, what do they look like? What do you feel?" Like some of these like what he's talking about like those the last 10 20% of a play or if a play is 6 seconds, what the last 2 seconds really are about. Like that's kind of what you get to feel I person I mean for me personally. So how does that final push on the rush? How's that final like rip across face to get in the gap on the run play? Uh the fall back uh linebacker play, but it's a little different just cuz everybody's scheme are a little bit different. So the backers play a little bit different. Something that you have to get used to. Um but I think it's going out there playing your playing your game, throwing out some plays that you want to get good at and then seeing how it fits and then coach off of it, but not really take too much to heart. So it's like, "Okay, we need to see you how you adjust in this situation. I'm not really too worried about the outcome, but as long as you're I see you like, "Okay, this is what I'm thinking and this is why I did it." I think that's what you're looking at especially young guys as well uh to go out and execute. >> What are you seeing out of guys like John and Hayden this camp? >> [cough and clears throat] >> Uh I mean a lot of good stuff. I mean John, he ever since he came first year and he and talk talk about another guy who got hurt his first year. Um just always playing so well, man. I mean it's kind of crazy to think he's in year four already. Um but I mean great player can play all three interior, knows the playbook in and out. It's not a drop when he goes in there. So uh and Hayden's taking a huge step from last year as well. Uh playing really fast, playing good with his hands, I think. He's still a bigger guy and he knows what his strengths are for that, but uh playing more loose and you know, can understand it, make those I think a lot of the time is especially for a lineman, when you get in the league, it's like first I need to adjust to the speed, then you need to understand the playbook and know where the hell I'm going. And then once you've kind of figured that out, then you can start doing a little micro adjustments and I think that's where some of those guys are at now where it's like, "Oh, instead of my hand here, I want it here." And that's a simple adjustment, but it's fun to get to that point. Like it took me a while to get to that point in my career where it was like, "Okay, now it's actually fun to learn about this again cuz I have the wherewithal and I'm I'm comfortable enough with everything else that I can take that step in the small adjustments." And I think those two are are are there. >> And doing a great job. >> Where is Where is Isaiah's confidence level compared to last year and compared to his rookie like >> I mean, I've always known Zay got it in him. So, he's been balling out, playing really well. I think um it's always hard. You kind of got to find your play style and what you are. I mean, all across the board, all five of us we we play a little bit different as long as put as long as we're on the same page, understand where we're all going to be at. Um but I think he's kind of found his style and what he what he's doing and he you know, he's he's marrying it and executing it and doing a a hell of a job about it. So, he's been balling out this camp and and I'm just stoked to see what he can do. >> Getting into the fourth week of camp, what's [clears throat] been the biggest difference having Jacoby back? >> I mean, it's just good to have him and you know, making sure like the whole huddle and the procedure and everything like that. It's just getting smoother and smoother and smoother and you know, he's a leader on this team. We all knew it. So, um it's great to have him back and he's been he's been playing really well and um yeah, it's good to have him in the huddle. >> How would you describe his leadership style? >> A little mix of new and old school, I guess. He's still got a little bit of old in him. He don't mind He don't mind getting on your ass a little bit. >> [laughter] >> But he is good. Nah, I like Jacoby a lot. I mean, that whole quarterback room in general, I mean, they've been balling out. It's kind of a it's almost like it's like a reverse show in a way that's like, "Damn, everyone's playing so good." It's kind of hard to figure out what we're going to do. So, they're I mean, yeah. I mean, all of them are just balling out and it's really good to see. So, um it's a good room, man. And I think they're having a lot of fun, and it's good to see. >> Speaking of leadership, last year you wore the C of the first for the first time. In what ways has your leadership maybe evolved or developed since, you know, you earned that honor last year to to now? >> Yeah, I mean, I think First, I was it was one of the coolest things in my career being being voted captain. Uh And I think once it happens, all of a sudden you get all these Okay, now let's get a little deeper. Now you get a little all these like internal conversations like, "Ooh, am I supposed to do this? What about this? Am I supposed to speak up? Am I Am I supposed to do X, Y, and Z?" And I think I kind of came to a point where I was like, "They voted for me because of me, so I'm going to keep doing what I'm doing, and if I feel like there's something that need to be said, then I'll say it, but I'm going to continue to do what I've been doing." Um if you because try to become something you're not, people see through that immediately. Um so, I'm not a hoorah guy. I'm really not. Uh more of a one-on-one kind of guy. Like, "Hey, how are you doing, dude? You good?" >> But but I think, you know, if if I start doing stuff I mean, obviously you need to step out of your comfort zone. I think that's a big important part, too. Like, I was I was privileged enough to be vote I had that C on my chest, and there were some moments where I needed to step up and and, you know, be that guy. Uh and also there's some certain parts of my game or off the field on and off the field where I'm like, "Okay, how can I improve?" Um so, there's definitely some things, but overall our king theme is just be yourself, and I think that's what I've tried to do. So, uh I'm not really trying to change a whole lot. Um Uh definitely it's an interesting perspective to have to now be like, "Oh, okay, now like you see me in that role." Um but uh yeah, personally, right or wrong or different, that's just kind of how I dealt with it. Um and that felt better doing it that way than trying to be something I'm not. >> Mhm.

title: HC Mike LaFLeur Press Conference 8.15.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Uh obviously you were talking about following up with Chase. We saw some reports. Can you what can you tell us about Chase? >> Yeah. No. Um confirmed with the MCL. So uh he'll uh he'll be out. Um you know for uh a good good amount of time if not the uh the whole year. So um yeah it sucks for him. Always think about the player first. It sucks for the Cardinals obviously when you lose a player that uh you know is a good player but but more importantly you just you hate it for the player. So You think you're going to put him on IR? Is that >> Yeah. Yeah. Yep. Yep. >> How's he kind of handling everything? >> He like a stud like just like how he plays. That's the person he is. So, he'll attack this thing and and uh like I said to him yesterday when I called him just, you know, somehow someway you're going to be better from this, you know, and because I I just think he's made the right stuff to to figure it out. >> Has he had surgery or is he when will it be if he has? >> Uh I I don't have this specific date. He has not had surgery now. >> When you say you're going to put him on IR, do you mean now or do you mean I >> I don't know the specifics in terms of exactly when when all that stuff has to happen. That's, you know, more of a Monty type deal. It's just all I know is obviously he's not going to be out there for practice today and that's what I'm focused on in terms of like some of that stuff with the roster and all that. I just Monty knows the timing of of those kind of things and I don't even ask the questions. >> When you start to look at that position, Isaiah Adams obviously is the starter there. What do you look at behind that as far as depth? Is is that something where John Gaines can kind of shift over? you look at other guys there. >> Yeah, I mean you got Hayden, you got uh that I think have played, you know, pretty good ball. Um whether it be in practice or or these games, you know, they're they're more than capable of stepping in. Um so we'll kind of mix and match some of those things in terms of, you know, um worst case scenarios. Uh so, you know, inevitably someone's going to miss some time. It's football and uh so we'll we'll start mixing and matching some of that this week. I have a lot of trust in in Fry, uh, you know, in terms of, you know, how he wants to disperse those reps and we'll kind of go from there. >> How did Isaiah look to you in his 11 snaps on whatever? >> Uh, solid like he's looked to me ever since OTAAS. I think every day he's just uh gotten a little bit better and um and that's shown since the pads have got on when we were in in um Glendale. And uh and I think you know in those kind of that 11 snaps like you said, I thought he played solid football. I think he's just been solid and steady. I don't think what what's really uh stood out to me with him is he looks like he plays at his pace which is a good thing. Uh he doesn't look rushed and um I think he's looks solid and sturdy and he needs to continue to improve. >> The NFL made the rule earlier the week or at least they announced that the head coach now has the ability to designate someone else to throw the challenge flag. Is that something you're going to keep that responsibility or do you plan to designate? >> It's either me or Mark Dalton. So it >> but in all seriousness, no I it'll 100% be me. What what I don't and I I kind of understood the ruling. Actually Mark's the one that told me in terms of the ruling just um us coaches are are are crazy and sometimes you you do it when you're not thinking straight. And so that I guess is the point of just having someone a little bit more level-headed. Uh what what I don't want to do is say well it was his fault that we did it. Like if if there's a red challenge flag, that's that's 100 and and it was wrong. That's on me and I don't want to blame anyone else. >> How was uh Jeremiah's ankle? >> Uh he came in yesterday a little bit more sore than um he you know he left. He was in great spirits even yesterday. I think you guys met with him or something like that. But uh we we'll keep him out this week um you know as uh we just let it heal. So a little bit more sore than we were anticipating. >> Any long-term concern? uh you know again this week and then we'll kind of go from there and reevaluate it. >> Do you think there's any chance that his availability for week one would be >> honestly it all I'm focusing is on August 15th Saturday here we are in our tempy block um you know and then we'll kind of reevaluate it going into next week >> but he will be he will be out this week though. >> We also noticed some discomfort from Nolan after the sack. Um any how is the status? >> Yeah, he's he's good. >> Yep. Elijah Higgins didn't imply. What is he dealing with? >> Uh he he's got a he had a concussion. Um so he'll uh he's he's been through the protocol and all that. Um and uh you know we should see him back shortly. >> Mike, [snorts] with a with a guy like Gardner, I mean obviously you have Brassette and you have a role for him. You you want to bring along Carson. How does a guy like Gardner kind of maneuver through his role with so many different moving parts here? >> Gardner's a pro, you know. Um, obviously he had extended uh time with the ones uh through OTAAS and I thought he just got better and better. I think he I mean he's played a lot of football. He's played a lot of good football in this league. He's seen a lot of different systems. Um he can operate the huddle as well as anyone I've really ever been around. Uh the game makes sense to him. He thinks about the game. Um he thinks about our concepts and and without overdoing it, thinking of stuff that could play off each other. So um he's just a pros pro. um you know, whether it be snap one of week one or you know, snap 50 of of week 17, like he's just always going to be ready. Um so, you know, it's um it's good that we have him. >> Coach, last year in LA, you guys utilize like every tight end [clears throat] on the roster imaginable, especially in the game in London, but how does that carry over now? What do you like about your group after McBride, and it's kind of been the rage this offseason to add a bunch of tight ends on rosters? >> Yeah. No, I thought you saw that uh particularly on day two of the draft. Uh I mean there was between the second and third rounds, I can't remember, you know, a draft class like that and you almost kind of knew that was going to happen. Like it's most teams, you know, I mean statistically we were the number one offense in in LA last year and so most people are going to study the top kind of teams and and they're doing the same thing on defense. Special teams coordinators are are studying the same. So naturally, uh, whether they played, you know, a team played the Rams or not, they were going to, you know, put some study into it and, oh wow, there's a lot of tight ends that they're utilizing. So kind of almost foresaw that happening. Um, you know, and we'll do what we think's best. Um, again, we're not going to be the Rams, we're not going to be the Niners, we're not going to be the Packers, we're going to be the Arizona Cardinals, and we're going to do what we think is best with with the guys that we got and um, you know, kind of take it from there. So I'm not going to go too much further in terms of schematics with that and the personnel. U, but um, yeah. >> Are you pleased with that what they've done so far? >> I am. Yeah. No, I'm I'm pleased with a lot of these groups, but we got a long way to go. >> What do you want out of your backup quarterback? Because I know what are like the [clears throat] prerequisites that you that you have in mind for what you want them to to be like to do to >> want to be the best backup quarterback of all time, you know? But no, I mean, it's what is a backup quarterback? Well, when you're you're one snap away at any given time and so you got to be ready to go and you're not going to always get the obviously the necessary reps.
