title: Todd Monken Postgame Press Conference at Bears: August 15th, 2026
text: All right. Um, man, that was a lot of fun. That that was getting out there with our guys, watching them play all the fruits of their labor uh from the spring and then and then camp, watching our guys compete. Obviously, not the result you want. I mean, I don't care. I mean, you're playing to win at the end of the day. We didn't do that. We didn't finish the game. didn't play well in the second half. Uh really on either side of the ball, but I do believe that the season is a marathon. That marathon starts in Jacksonville. We're just still in training. Today was basically we're we went out there today and we are 13 miles into our training and we'll get closer next week and we'll get closer the week after. There's a lot to clean up. There is coaching and and playing. Uh [snorts] so so again frustrating at certain levels, but um certainly you can't turn the ball over three times. Uh you certainly can't do that. Uh but uh and there were there were some things operationally that I know we can clean up, but I was uh I thought at moments we threw the ball well and that's what we needed to see. Would we be able to throw? We're going to be able to run the football. Um so there were certain things that we wanted to at least keep it simple today with, but I wanted to see how we'd be being able to throw it and I thought our quarterbacks uh played well in that regard. How did you think uh Deshawn Watson did in his half? >> Oh, it was awesome. I mean, it was so cool to watch him play. I mean, I get all of the the frustration by fans himself, but for him to come back and work like he did is a unbelievable credit to him. And then to go out there, he was having fun today and that is so cool. And I thought he really functioned at a high level. Certainly we don't want to be taking timeouts. We sure as heck can't take delay of games. Okay. But it was fun watching him play and watching us put the next step forward and see where we're at. >> Todd, was the plan so it seemed like he started out with some nice easy throws. Was the plan to sort of let him get out there and kind of get into a rhythm, not put, you know, maybe too much on on his plate early on with the with with the game plan. >> Sure. And and we had some other things called and they got us out of it. I mean, again, we were trying to stay as simple as we can, but yet give the quarterbacks opportunities to to play and to function. And um you know, we didn't game plan for Chicago. Um, we certainly wanted to run the things that our quarterbacks felt comfortable with and where we were at. And we're certainly going to build off that moving forward, but it was it was fun watching him again operate, give him some completions, and uh, you know, get his feet wet a little bit. >> Thought he had his hand and forearm checked a little bit after that one hit on the two minute drive. >> Yeah, he's fine. He's fine. Yep. >> Go ahead. >> What' you see from Casey on his be able to see him get that that opportunity to find the end zone in his first NFL? >> Well, we we were trying to do a number of things offensively. First and foremost, we were trying to get some of our skilled guys touches. So, and you can see the explosiveness whether it was the punt return or the fly sweep that we got it to. So, I'm happy for him. He's worked awfully hard and he got a few opportunities and made the most of it. >> You got Spencer a lot of run there at left tack. Was the plan always to keep him in as long as Deshawn was was in at? >> Yes, the the the plan was to let him to continue to play, get some of the other starters off out and allow him to continue to play through pretty much the first half. >> Todd, what's the next step in the quarterback competition now? >> Well, when we practice against Buffalo, we will give both of the quarterbacks opportunities with the ones against the Bills. Shador will start against uh the Bills. Deshawn will play in the third quarter and Dylan play in the fourth. >> So it just it just flipped. >> Todd on should the the interception should go through was that just an overthrow or was there >> I'll have to see it. I'll have to see if there was a little push that got in his face. Looked like we had a you know clear out with a dagger concept and uh looked like he was open. Looked like the ball sailed a little bit on him. Um a little bit like what happened with Dylan. I really, again, the positive thing is they were both in the right place. I believe that. Again, I'll have to see the film, but I believe they were in the right spot. Both interceptions. Um, we had Gage on the one from Dilly. Just let it sail. Maybe the ball got a little bit wet. It was humid out there, but I like that part of it that we're in the right spot. >> Where would you say the the quarterback competition stands right now coming out of this game? Did these guys go into that joint practice against the Bills still kind of pretty even? And can anybody still win this thing by maybe like after the Bills game? >> I'm not ready to say it yet. I mean, the plan was always to uh get through the Bills game, switch up who was going to start, who's going to play in the the second uh the second half, and then we'll go from there. Every day is important. Monday is going to be important, right? Uh being in the meeting rooms are going to be important. listening to uh to the players talk about what they saw, right? That's part of it, too. What they saw, how they feel. We'll go to back to work Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, have a great practice against Buffalo. Uh then we'll walk through on Friday, and then we'll go compete our rear ends off against the Bills and see where we're at, and then we'll re-evaluate. Then, we'll certainly watch it tomorrow and have an idea of how we thought our guys played. I mean, that that's a part of it. That that is a part of we're always in the evaluation process, and we're going to do the same thing as a coaching staff. I mean, there's certainly things we're going to look back at and say, "How [snorts] do we coach that better? How do we scheme it better?" Uh, moving forward, who do we want to be moving forward? >> How concerned are you about the depth at cornerback? Because another two guys got hurt today. That's just been a position where much like defensive tackle, it's just, you know, it's really starting to eat into that uh that depth a little bit. >> Well, everybody at this point in the year has has injuries. um some longer than others, some nagging injuries that you're going to work through. So, that's just what that just happens to be the position group now, right? Uh so, again, we've got good depth there. We'll just next man up and go out there and compete. >> Did Deshawn show you anything that you really needed to see this game? And do you think he will play at all against the Bills? >> Oh, yeah. He's going to play against Bills and play the third quarter. What I wanted to see was how comfortable he was leading up to the game. Um, how comfortable he was in the huddle. Certainly, there were things from a operational standpoint we can do better, but I wanted to see if he was enjoying himself. Was this still fun for him to play through the ups and the downs? Sure, he's not happy about certain throws that he could have made. a couple of them that would have extended drills. Um, sure he's thrilled about a quarterback sneak that we threw on him there to get a first down, but it was fun watching him play. It was uh it was fun. >> So, he answered those questions positively for you. >> In my mind, he did. >> Before you got here, he never sneaked much. Put in a tight end to sneak. So, have you guys talked about him sneaking? >> He said he can sneak. He said, "I'm a powerful dude, man. Just give me the ball. I'll get you inches." I said, "Great." I said, "Let's roll." >> Had a couple of ro backup defensive ends that had those two sacks. So, what how beneficial is it to see those guys be able to make plays um especially to have the depth um on the defensive line? >> Again, I love watching our guys play. I mean, all they do is they show up and say, "Spot the ball." I know I say that all the time, but it is so fun to watch those guys play. We just got worn down, you know. We We just got worn down. We after the first drive, I think that Shidor got in there and and we got stopped on fourth down. We just never got any traction till the last drive. And so we never and we turned the ball over and our guys just got tired over there. And uh that's that's not a good recipe for success is turning the ball over, they score, turn it over, uh they score. just we just we just couldn't stack any plays together to to help ourselves out. >> Couple more here. >> What about Deshawn overcoming some adversity on some of those those drives including being in first and 25 and uh you know just some of the other stuff that happened that he had to kind of get you out of jams. >> Yeah, it's all part of it. We were trying to get him a two-minute at the end and I would have never called that timeout if that was a regular game. We wouldn't have done that. But we're trying to get a two-minute right. It didn't turn out great, but I wouldn't have done that in regular. I would have let them decide whether they were going to let the clock run down, but we were trying to get the ball back. If we get a stop there, we get another opportunity uh to go two-minute there. Um because I wanted to see Deshawn go out there and play and get a two-minute uh which we did. I mean, we did right before that, but I wanted to get another opportunity for him to go out there and play because the number one evaluation we have is the quarterback position. So, why not try and get more plays? and that obviously it gave him a field goal at halftime and again if that was a regular game we would not have done that. >> Todd um you mentioned that what the plan is for the quarterbacks uh for Buffalo is the plan to is going to pretty much be the same for the offensive line in front of them or are you hoping to maybe you know >> switch things up? >> We'll see because we practice with them Thursday. So we have to talk about the reps we're going to have Thursday because the reps and I I talk with Joe Brady tomorrow. So, we're going to talk about how the practice goes. But, if it's really um heavy in terms of our ones and our upper level twos, then I could see a world where a number of those guys don't play in the game because of the work they got on Thursday. We would certainly not want to uh work them at a high level on Thursday and then expect them to turn around, especially against a team like Buffalo and and their players, and then play on Saturday. >> The reason to split the reps Thursday just keep it fair as possible >> as best as we can. The hardest part is you're not going to have similar blocks, right? You could have a rundown period and get back on track. Third downs two minute. You you're not going to have two different blocks or two similar blocks where the quarterbacks get the equal. It's just what you have to do. It's the closest you get. We want to see them compete as much as we can. And both of them had a turnover. One was a fumble. But I was really pleased with our quarterback play. It's not going to feel like that. Turn it over three times. That's never going to be ideal. But to me, it felt like we were we are going to be able to throw the football, be effective in that. Certainly do a better job coaching uh in the run game and protections and our play actions and everything that we do, we're going to get better at. But I was pleased with our quarterback play. I mean, for Shadur not to play the first half and to come right out and we open it up with a throw uh hits Gage, I think if I have it right and then we get a big third down and they go zero and we block it up and he hits, you know, our slot on a crossing route. Obviously, we didn't finish. Got to call it better. Got to coach better. Got to play better. But those are the things you're looking for. I mean, did anybody not see it and say, "Wow, I think I think we might be okay there. I think I think our quarterbacks are pretty good. We just got to do a better job coaching them and playing around them. >> Confidence um that in the event that Deshawn wins the job uh that he would be able to go out there and and function as a good quality starting NFL >> 100%. No, I don't I mean we're >> it's a preseason game. It's the closest thing we have, right? Right. But I am It beats the alternative, right? What's the alternative? They didn't play good. We didn't complete passes, right? We didn't look like we could halfway function as an offense. That we didn't have enough skill. Not true. We do. That we don't have tailbacks. Now we do. Uh we certainly didn't run it very well. Guys, you're not going to score a lot if you can't run the football. I mean, you can't control the game. I mean, we kept ourselves in long yardage situations, and that's going to be very difficult. I give the quarterbacks a lot of credit. for what we put them through in terms of the down and distances we had. Um, and certainly, like I said, I mean, there's a no one's going to make more mistakes than I do in a game. Nobody. There's not one player in terms of wanting calls back other than the red flag. My first red flag. I'm one for one. Make sure you, you know, holy cow. I know you guys when I don't get it right, you're gonna say that So, at least get I'm one for one on the damn challenge. All right. So, I I I'm fired up. I I really I think our team is only going to continue to get better and we're going to continue to develop our young players and continue to progress. But I was hoping our quarterbacks would play like that and function like that and I didn't see from our sideline. I saw our guys competing. I'm fired up. I'm fired up to see where we're at coming this week. >> Thanks, coach. Thank you everybody.

title: Deshaun Watson Postgame Press Conference at Bears: August 15th, 2026
text: That was a long time coming. How did it feel? >> No, most definitely. Uh felt good, felt excited just to be back on the field. Um you know, go through pregame, get warmed up, take the field for the first time in I don't even know how long it has been, but uh definitely a a good moment for myself. >> Seemed like they uh coach sort of eased you into this, but gave you some nice easy throws to kind of get get into a rhythm early. How important was that just to find that rhythm, you know, early on and and not struggle to get get there? >> Uh it's always good. I think for any quarterback, not not just myself, but anybody that's, you know, starting off the season or even starting a game, you know, the biggest key for a quarterback and receiver is just getting completions, seeing the ball get to the receiver's hands and they catching it and and getting positive yards and moving down the field, so uh >> Coach said that there were a number of things that he wanted to see from you that he did see today, uh including the fact that you look like you were having fun and enjoying being back out there. Uh is that what it felt like to you, kind of? >> Most definitely. I have fun with the guys, enjoying myself, smiling, um you know, getting hit a little bit, uh going through certain situations, um talking with coach on the headset, so everything was good um to be back out there and, you know, I was definitely having fun. >> How would you How would you assess How would you assess your performance and then like what what what encourages you and what do you feel like you want to work on some more in practice coming up? >> Uh there's always things to work on. Just continue to work at the operation. Just continue to get in and out the huddle. Um you know, just getting back in the groove of just seeing the operation, play clock, uh down and distances, you know, where certain situations, getting down to my check downs. Uh but, you know, just really just, you know, trying to stay positive, getting completions, moving the ball, and not taking any negative plays. That's the key. Um so there's a lot more to improve and we have more time in the next couple of weeks to do that. >> End of the game, were you able to keep up after being >> Yeah. Yeah, it was good. It was good to be able to to feel that, you know, things that you know, of course it was moving fast, but also being able to recognize different coverages and seeing the blitzes and and things like that was uh it was good to be able to see. >> How did your hand come out of it? I saw you shaking your hand a little bit and then you got it checked. I think your hand and your forearm a little bit. >> Yeah, it was just my forearm. I got hit in my elbow. Um I think it was I guess it was my funny bone, but just a little numbness, but it went away um as the game kind of continued to go on, but at that moment it was just just a little funny bone thing. >> Coming kind of off of that, just you mentioned getting hit and you know, it's been a while since you you've really, you know, gained hits and that sort of thing, but how did you feel like, you know, you you kind of went through that and you know, processed all that today? >> Yeah, it was good. You know, I didn't get as get hit as hard and that's the key is just being able to stay healthy and not try to take any unnecessary hits or uh blows that that that's going to, you know, add any extra, you know, distractions to your body, so it was good to be able to feel the the hits and get tackled a little bit and just, you know, again, play football and you know, throw the ball around and and be out there just calling plays. >> Looked like a pretty good start for Concepcion. What did you think of what you saw from him? >> Yeah, he's he's a very talented player. Um he is going to make a lot of plays for this team and he's going to continue to just get better as the more time he plays and get those reps and you know, uh get out there and once, you know, coaching scheme of plays to get him the ball, uh he can be very dangerous. >> Coach said that um that he 100% believes after seeing you out there today, uh believes that if you win the starting job that you can go out there and be quality starting NFL quarterback. Um how do you feel not only about him saying that, but how do you feel about that for yourself? >> Yeah, yeah. I mean, that's always been my mentality, so I don't think that's anything that I doubt in myself. That's the reason why I work hard these last 2 years, you know, to get back to that. You know, you know, I had some some challenges with some injuries and suspension and, you know, now being able to, you know, get a full off-season and continue to work my way back up, you know, it takes time. But, at the same time, I don't doubt myself in any way that I can't play at a high level. >> There's all been a lot of talk about pre-snap and processing and all that. How did you feel like operationally that went for you today? >> Uh it was good, you know, a couple things I had one delay of game. You know, we had a couple motions and it got down to one. Um and, you know, being pre-season, I think coach mentioned, you know, regular season, you know, we want to keep the time outs, maybe take a time out, but you know, that was those are the things that you got to be able to get the guys in and out the huddle. I know we switching personnels and have different motions, but as a quarterback, you kind of you have to manage that. And, um you know, that's one thing that that pops in the top of my head, but as far as operating, seeing the defense, seeing where the ball needs to go, um it was pretty solid today. >> Coach also mentioned that that he will split the first team reps against the Bills and that you will play in the third quarter after Schurmur starts the Bills game. So, how do you feel about the fact that the competition is continuing and that you're going to have more opportunities and it's kind of a big week? >> Yeah, just again, take advantage of those opportunities. Whenever the that my number is called and, you know, I'm the guy out there leading the group, you know, you got to continue to just find ways to get better, find success, and be positive with it. So, um yeah, we just had to take it one day at a time. >> You had Spencer out there with you the whole time. What did you see out of the rookie, you know, getting his first his first crack at it? >> Yeah, he was good. I think, uh you know, he was, you know, making sure that left side was, you know, very very, uh comfortable. And, uh I think that, you know, with him going against Verse each and every day prepared him for these moments. So, uh Spencer's just definitely going to be a big factor for this team. Um you know, I think that's why we drafted him high is to be able to come in and and compete and and be that guy for us. >> You got the sneak. How How did that feel to, you know, to convert that? And is that something that you don't mind doing whatsoever if you're called upon to do it regularly? >> Yeah, I don't mind. Whatever is going to help the team, you know, continue to move drives and and have that success. Um, not something I want to live in, but uh, definitely, you know, whenever it's called, you know, I want to make sure that I'm I'm ready for it and and keep the chains moving. >> Once again, can you sort of when you look out there and you see, you know, K.C. and Denzel and Isaiah and Jerry and everybody, Harold, um, can you see how uh, if you're playing at your peak efficiency that this could be an explosive offense? >> Yeah, definitely can. I mean, all those guys are very explosive with the ball in their hands. Um, seen it Seen it today with K.C., Denzel, you've seen flashes, obviously last year with Harold, and then Jerry all all obviously have shown that over his years. So, you know, all those guys being young and being in fresh and, you know, having those opportunities to get the ball in their hands can be very very explosive. So, you know, we're definitely excited for that and continue to put those reps in and get that trust and and that rhythm back. >> Do you feel like you've Do you feel like you've shown enough uh, to this point to be the starter? >> Um, you know, again, it it goes back to what, you know, Todd and and the organization and the coaching staff want. So, again, every every opportunity that I get, I want to continue to prove. I want to continue to just keep taking, you know, one step forward. Um, and every day is going to be a challenge, but, you know, that's the that's the whole thing about this NFL. It's a business and every day is a challenge and you got to continue to prove yourself. >> And one more if nobody else has taken it. And that is, uh, you moved around a little bit. Um, how did you feel on your twice surgically repaired leg? >> Felt good. Felt healthy. Felt no worries about it. Wasn't thinking about it. So, uh, it was good to be able to move around, run around, and and be in live action, trying to, you know, other guys trying to, you know, hit me and be confident with it, so. Um, the work has definitely been put in. Thank you.

title: Shedeur Sanders Postgame Press Conference at Bears | August 15th, 2026
text: What was it like for you just to be back out there after the off-season putting some of the work you've done? >> Yeah. Yeah, it was fun. Being out there was fun for sure. Um being able to to to to see the game was was truly it was truly amazing from like just the preparation everything I was so excited. >> How did it feel to start off with two big passes to Gage and and Saluk and just to kind of get rolling right away? >> I mean I don't really get excited. I don't get excited about the big plays and that stuff no more because it's like it's it's it's it's playing chess. It's like if you do this we're going to do that. You know, so it's just the right move in the right time was the right play call in the right time and um I was super excited. I was super excited about about about the play call and and everything that we executed it and all of our players was thinking the same thing at the same time. >> How did you think things went just from operational standpoint the huddle talking with coach Mullen and things like that? >> Uh I was early on I would say I would say um the operation wise it it was definitely a little faster in the game. So we definitely had a good communication uh in the huddle talking about everything and um just being able to step out the huddle, you know, when the play call is getting called so there's no miscommunication like between the line and what they're hearing what I'm saying anything. So that was exciting to be able to get that and now the coaches been emphasizing that. Um now it's kind of like it wasn't as loud so it's so so so it's we're able to understand it a little bit more of what they're saying and why they're saying certain things. >> Were you happy to be able to kind of get your feet wet a little bit before you go into your start next week against the Bills? >> Oh no, my feet get wet every day at practice. It just felt like another day at practice, honestly, um to me, but um even this week being on the road, communicating with the quarterback room, and just talking ball and everything, um I was able to unlock another point of view and be able to see things a little differently, so that's what I was excited about, and uh being able to get those different point of views from everybody in the quarterback room that has experience, it was uh it was great. >> What did you see on the interception? >> What I see? The right read, just a little just slip, you know. It was the right read, it just slipped, so that that's that's what makes me that's what makes me be mad a little bit because of it. But, you know, I I I don't any decision I make I'm I know it's the right decision. I just didn't execute the decision, but the right decision was made. So, every day I look in and I see about decision-making, like, how's my decisions I'm making, and uh that's how I grade myself off of, you know. Obviously, turning the ball over and all that stuff is is is not great, you know, and it won't survive a long time in the league doing that, but as long as my eyes and my feet and everything was in the right place, being able to execute and and just may happen. So, I look at the positive of things, you know. I'm alive, I'm breathing, I'm able to come up here and talk to y'all, so you know, I can't be that down. >> Tough Tough said the same thing. He said he thought you and Dylan on the interception both had the right read, just for some reason like the execution was a little off. It sounds like that's Is that pretty encouraging for you with this like like you probably have faith you're going to be able to execute most of the time, but it's about the decision-making probably? >> No, we definitely want to execute, so we don't want to make that a habit, but, you know, it may happen. yeah. Overall, we both had we both felt the same thing. The ball was a little sandy. So So, that was That was That was uh just a moment just to laugh at, you know, between us, honestly. Um because it was the right decision. I talked to him when he got to the sideline. I I said, "Hey, what happened, big?" Uh my bad. I said, "Hey, what happened?" He like, "Bro, the ball sandy." I said, "Bro, I know the ball sandy." So, it was just It was just a good moment to just talk about it. And and and laugh about af- after it's over, but the decision-making and um being able to execute what was out there was was the best thing. >> So, what comes to When it comes to post-snap, like your footwork processing and even, you know, making sure you get through your reads properly, were you happy with, you know, how you performed when, you know, with the live bullets flying at you? >> Yeah, I feel like bullets always flying in practice. I always feel like that, so it's the the the the difference is the attitude, how we go about practice every day. That's what makes the game more like real. And even having some experience in in the reps and the experience of last year uh helps me in the film study. Being able to look at the film and watch everything to to make the mind go a little faster. It's It's It's like you could think something, but then after you think something, you got to do it. So, it's just about how much do you know it to be able to recognize it as things going on. So, I think I had great uh post-snap visibility and being able to see what was going on. and, you know, it was a great game plan that our coaches had. You know, did we Were we able to put up the points and do what we were supposed to do? That matters in this league. Uh wins and losses, nah. We ain't We wasn't able to accomplish about that. We wasn't able to accomplish that today, but overall, I like the I like the process that we're going in now. I like it. I'm really excited about that. >> Zach, let me ask you a question. What was your best What was your best throw today? >> Check down to the running back in the red zone. That was the best throw. To me. Cuz I mean, I expect they go cover zero. title: Browns @ Bears Postgame Recap | Cleveland Browns
text: Nathan Zegura here at Soldier Field with your game recap presented by Vivid Seats. The Browns lose the preseason opener 34 to 10 to the Chicago Bears. Now, the Bears did not play their starters on offense. They did play their starters on defense. Deshaun Watson, of course, getting the start for the Browns at quarterback and was efficient in the pass game. 11 of 15 for 126 yards. He did not throw a touchdown, but he led the Browns on two scoring drives. A 50-yard field goal from Andre Smith and then a 14-yard touchdown run for K C Conceicao. And Conceicao looked as advertised. The Paul Hornung Award winner as the most versatile player in college football showed all three phases of his game. He had a punt return for 31 yards early in this one. He also had the run, the 14-yard touchdown run on a jet sweep, and he caught three passes for 27 yards. So, four touches, 41 yards, and a touchdown, and the punt return, he looked good. Denzel Boston looked good. And going back to Deshaun Watson, did not push the ball down the field. The biggest pass play of the day was a screen to Dylan Sampson for 43 yards. Got a great block from Luke Wypler, but he was efficient and calm in the pocket. And really, when the starting offensive line was out there, he looked even better. As the second team offensive line came in, there was a little bit more pressure, and the Browns offense stalled. But, they were up 10-nothing when their players of consequence really left the field. Ultimately, the Bears would go on and score 34. We've talked about depth issues for the Cleveland Browns at the cornerback position, at the linebacker position, and really the lack of experience in that depth. Well, that showed today. Case Keenum, the 15-year veteran for the Bears in the second half, really picked the Browns apart. But, overall, I think an encouraging day with Deshaun Watson. Dorian Sanders played in the third quarter and made some great throws. There's one where they brought an all-out blitz. He kind of stepped back, found Luke Floria for a huge gain. Unfortunately, that would drive would stall. They were unable to convert on a fourth down deep in Chicago territory. He would throw an interception as well. Made the right read. The ball just came out of his hands a little bit high, and it was intercepted. Dylan Gabriel came in as the final quarterback, threw an interception similar to Shedeur's where the The just got away from him, over threw the receiver and it was intercepted. So, next week it will be Shurmur Sanders getting the start against the Buffalo Bills. So, all eyes will be on that as this Brown quarterback competition continues to unfold and really a lot of eyes going to be on Thursday, the joint practice with the Buffalo Bills at the CrossCountry Mortgage Campus. That should give some insights on to how this thing is going. So, Todd Monken not a winner in his debut, but hey, it's the preseason. These ones don't count. The Browns will have the Bills next week. They'll finish out the preseason at home with the Patriots and then it will be Jacksonville, the season opener on the road. This has been your game recap presented by Vivid Seats.

So, how do you feel about the fact that the competition is continuing and that you're going to have more opportunities and it's kind of a big week. >> Yeah, just again, take advantage of those opportunities. Whenever that that my number is called and you know, I'm the guy out there leading the group, you know, you got to continue to just find ways to get better, find success and be positive with it. So, yeah, we just had a take one day at a time. >> You had Spencer out there with you the whole time. What did you see out of the rookie, you know, getting his first his first crack at it? >> Yeah, he was good. I think uh you know, he was, you know, making sure that left side was, you know, very very uh comfortable and I think that, you know, with him going against verse each and every day prepared him for these moments. So, uh Spencer is just definitely going to be a big factor for this team. Um you know, I think that's why we drafted him high is to be able to come in and and compete and and be that guy for us. >> You got the sneak. How did How did that feel to, you know, to convert that? And is that something that you don't mind doing whatsoever if you're called upon to do it regularly? >> Yeah, I don't mind. Whatever is going to help the team, you know, continue to move drives and and have that success. Um not something I want to live in, but uh definitely, you know, whenever it's called, you know, I want to make sure that I'm I'm ready for it and and keep the chains moving. >> Once again, can you sort of, when you look out there and you see, you know, Casey and Denzel and Isaiah and Jerry and everybody, Harold, um can you see how uh if you're playing at your peak efficiency that this could be an explosive offense? >> Yeah, definitely can. I mean, all those guys are very explosive with the ball in their hands. Um we've seen it seen it today with Casey, Denzel you've seen flashes, obviously last year with Harold, and then Jerry I'll I'll obviously has shown that over his years. So, you know, all those guys being young and being in fresh and, you know, having those opportunities to get the ball in their hands can be very very explosive. So, you know, we're definitely excited for that and continue to put those reps in and get that trust and and that rhythm back. >> Do you feel like you've Do you feel like you've shown enough uh to this point to be the starter? >> Um you know, again, it goes back to what, you know, Todd and and the organization and the coaching staff want. So, again, every every opportunity that I get, I want to continue to prove. I want to continue to just keep taking, you know, one step forward. Uh and every day is going to be a challenge, but, you know, that's the that's the whole thing about this NFL. It's a business and every day is a challenge, so you got to continue to prove yourself. >> And one more if nobody else has taken it, and that is uh you moved around a little bit. Um how did you feel on your twice surgically repaired leg? >> Felt good. Felt healthy. Felt no worries about it. Wasn't thinking about it. So, I was good to be able to move around, run around, and and be in live action trying to, you know, other guys trying to, you know, hit me and be confident with it. So, work has definitely been put in. Thank you. >> Thank you.

title: Zac Taylor Press Conference - August 15
text: [music] >> Does it have anything on it or is it just sitting? >> No, it's just that knee. >> [clears throat] >> Now that B.J. Hill uh activated, what's the coverage plan going to be like this week and going on? >> Getting him back in individual. Uh we've got two practices here the next two days, so the point of getting him going today um see see how he feels after today, what the plan will be for tomorrow, and then Tuesday. So, really just kind of taking it this this next 4-day segment there, but he's in the right spot now to get out there and start working. His rehab has gone well, and so I'm excited to get him back on the field and see what he can do. >> Anybody you'll have limited today coming off the game? >> McKinley um McKinley will be out today. I think he's he's the primary one from the game um that will be restricted today. >> Any uh when you saw the tape anything that you didn't notice or feedback? >> No, I mean there's always preseason one, there's always going to be some clean some things to clean up operationally. I think on offense that's probably the main takeaway is operationally we weren't great. Um yeah, you know, I it's I'm not going to lower our standard just cuz it was a preseason game, but sometimes when you're you're changing up personnel constantly that that these things can happen. Uh but I like to speak cleaner this week obviously, and I expect us to be after the practice in the game. But um I thought the guys played hard, they competed. A lot of guys got opportunity, we put a lot of guys out there and found a way to win the game, so that was that was fun for us to see. >> What was your impression of the backup offensive line? They got a lot of run while you were out there. [snorts] >> They did. I think there's pros and cons to it. You know, it's obvious things that we're going to improve, and um there's still a lot of competition there, so I think that's the main takeaway. Is there's still a lot of competition for for those number two jobs on the O-line. >> After the game you spoke about running out the clock to win. Like when you get into the regular season, how much of that is scheme, how much of that is the talent, how much of that is just like the will that that moves the ball forward? >> Both all three of those things that you just mentioned. I think that the scheme is really important to put our guys in an advantageous situation to where they can now get us that extra yard or two for some tough looks cuz you're typically going to be out numbered. So, you want to give them the best opportunity to be able to to grind out of a four-yard run, which is really challenging in a four-minute look. So, um I I think all the above. I I think in the preseason game we're going to hold our guys accountable, find a way. We're not giving them every scheme answer to be able to do that. So, sometimes it's not their best hand going forward, but but there's still opportunity there on those three plays that we ran for us to get a little bit more than what we got. >> When you look at like just the regular season of it's like what do you feel like you guys can be doing in those four minutes doing better in those four >> I can't tell you that, Charlie. I mean, we spent a lot of time on that. >> Coach, the rookies Powell, Young, Landers, >> [snorts] >> Jack. >> Yeah. >> Um thoughts on their you know, what they did first time out of the gate. >> Yeah, I thought um they all showed well. I thought that those guys have improved over the course of camp. They've They've all shown us, you know, you can throw Byron Parker in there too. He got a lot of run in there. I think the two that who Bobo and uh uh Connor were the two that didn't get to play. Um but I was I was pleased with with what they showed us. There's improvement, you know, that I'm sure there's a lot of excitement as they go out there for the first couple snaps and and some things that they can get better at, but um I'm certainly pleased with the direction that all these guys are heading in right now. >> What do you think of Chris Jenkins and just kind of what you've seen from him? >> Yeah, just competing. You know, we we obviously for a guy like that we we added guys to the mix. Um and Chris has really just put his head down and worked and I thought he showed well in the game the other day, you know, and in finding a role for himself and finding a way to impact the defense and you know, a lot of times with those D-tackles, they're not always the guy making the play, but maybe they created the play for somebody next to them or somebody behind them. And [snorts] so, I think Chris um is a really unselfish player that way and and is just trying to play his role the best of his abilities and and make an impact on our team. >> How does now inserting B.J. into this defensive tackle room, the defensive line you've seen so far in camp, what does that add to that unit in your eyes? >> Well, obviously a starter capable player who's got a lot of experience um who's been in a lot of different situations that I think is going to help those around him, too. So, I think when you just add him to the mix of guys that we have right now, we've always been counting on B.J. to come back and help us and and we'll certainly [clears throat] over the next week make it make it happen the right way for him as he hasn't been on the field in a while, but uh leadership experience I I just think that there's a lot he can bring to the table there. >> How have you seen Jordan Battle kind of develop over the years and get to the point where he seems to be a guy playing with a lot of confidence now? >> He's always been a confident guy. Um so now his years in the league I think have just put him in a with the experience that he's gotten to be able to play fast and you know, he's he's I I just have always appreciated his confidence and energy. I think guys respond well to that. Um I've always had a lot of confidence because of that and and so now he's just he's playing really fast. He's seeing the defense very clearly. He's making high-level adjustments the first day of training camp we had here. So, you can tell that the scheme makes sense to him and he's ready for for year two in this exact system. So, I've just I've been I've been pleased with the job that he's doing right now in training camp. >> Ja'Quan shared with us that after the game on Thursday that Dontae Myers drove up here from Atlanta on a night's notice to throw with him before the start of training camp. Just wondering your thoughts on his development through camp till this point. >> He's worked really hard. some of you all may know the background better than I do overall. You know, I kind of see the scouting background, but you don't know the depth of what he went through to get there. And so he's certainly put a lot into it. So, it's not surprising that on a whim he's going to come up and make sure he doesn't miss an opportunity that he's maybe waited his whole life for. So, um I think the competition in that room has been really good, you know, at the receiver spots and at the returner spot. And all those guys have really shown up, Dante being one of them. But, there's still some time to let it play out here um a lot of opportunity for those guys will be forthcoming. >> So, you Thursday's uh Thursday's joint practice is kind of like a pseudo preseason game. How do you approach uh practice like that since you guys didn't do it last season? >> Which compa- I think for our guys when they exit the locker room and go on the practice field, it feels like a game to them. You know, it's um it's another opponent that that you know, we haven't seen in practice for the last 3 weeks. And so, they'll be excited to go do that. So, there's a lot of that energy and tempo that's going to come with that. And [snorts] we'll we'll get a chance to check the box on about every different situation that can come up in practice. Normal downs, third down, red zone, end of game, 2-minute, 4-minute. So, I know our guys will be excited for it. You know, and we'll we'll treat it like we would in a game. It's just more controlled environment. You get a chance to make sure you're hitting certain situations and getting guys certain reps for for certain looks and um so, it's good it's good change of pace for camp. I think for our guys something to look forward to, something to do here at our home field, and and it'll be good practice for us. >> And how will that impact two plays? How will that impact two plays on >> Yeah, on Saturday. It'll It'll impact two plays on Saturday. >> Going off of the joint practice question, do you kind of approach these next couple of days a little differently knowing that, you know, Thursday's going to be a high-energy day or anything like that? >> Wednesday would, you know, so we'll just do a walk-through on Wednesday to give them that day back. But, we're going to go pretty hard at it on Tuesday. So, you know, we're going to get good work in the next 2 days here, Saturday, Sunday, Monday will be a day off. Tuesday is going to be a physical, long practice. Wednesday will be walk-through only, and then Thursday will go essentially play game. >> You were talking to Cleve about talking about today and Sunday. Uh talking, you know, I guess you look forward to Sunday. >> I like to practice. You know, it's uh spent a lot of time thinking about what we want to work on and and how we want to structure the faces and scripts and So, we have red zone lockout today. I think it's your favorite drill. You know, it's it's who's going to win red zone lockout if if of course the storm gives us It looks like it's coming. I don't know. I'm I'm a part-time weatherman right now, so I think uh full-time weatherman, so we'll we'll see. Hopefully. But we we got a chance to get some good work in today. That'll be fun. >> So, C Wright left the team here so what are the opportunities? Do you have any other information on what that might be? >> I I don't know how to properly define it for him. He called us last night and let us know that um he had an opportunity. I know it was a difficult decision for him. I think two things he's really passionate about were colliding and and he decided to pursue this opportunity. So, he he's great kid, comes from a great university. Um and you know, we [clears throat] wish him the best. He he was fun to be around. He really competed hard for us. It's fun watching him play. I thought he was ascending as a player, uh but but obviously he's chosen to go a different path. >> What kind of a camp do you feel like Orlando Orlando has had? >> I I think he's motivated to to give us the best version of himself. You know, and so he's been a strong leader on this team. And I think anytime something doesn't go perfectly, he he wears it, you know, and um takes ownership for it. So, I I think anytime Joe gets hit, you know, all those guys are are trying to figure out what they can do better. And and we all are. None of us want to be in that position, so um and there's things that we can always do to help those guys as well. >> I think you said he played eight snaps, I think. Something like that. Was that Is that what you're trying to get Just see your tailor, you said? >> Yes, sir. >> Okay. >> Is that cuz you're trying to get all get those other guys, you know, Locks, Josh, and some of those guys? >> Yeah, I I Yeah, it's all You know, it's Um sometimes you hit the snap count you're looking for with guys. Sometimes the game the game just goes away where where guys play more or less than you want. And then you got two other games to figure out how you want to handle that to to recover that. So, um I wouldn't always read too much into the snap counts guys get in the preseason games because we got we got two more to play. >> I think Josh is Josh new >> I think he's playing with a lot of confidence. He understands the scheme. And so, that gives him a chance to to play the best of his abilities year two doing the things we're asking him to to do. And he's been really competitive for us. And and I've got faith in him that if he's out there, um he can make some plays for us. >> How do you think Josh Johnson played for you? >> I I thought he managed it really well. He did. And it's uh you know, my first time calling a game with him. Uh I I thought he handled the huddle really well. I thought It It can be challenging because again, you got some guys that don't always get a ton of the reps. And so, there's there's some alignment things that as a quarterback, you've got to lead the charge and make sure everything's operational. And I thought Josh um did a good job getting the line of scrimmage. When the ball was snapped, he made really good decisions, took care of the ball. You know, that we had that the intentional grounding before the half. That's not on him. Um but I I was proud of the way Josh played. >> Sometimes coaches use the preseason for your staff to do different things on game day. Have Did you do anything like that? Do you have plans to do anything like that? >> Not yesterday. No, not yesterday. We didn't or two whatever it was two days ago. Um nothing different, you know, but we will look at these next two games, particularly on offense. You know, Al will let Al make the decisions he wants to make on defense. It's about getting yourself in a position to be ready for the season. So, everyone's a little bit different. Um with me and Pitch, I I do like I think it's good for Pitch to be able to call some plays, call some games, call a half, however it shakes out. And it helps him supplement me during the season, you know, to be in that those shoes of calling plays and seeing the things you go through and the decisions you got to make. Um it's good for me, too, to be able to be in a support role. So, we have the next two games to sort out how that's going to be defined. Um but but he's always done a great job when those opportunities have arisen. >> This year, you guys have a smaller number of undrafted free agent rookies. It felt like you brought a lot of older guys back from the practice squad or stuff like that. Have you felt that difference in that experience on the back of your roster? >> I I I haven't thought a lot about that, to be quite frank with you. Um so, I'm kind of going through it in my mind. Yeah, I I feel like there's probably not as much youth to where they're seeing it for the first time. You know, you There's some names that are clicking in my head that are veteran players that um have been here. I mean, looking at our practice squad list from the final cuts last year to now, there is a lot of carryover there. So, these guys know what to expect, and so they do operate at a higher level. Um I don't know if I just gave you a great answer, but that's that's what I got for you. >> Is there a different vibe with Press when it's preseason, or is it uh still, you kind of your heart of it? >> Uh yeah. Yeah, I'd like to beat him. Uh I don't know if this game will count in the the Taylor family uh polls. I think it's the first question. I think it's the first time we played him in the preseason, actually. Um I tried to call I tried to call him as he was in the press box to see if he'd answer and I could get him fined, but he didn't answer just now. I think we're past that point right now, so I had a script question for Thursday, but >> it'll be fun to see him. You know, it's a great opportunity for my family, you know, it'd be fun for my parents and siblings to all come and his family to come and cousins get to see each other in rare that you get a more deep decompressed environment, you know, to be able to um enjoy the whole family. It's often times been when we're playing them in a high-stress situation. We always play them in December. It's always uh everything is on the line. The whole world's on the line, and that's what we're playing. That's stressful. Not for me necessarily, but for the families, and so it would be good to to get these guys in August and have them come down here and um after the practice, enjoy some time with their family. >> So, you could you could talk to him during this week, right? >> Yeah. Yeah, yeah. There's Yeah, this is this is just practice. >> But what do you got to do from a logistical standpoint? >> We do have to do it from a logistical standpoint, yeah. >> How many people are you expecting? >> My whole family. Yeah, just my immediate family his immediate family, my immediate family, and my my parents and siblings. >> That See, you know was he the last guy who would get picked in your games cuz he was like the little guy, the little brother or something? >> Um yeah. Well, no. He wasn't. No, there was three of them. Uh it was him, Sam, and Blaine. I would say Press was usually the bigger of the three. So, depending on the sport, I would I would say who was usually last. But yes, he was 5 years younger than me. So, um he was they were the little kids. That's how we viewed them back then. I wouldn't say that anymore. He's got four kids of his own now. Uh but yeah, back then, yeah. I mean, imagine I'm a freshman, eighth grader, and he's in fourth grade, fifth grade, and yeah, you wanted to punch him sometimes. Probably did. >> I was hoping you did. >> [laughter] >> I think he punched me more than I punched him, to be honest about something. >> He might want to punch him Thursday. Who knows? >> Yeah, maybe. Maybe after the game. It's going to happen though. >> Me and Ben get into it, he's got to jump in. He's got to pick sides. Maybe I'm not going to be able to do that. Yeah. >> All right, thank you. >> Hey, sir. If you roll out of town then >> [music]

title: Cowboys Players Discuss First Preseason Win | Player Interviews
text: Can you just talk about I mean undrafted rookie and I mean it's not a small school but it's not a power program but being able to come out here and put on the show that you put talk about your grit. What this says as far as you know your abilities go. >> Um I say just waking up every day having gratitude towards the game. Um shoot I came from Auburn. I came from Georgia Southern. I done seen it all. Um just to be here at this level just putting it all together and being the best version of myself every day is the main ultimate goal of just life. Um, sometimes you get knocked down, sometimes you bring up and shoot, today um, showed it all. Like just being undrafted itself um, just put a chip on your shoulder. Like now that I look at it, I'm I'm glad I'm glad I got drafted cuz you can be the best version of yourself every single day and you don't feel complacent a little bit. Like I feel like it put an edge to me just a little bit more. You know what I'm saying? So I'm I'm very very highly thankful. >> What's going through your mind as you're making that catch, that touchdown catch from Joe Milton, the one-handed? >> Yeah. Um, shoot. When the ball in the ass is mine, that's that's that's always been a mindset from Georgia Southern and the Auburn. Um, and just having that mentality cuz I feel like just playing football in general is having the right mentality. So, yeah. >> You set the school record at Georgia Southern for touchdown catches last year. What makes you so good at getting the ball when it's in the air and and that it's yours? >> Um, I say I say being dependable on gaining trust from the um from the coaches, from anybody for real. So just being dependable and just showing showing everybody that you can do what you got to do. Um be available at all times. So I feel like just being here in the NFL is just about being available. Um building trust, building the best version of yourself and be on your feet at at the end of the day. >> You mentioned that chip on your shoulder. Um and then the edge you play with every day. What does that edge look like on a daily basis at camp? How much does that remind you to not get complacent on a daily basis? >> I say um it's from the way you wake up. Um from the way you wake up. Um, shoot. Every day, don't feel complacent. Wake up with a with a with a edge. Um, showing gratitude. Like, don't show up every day and be like, "Man, I got to I got to survive today." No, you don't want to be like that. So, me as a as a me as a person, I'm showing up every day with gratitude. Every every single day to play the game I love every day is football. So, it's it's a it's a privilege. So, that's the um main thing, too. You mentioned going undrafted back in April, draft week before the swings of emotions. And how does this night make you feel in a totally different place than that? >> Uh, I say it was a it was a it was a great feeling cuz I feel like I get to prove another um people wrong again. Um, that just that's just who I am. That's been my whole life story. Um, my little sister right here, she done prove everybody wrong. Um, so that's that's just who I am. Um just we all like the way my family built we always prove everybody wrong. So we just continue to do that and be the best version of ourel every single day we wake up. >> You share about her story. >> Yeah. Um she had kidney failure. Um people said she wasn't going to make it past three. Um she still proved people wrong and she lived to 17 years old. So um this this past week was kind of um a little rough for me cuz August 13th, 2021 was one of the ways she passed away. Um, so I'm I'm blessed. Um, just living living through her every single day. And I feel like she lived through me today. So that's that's just the exciting thing about me every single day is the way I can share my story and be the best version of myself every single day. >> Uh, a lot of receivers have better chemistry with one quarterback versus another quarterback. You were out there producing with Sam How comes in, you produce with Joe Mill. What does that say about your skill set as far as your ability to do it regardless of who's under? Um, I say talking like communication is the biggest key when you come to football or being with a team. Just talking. Um, just have a good conversation with people and you building every single day. You have an opportunity to go with a quarterback this and that and that and that and that and that and that and that and that and that and that third. I'm talking to Dak. I'm talking to Sam. I'm talking to Joe. I'm talking to everybody. That's how you build a connection with a quarterback. Um, JC French was my quarterback at Georgia Southern. I built a connection with P. Thorne was my quarterback at uh Auburn. So, just building a connection with them. Um they just text my phone to this day. So it make you feel like you did something right. >> Yeah. >> You mentioned your sister. Um what would she say after a performance like this? >> She'll be proud of me. She'll be she she's smiling at me right now. That's how that's how I live through it. Like she she's smiling at me and I'm happy for it. >> To be able to have a performance like that, but also have a guy like CD Lamb have the biggest celebration for you when you come back. What does that mean to you? I say like on Sundays you watching them play and living out the dream that you living right now. It's a blessing and that's that's how you look at it for real. So I'm just thankful to even share the room with them, get knowledge from them. Um and that's for everybody in the room. I'm just getting knowledge. I'm pour everybody pouring into me. So that's a blessing in itself. >> You've been doing this in person, but do game. What does that mean? >> How your dreams become a reality. That's that's just how it is. And every day from the preparation, that's how I look at it. Um, I feel like I could have I could have um came out here and did what I got to do. So, just keep keep doing what I'm doing. It's preparation. Say every time. So, yeah. >> All right. Thank you. >> Thank y'all so much. >> Joe, uh, without over before you go back and watch the film, what's the the biggest takeaway you have for both yourself from this game, but as well as just the offense and being able to move the ball? >> Um, the biggest takeaway I have for myself is probably just um, keep seeing it, man. Um, just keep seeing it, keep aggressing. Um, and just keep having fun. I think that's to my biggest my biggest blessing is to have fun. So, um, just keep doing that. And then for the team, man, just keep going. Um, keep chipping away one play at a time. Uh, champions find a way. >> Speaking of having fun, how much fun did you have watching Camden Brown bring that ball, man? >> Oh, shoot man. I was on the ground um hoping um really not hoping. I seen him pretty much watch him run his whole route um as I was taking my snap from under the center. It was great, man. Just to see a rookie come in undrafted, just make a catch like that, especially one hand. For sure. >> What impresses you most about what he's able to do from what you've seen so far? >> A lot. I don't know where to start from with that uh with that guy. But um Cam is a a great person. Great kid, man. Uh well, he's a adult now, but younger than me, so great kid, man. You know, just someone that loves to learn. Um someone that literally asks questions every day. Um and he's one of the per one of the people that if he don't know it, he will ask. So that's probably my biggest my biggest thing on camp for sure. >> What do you think back to, you know, this time last year and playing in these games? How much different do you feel in your game now? >> Uh, a lot different. Um, I'm able to I went through a whole year of game planning with these coaches. So, I'm able to game plan the right way now. Um, get an understanding of what they're thinking. Um, shoot, I was able to fix a play and last year I don't think I would have I would have be able to did that. Uh, so I was able to fix a play today. So, uh, it's great, man. It's great. >> Not that you weren't confident last year, but kind of speaking to what you just said, you were able to fix a play. Do you feel more confident? >> Absolutely. Absolutely. I feel more confident, but I also just feel just me. Um, I feel like Joe. Um, and shout out to the coaches that was out there today coaching and was able to put me in the right position. >> Said, you know, the battle for GB will be decided a lot in these series games. So, obviously there's pressure on these three days. Pressure made diamonds. Pressure made diamonds. That's how I look at it. >> How do you feel about your Cowboys debut? >> Um, it was fun. Anytime you get to go out there and play football, um, it's fun. We move the ball. All right. Um, obviously there's some plays that, uh, we like to have back, but it was good to get out there and, um, play with the guys, and we have a lot of fun out there. I'm sure there's things that we we can clean up, but, um, like I said, it was just good to get out there and play football again. >> Was a night of sustained drives. I mean, there were some really long ones. You don't really seem to see too much of that in preseason games. Seahawks had some too that you felt like you were maybe able to get in a little more rhythm. >> Yeah, for sure. Um yeah, we put that one I think I don't know how many plays it was 16 17 play drive together. Um it's just a you know it shows you how how well we were able to execute. Um but we did a lot of good things. A lot of guys made a lot of good plays. Um so something to build on for sure. >> Sorry. Yep. All good. Sam, before you go guys go back and watch the film, what, you know, in real time, what do you feel your biggest positive take away from this offense was against the feed off? >> Yeah, I think we showed when we do what we're supposed to do and everyone knows their job, we show how we can move the football. Um, no matter what group is in there, no matter, you know, where everybody's at in the depth chart, if we go in there and do what we're supposed to do, we can move the football. Um, we have a lot of guys on this team that can make plays. Um, and I think that showed tonight. And so, we just got to keep growing, keep building, um, you know, use this game as momentum to keep getting better. Speaking of guys that can make plays, what do you make of the game that uh that Camden Brown has had, but also the fact that he's stacking that on top of the good [clears throat] days he's having at Oxford? >> For sure. Like you said it, you said it well. He's he's been having a really good camp. I love throwing to him. Joe loves throwing to him. So Cam has been a great player. Um you know, he's he gets open and when you throw it to him, he catches it. Um and so he's he works so hard. title: Brian Schottenheimer: Postgame Preseason Week 1 #DALvsSEA
text: Uh, Joe Hoy in Dallas, Morning News. Uh, Brian, just give us your overall first impressions of tonight's game. >> Yeah, a lot of great things, Joe. Uh, thought the second half was really, um, really well played. I thought, uh, defensively they were amazing. I think, uh, three or four, um, three and four and outs. I thought they were awesome. A couple of the red zone stops. Um, Jonathan Mingo, I think in the first half made an incredible play, you know, on a punt return, stopped it, and then obviously we muffed the fumble there. Late, defense goes right back out there. Um, little bit of training camp football, a little sloppy. Um, that's kind of what you deal with, but overall I thought the team effort, uh, to get the win, um, against a good opponent, uh, was was really good. Um, things we obviously need to clean up, the penalties. Uh, they threw a lot of penalties really on both teams. Uh, but, you know, that's what the preseason for. Work on your hand placement, get better. Um, but to overall I was really, really proud of our guys. >> Cam Brown has made plays, multiple touchdown catches in training camp, obviously two tonight. What have you seen from him, and just what can you say about his performance tonight? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, the game's not too big for him. He does that every, every, every day in practice. We see it all the time, and um, you know, I thought it was a really, really good throw by Sam. Tight coverage, but they trust him. And then, you know, Joe's throw on the the fade, he gets blasted. Um, and uh, one-handed catch from him, but he's been doing that the whole time. And what I love about him is, you know, he does the little things, too. You you watch him on special teams, and one-on-one drills, things like that. He realizes that, you know, that's how you make this football team. When you've got a receiver room that's filled with George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb, Ryan Flournoy, people like that, you know, that stuff matters. So, um, you know, really good day, but he's got to keep stacking them like he's been doing. >> Clarence Hill, Dallas Cowboys. It seemed like you were rewarding him last week by giving him reps with the first team. Does it confirm going into the game what you've been seeing in practice? >> Um, talking about Cam? >> Yeah. >> Yeah, I mean, yeah, I mean, we've wanted to get him in there a little bit, uh, with the first team. And when we put him in there, uh, he's done a really good job, you know, Clarence and um, we actually moved him over to that position for the second one, you know, cuz he normally plays flanker and we moved him over there and like I said, the throw from Joe was terrific, but you know, the the the catch was incredible as well and but yeah, he's just consistent, man, and that's what we want as coaches. We want people that are consistent, they're the same every day and yeah, they might have a bad day or dip, but then they bring it right back. >> Defensively, they actually got four trips inside the red zone and they only scored seven points. I mean, I know it's backups whatever it was, but that's kind of what you want to see from your defense. >> Yeah, I mean, the defense the defense's job is to keep people out of the end zone. I mean, that's what we're tasked to do and you know, I'm fine winning games 7 to 3, 10 to 7. I don't care. But I thought they were were terrific. I thought you know, we were a little sloppy early on, you know, and we gave them some hidden yards with penalties early on, but I thought they really buttoned down and I thought the pass rush was really good. We let Milroe get out a few times, which he's very athletic, but overall, I was very very pleased. Anytime you can get three and outs and four and outs in the red zone stops, that's what you want. >> Nick Harris from the Star-Telegram, how would you evaluate your quarterbacks tonight and specifically with up and down play up front? >> Yeah, you know, it's hard to speak on quarterbacks, Nick, when you don't watch the film, but I thought both guys functioned outstanding. You know, they both were tasked with going out there and playing against heavy pressure, you know, a Mike McDonald, Aidan O'Connell Day, you know, defense is going to be a heavy pressure team and they brought a bunch of things against us that you know, not that we weren't prepared for, but that maybe we didn't handle very well. So, they were taking some shots, but they just hung in there and made the throws when they had to make them and they were both very efficient, you know, and that's what we want. You know, we want to we evaluate quarterbacks by a couple things. One, moving the team, scoring points and then two, protecting the football and I thought both guys did that. Joe with his legs, I mean, you know, he's pretty much unstoppable on quarterback sneaks and so, it didn't take me long to figure out that I wasn't going to do anything different. I was just going to let him sneak it, and uh you know, he's a big, powerful man, but they both played well. >> Uh would you say your offensive line settled in in the second half? >> Uh I think so. You know, a lot of moving parts. It's hard. You know, a lot of moving parts. Like I said, they threw a lot of things at us. Uh I want to look at the film. Um definitely some leaky moments. Um but early on, especially, we struggled to move their guys up front. I think you'll see that. That's why the run numbers in the in the first half weren't very good. They were doing a good job plugging up the middle, and um you know, so, we started the second half actually with a perimeter play, and we have those. Uh we didn't want to show too many of them, but um you know, uh give them some credit cuz I thought early on their defensive uh front was really a handful for us. >> And just kind of on that, is it kind of tough to evaluate running backs when the those kind of things are happening right now? >> Yeah. Yeah, I mean, you know, you got to you got to get what's blocked. And um again, I thought all of our guys ran hard. I mean, give it up for Malik Davis. I mean, you know, just the uh holiday horror. I mean, he just you wasn't a holi- was a holiday day? I don't think it was a holiday day, but uh I mean, he's amazing. Christmas Day, Thanksgiving Day, whatever the day is, 14th of August. Um I love that I love that guy. >> Coach, Tommy Lusk at Go Power Cat if you could expand a little bit more on your all of your running backs, Jayden, Phil, those guys. What what's the I know you want to watch the film back, but what did you like from each of those guys? >> Yeah, you know, again, I think, you know, I'll I'll work backwards. I thought late in the game, you know, Izzy ran really hard, man. I mean, it was heavy box, and they knew that we were in four-minute, and you know, I'm really proud of our ability to stay on the field and not have to give them the ball back after we got the big stop after the muffed punt, and um thought Izzy ran really, really hard. Uh I thought the receivers blocked really well. Malik, you know, he's just a slasher, man, and his vision and understanding of blocking schemes and all that, I think, was great. Um you know, Phil had some really good runs. Um and then, you know, Jayden, there wasn't a whole lot there, but you know, you get him going on screens and things like that. He's just He's a weapon, so again, I'll know more watching the film, but uh they all ran hard. Um we found our rhythm a little bit in the second half. Um and uh um you know, there's certainly a lot to clean up there. >> Any early thoughts on Caleb Downs and Malachi Warner and what they did in their albeit limited time today? >> Yeah, um not really. Um again, I know it seemed like Caleb was out pretty quick. Um that was the plan, of course, which you stick to the plan and then I thought Malachi had a couple really good rushes that I saw affecting the quarterback and um you know, I thought he definitely settled in, but for the most part those guys we see it every day. They're going to get great work against the Saints here in a couple days and um all in all, I thought uh you know, they played they played well. >> Andrew Destin with the Associated Press. Uh do you have any update on Phil, how his status is today? >> Yeah, he's okay. I talked to him. Yeah, he's he's okay. I think we came out of okay, little bumps and bruises. You know, Justin Barron, he got rocked a little bit. Um and then uh Phil, but uh I think everybody's okay and um you know, we'll figure out a little bit more when we, you know, wake up in Oxnard tomorrow morning and get them all treated, but I know the masseuses are going to be busy tomorrow, so um it's physical game and as you would expect coming in to play in the Seahawks led by Mike McDonald. >> Couple of things. You think Holden was pressing a little bit trying to return that punt? >> Um I don't know. I mean, I want to talk to him. I know he was disappointed. I mean, he knew he made a mistake. Uh Tress Wayans wants to win. He's competing. I think anytime players step up, you know, you can be affected by that, but uh Tress Wayans is a pro and he'll bounce back. >> And um we talked about all the edge rushers, but James Houston continues to show up. I mean, he's like Malik Davis on that side. You talk about everybody else and >> they still make >> He's mad at me cuz I I I took the I accepted the penalty, you know. So, I said, "Hey, you get lots of sacks. You'll be fine." But uh yeah, I mean, the guy's just got a a knack. I mean, he's a awesome rusher and um you know, he uh he's been doing it uh in this league for a long time and uh I really just appreciate the way he works and uh it's uh it's a special trait that he has. >> Uh CP's first game obviously calling plays from the sideline. How do you think that went for him? Obviously the defense settled down after the first drive. >> Yeah, I thought he was really good, you know, and I was over there listening on two and uh you know, he is he is what he is, man. He's calm, cool, convicted. Uh again, uh when we uh gave him the ball on the muff punt down there late he said, "Nah, man." I mean, like he was there was zero you know, we need that. We need the adversity. There's going to be adversity and uh that's going to happen in in the season and so it was really cool for our guys to respond, but um I thought he did a great job.
