title: Ennis Rakestraw Jr. and Chris Smith Media Availability | 2026 Training Camp Day 12
text: What does it feel like to be out here specifically today given, you know, just the kind of scare that you faced the other night? >> Um, it it feel good to be back, you know. It's just a contusion, so I'm good. I'm out here to the next practice putting hands on people. It's just a part of the game. I just got to stay healthy. That's it. >> Does that I mean, just just the emotions of that moment though. I mean, how much fear did you have to deal with in that the sense of relief when, you know, you get checked out and process it, realize that it is just a contusion? >> I already kind of knew it was a contusion, but you know, they got to go through tests regardless to see what it is. And then the test came back negative. Just a good sigh of relief, you know. I prayed. Um, I ain't never think I wasn't going to play again. I knew I feel like it was contusion, so I'm just happy to be right. >> Do you feel like that's a reflection of the work you put in though to make sure your body was right and could maybe handle a little bit more? I mean, I don't know. We talked about this a little bit just the the upper body work you've kind of put in. Do you think that was, you know, maybe helpful in this situation? >> Um, yeah. Big back, you know, got to bring it down somehow. It's just the nature of the game. It's it's part of the business. If if I didn't make the tackle, he probably would have scored, so I'm sometimes got to throw your body in there. That's what I signed up for. >> So, the worst part of it that you didn't get get the full workload that you thought you maybe you were going to get that day? >> Yeah, but you know, another preseason game coming up. Just thing I do out here is stack days, get better. I had some up and down moments. Now I'm just trying to stay here. >> When you process the film from that one, I mean, it's what what did you like about the performance? What did you, you know, want to tighten up for the upcoming week? >> I think I had one man man rep where the catch was the out route, you know. Other than that, it was like zones. I just hate how PFF did me, but it is what it is, you know. They don't know what they're talking about anyway. They couldn't even tell me what coverage he was in, but like I said, I just got to get better. We all going to get better and just get ready for the next game. >> How do you feel at this point in camp? What was maybe the main focus this off season for you? >> Get to this point, you know, like get to a preseason game. Last year, like my goal is when I stepped on this year was to make it through day one cuz I got hurt day one. Then make it to the first preseason game. I made it through. People thought I didn't, but I made it through the first preseason game. So, I just keep checking the small boxes every day and everything will come back where it's supposed to come out to. >> Another box to check too you spent some fun healthy competition with Jaylen out here with you guys going one-on-one. Just can you take us inside that competition between the two of you and how you make each other better? >> Uh he told me something that he seen while he was beating me and I appreciated it and then when I went to him again, I changed it up and he was like we like see that's why I dabbed him up after the play that went viral. I'm like okay, so like finally he told me what I need to do and then today had some good reps. It just all them guys good. Jaylen, Saint, they top for a reason. So, you know, they go get paid theirs and it's just my turn to get paid mine. That's it. >> How valuable is that valuable to get that kind of information from somebody like that? >> Um I feel like it's we all want everybody to get better and y'all just want to stack days and win. So, anybody help anybody. In the DB room when we watch it together they DJ, Rock, Whiteside, everybody got feedback and coaches. So, we just trying to make everybody better at the end of the day. That's all we can do. >> So, what about that Jaylen feedback? Was that earlier in camp or was that earlier today? >> No, that was earlier in camp. That was the right after the punch out and then after the punch out play he was like the play before that I knew you was going to like your hips. I was like how you know? And then he told me I ain't going to say it on camera, but he told me. So, okay, bet. So, then the next day we came and then he ran that route and I was on it. I dabbed him up. I was like I see what you talking about. I appreciate it. >> This is a stance battle cuz it seemed like early on he was winning a lot of those snaps and then now as camp progresses you're not giving up >> Yes, he told me what he told he found my kryptonite so I had to change it. >> You mentioned you mentioned the PFF, but I mean like the coaches evaluation. What were the things that they said were good and then what did they what did they say they needed to work on coming out of the game? >> Um like I'll say on that one play on the third down that was probably my biggest play that I feel bad about cuz my leverage I should have just stayed to the outside. I was too high and shoulders was too tall. So, that's the technique thing, you know. We you've got to fix the little technique issues. All that PFF stuff, man, they got it cool. Y'all grade how y'all want to grade, but it is what it is. I'm just here to do what I got to do, and whatever the play says we need to do, that's what I'm going to do. >> What did they What did they say though that was encouraging like that? What that they liked? >> They liked how I played. Like I came up and like, you know, a lot of people talk about shoulders. I made a couple tackles in the game, so I'm not scared to throw it up in there, and that's what we all about. DBs that can tackle, run, and hit. >> Mhm. Uh I guess I mean in general like, I mean, how do you take something, you know, the the snaps that you did get and and apply them to to training camp? I mean, what How do you How do you go about doing that I guess going forward? >> Another opportunity. Next game, next practice. That's all I can do. >> And you're talking about learning from Jamo in practice. I mean, you got a chance to go out there against like Chase and Higgins there, too. What can you take away from that? I mean, seeing their main guys out there. >> St. Brown and Jamo, releases is probably top-tier. And a lot of people in league is, well, you go versus them every day, it kind of like give you confidence to go versus other people. And then when you see what they do, I saw Cassian St. do this before. I seen Jamo do that. So it really help when you got guys like them two here. Not just them guys. Test love. We got Laporta. All of them they do what they do. >> Because of you know, the the like the like the preseason experience last year, I mean, was it good to get as many opportun- I mean, to play plays, I mean, the target I mean, having having them, you know, target receivers that you were covering? >> I was Yeah, I was anxious to be honest cuz you know, I ain't played football in almo- like a year and some, almost two, so I was kind of anxious going out there. And then when when the bullets got to flying and everything I got I'm like, "Okay, like I'm back to like football. Like I'm finally in football." So it was my first time being in real football, guys, so jitters out. Next game. >> But who do you think uh just working out something else, but who do you Out of all the players on the team, who do you think is primed for a big season? >> Jamo. Yeah, I I I would say Jamo, man, like sky's limit. Jamo Jamo stay with he doing right here. He going to he going to be what we all believe he is and what he know he is. >> Just based just based on >> Just based on everything. Like every day like he stack days every day. He come out here he compete. He talk trash make you mad that makes you compete harder. That's a leader. >> You know big Judson that that >> Yeah. Yeah, I feel like I mean until camp's over I you know, I'm never going to like be complacent in that but Um so yeah, I don't know I'll just continue to attack every day and just you know keep my head down and not really worry about the end goal just worry about you know the days in front of me. So yeah. >> These guys make errors too but that that play with 10 guys on the field can you just walk me through what you saw why you >> Yeah. Yeah, I mean obviously usually another defensive tackle is on the outside of me. So when I didn't see anyone I looked to the sideline and they're about to snap it. I was just like hey like let me just even it out. I'll go over the center and like we'll try to get out the down but yeah. >> And so what's your mindset then like I got to >> Just clog it yeah just literally clog up the middle like you know they I know it's going to be it was probably 7 yards until um the end zone. So I was just like hey let me just do my best and just try to clog it up and nasty it up so they don't have just like a clear sorry attacking running lane in it. So yeah. >> How do you think you played overall that game? >> Played solid you know there's definitely a couple plays you want back just technique wise but I thought overall I played fine.

title: Dan Campbell Press Conference | 2026 Training Camp Day 12
text: You know, thought a number of guys played really well. Uh especially for their first time under the lights. Um you know, I thought number of guys got better. Some guys that um you know, weren't weren't as good, but you know, the uh no matter who you are, it's about you know, cleaning up the errors, learning from the mistakes, and then growing and getting better. So, uh that's that's what preseason is all about, and we were actually fortunate. We got a number of different situations, looks that you ordinarily don't get, certainly in the preseason, but that first preseason game is a lot of in the half, in the game. Um just you know, a lot of critical situations of you know, for us to be in defensively, offensively, the quarterback, uh special teams. So, it was good. It It was good in that regard. Um Always want to win. You know that You don't want to lose sight of that, but we also were trying to find what guys do well, and can they grow? Is it you know, can they compete? What What are their What's their niche? And And I think we got a little closer to that, finding that out on this roster. Questions? >> Oops, sorry. Uh after watching the film, what maybe stood out of the play in particular up front on the offensive line? Maybe the all all units? >> Well, when we did it right up front, um you know, when we were all together doing it right, using the fundamentals, man, it was pretty. And I mean, we were effective. You know, I thought a number of things in the run game were were really good. Got Sailors going. Um Blackshire had some runs. Um >> [clears throat] >> and that was good to see. And really, the protection was pretty good. You know, I I thought the protection overall was uh you know, was was pretty good. So, there again, it's some of the fundamental stuff. Um Just cleaning some of those guys up, but like I said, I thought Larry handled his business over there at left tackle. I thought Blake Miller did a good job at right tackle. Um Mahogany was a force, you know. Uh, it's just about cleaning up some of the fundamentals, but you know, it was good to see. >> Just to stay with that O-line for a sec, Mahogany, you know, he's taken the vast majority of the the first team reps. Is he closer to locking up that job? And, you know, can you expand a little bit, penalties aside, how he played? >> Yeah, uh, this is still an ongoing battle, and really it it's you know, we're going to I think we'll get Juice back today to where he can work a little bit, and hopefully each day he gets more and more reps. And so, um, that we're not going to do very much team if any today. We'll do a couple of situations, but but really today's, uh, you know, individual one-on-one technique work. Uh, and then the next 2 days will really get going, but get him back and kind of see where that is. And Bartch is is back, you know, he'll be getting more and more reps. So, um, let Mahogany and Bartch, you know, go at it over there at the left guard. And then, obviously, we're evaluating Juice too at center, you know, with Seth or or is it Ratledge? And, you know, we're going to we we got to find the five best. And so, this is an ongoing battle. I thought, uh, I just mentioned this Mahogany, I thought he was a physical force, you know? And when he does it right, it's pretty, and it's powerful, it's explosive, and in the pass game, he's got to anchor, you know, and then, uh, sometimes it just gets a little out of sorts, you know? So, it's just uh, the consistency of it. But, uh, we're going to work him a little bit, you know, I don't know how much we'll do in team, but certainly we're going to be snapping him some, um, pre-practice. And then, he's been going through some of the calls, things like that. So, we're just prepared, um, you know, we got to be able to you know, we got to be willing to go wherever we can go with this. >> There's a lot of stuff, um, >> you you like to say your eyes are open to possibilities. I don't I don't know like how many people really expected him to to have an opportunity to start in a situation, but he put a lot of guys on their their butts in that game. I'm just curious, you know, what what you thought of um, you know, the way he came out and acquitted himself. >> Well, the you know, one of the things we talk about with say he's not he's not this enormous person, you know, he's and and so his niche is playing low. He's quick. He's he's super sharp and he's quick and he's really good at the second level and then pass game is the anchor, right? He's just got to bend and he's got to do and a lot of cases he's got to do double what somebody else does that that has more stature, you know, size or stature to him. That's that's the hand he's dealt. Uh I thought he did that the other night. I did think he anchored better. I thought he strained. I thought he tried to do all the little things, you know, and and that's credit to him. So, you know, I certainly was not disappointed with him the other day. >> Dan, after watching the tape, what do you think of Keith Abney's NFL debut and especially on special teams? >> Yeah, I I thought Abney played a good game. I I you know, the he feels like a football player. He's felt that way out here and that that showed up the other night. He just he's got a knack. He's pretty instinctive. Plays aggressive, not too big for him. And and I thought he did some things certainly on defense but special teams, too. There was a couple of you know, things where he's out there at jammer that were a little bit we got to work on some stuff. Um but overall he he certainly showed up, man. It was it was that was a that was that was good by him. >> You said Juice is coming back. Anybody else Darrel Moore, Malcolm, anybody else? >> Yeah, Moore will start working back here a little bit. We'll we'll work those guys progressively. Um get them back every every day a little bit more and more provided no setbacks. So, you know, I think we'll get Vahe out there a little bit. You know, Moore is one of them. We talked about Juice. I think D.J. Reed's going to start working back in. So, we're about to get a lot of guys back here. >> What was your evaluation of Ennis, Dan? >> I'm sorry. >> an update on Ennis just physically? >> Yeah, he should be good. He should be good. >> Speaking of that, what was your evaluation of him before he got hurt? >> Of Ennis? Uh I thought man, I there was a couple of really good coverage reps in there. You know, there's one and then there's one where it looks like it's on him, it's not on him, you know, um third and 16. We're supposed to have somebody underneath him. We told him to you know, play high over the top of that. There's supposed to be somebody insulating, so that was a we had a mental error underneath it uh but I thought he had a good a couple of really good challenge reps outside and then you know, it was unfortunate that um we we couldn't get a full dose with him because of you know, his uh his injury. But but it's not serious. He should be out there running around. >> Did you feel like he was hurting you a lot? >> Uh not necessarily. Uh I didn't feel that way going in there. I I think those guys are going to run with their going to run, you know, um and take the best play uh available, set their guys up. You know, normally that goes at the boundary, so >> Was there was there anyone um who might not have caught your eye from the sideline or in the moment who wound up popping when you went back and and watched the tape? >> Um watching the tape Well, I I think this can this match happens naturally. Sometimes you can't always see all the dirty work that goes on. You're not going to know till you get in there. Like Chris Smith, I thought played his tail off. You know, the the amount of just slug it out dirty work that guy does. I mean, we had one clip, we only got 10 on defense and he just he's smart enough to say, you know what? Fine. I he just gets to zero nose to balance out the front. Well, he got three. And he battles in there. He takes three guys on. Um you know, I I thought he I thought he played well, you know, and uh and you don't always get to see that stuff cuz there's so much going on in there, but but he did a good job. Um you know, one guy just bring it up because of the play that he made, you know, just stepped in the door. It's like, who is this guy? And and uh Cooper, you know, it was a hell of a hit he made over there. I know it was one play, but it's like, I know who he is now. Um he got a ball out. So, you know, but there was there was a number of guys I thought played really well, and it was good to see. And I think more than anything, especially for the young guys, you just want to know it's not too much for them, you know? And for the guys that it is, okay, now now let's see how they respond. Was that a one-time deal, or is it oh it's just you know, it is a lot. So, um but it was good for the first outing. >> Maybe the highest for for a couple years now. You guys have like Chris Smith for a couple years now. You know, we cuz he does so much of that dirty work, playing the nose, and some things that we don't see. What is it that you like about him? What what jumps out so much of >> does everything right. He does all the little things right. Um you know, you don't he doesn't make the same mistake twice. He's he's the guys you love to coach because he he's up here all off season, works his tail off, um is always trying to hone his game. Um he plays disciplined football. you know, he he he's a grinder, man. He'll do it he'll take on double teams if you ask him to do it for if you ask him to do it. And that that's a thankless job, and it's hard, and it's nobody really sees that. You don't get any love. Um but he didn't care. Like like to him, that that means more to him to know that he's keeping his linebacker free. Like that that's that's his heaven. You know, um so it's unselfish, and and it's hard. It's a nasty job, and it's not for everybody. And so, that's why you appreciate it. >> Do you feel like the uh receivers distinguish themselves from the game? >> Man, that that's um yeah. yeah. That room right now is interesting. Um Tay Martin showed up again. Blocking, made a one-on-one catch, separated, special teams. He he forced a penalty and that was just one play on special teams. He made more than that. Uh in in the return units and the cover units, um I thought Black showed up, made some plays, you know? he's intriguing. Uh we got Cedric back, you know, he he kind of had that little hip flexor, but I mean, you know, we only got limited reps with him, but I mean, he he's a crafty, savvy veteran. Just just knows how to play, man. He gets it. Smart dude, can play all the positions. Goes out there and makes play for us, you know? Uh and he'll mix it up and block. And he's played teams before. We know Tom Kennedy, you know, reliable, uh steady. So, I mean, that those guys it that room right now is it's an all out right now. So, it's it's pretty exciting. >> You know, we talked to you about Drew and [clears throat] the communication and trying to work through it, but outside of of the obvious of him coming in as the new OC, were there any new game day logistics or communications or guys getting to the bigger role that that worked or didn't work that maybe you worked through in the preseason opener? No, I mean, I mean, I I think there's little things that come up, you know, wanting to get a guy a ball uh or run it here or you know, uh run behind this guy, you know, just those little things that that that come from me that you chirp or you know, that would break his rhythm a little bit, you know, that that's all natural and part of it. Uh But I think it everything everything between us is it was good. I mean, I think that's what you want is he's figuring out my dialogue and my dialect. It's not just you know, uh you know, and what does that mean when I do say it? Does it mean that it's a bad thing? could mean I'm excited or it means run that play again or it means don't run that play again or it means throw to this guy. So, um the four-letter word has many meanings. Um But no, he he did a good job. I thought he was in the flow. You know, he's he's what I thought he would be. He doesn't get friz- frizzled, man. He's on it. He's always thinking of the next play or the one even beyond that. He's got a plan for what's coming up next. Uh Pacheco's still a little bit off or little bit out, I should say. We don't anticipate him being back this week. So, between that, Gibbs got back. You know, he's he's a smart and instinctive player. Just sometimes he just gets lost. And so, if he can start to show that over the last, you know, 2-3 weeks of of of training camp here, he will absolutely have a shot. text: Day 10 of Colts training camp. We're inside the facilities at Grand Park here today with the weather. They've got to have something that the coaching staff can isolate. You don't really have backups who are kind of just the all-around type of player. What has stood out to you most about him in his um skill set and how he's fit into the room and the competition and everything? >> His physicality and his uh energy is unmatched. Uh he loves it. He loves it and we love him. Um he brings a different juice to the room as well. Uh just always ready to go out there, strike somebody, always ready to go out there defend somebody. He's always ready to do what he needs to do. And he's also uh just like CJ, he's eager. He's always asking questions. He always wants to know what's going on. He always wants to know how you can get better as well. So, it's always fun having Bryce as well. >> They really kind of remade the linebacker room uh this off season had a lot of new pieces. On Thursday, there was a series where you, Bryce, and Austin in succession all made big plays to end the drive. What What did that feel like? Just the linebackers putting their stamp on that drive. >> Uh it felt great cuz you know it's it's what we going what we're trying to do for this team. We're also we're trying to make plays for this team. We're trying to do our right assignments for this team. And you know, it's the stuff that we do also after practice. You know, we're always together. We always got a drill or two that we do. You know, we always talk about things that we need to do in the meeting room that we need to uh work on. Our coach always ask us write two write two things down that you need to work on and we always try to fulfill those needs to the best of our abilities. So, um just make seeing all of us make plays, especially this past uh this past game, it was it was it was exciting, man. cuz it's just, you know, it's a feeling when you see everybody doing what you know they can do and everybody enjoying each other at the same time. That's what builds our team and that's what builds this brotherhood. >> Know when we would talk to Chris Ballard or or Lou or even Shane throughout this offseason, they would sometimes tell us like, you know, Jaylen can be healthy. Um they like think of just the the big impact that he could have on this team being healthy, being able to compete and contribute. What does that mean to you right now at this point training? >> Um it keeps me motivated. You know what I mean? and it keeps me motivated just to see that they look at me in that way and just to be able to know that I have the skill set that they're looking for to help this team out as well. I just want to help this team out any way that I can. Whether it's defense, whether it's special teams, either way, I just want to be able to help this team get to where we want to be. >> Anyone else? >> CJ, >> how is CJ kind of living vicariously through you guys right now? I mean, he had to miss a little time at the beginning and now lately, like, how has he stayed engaged behind the scenes? Yeah, I'd say the biggest thing is on the sideline. He's always asking what the call is. Um staying present, repeating the call and you know the signals on the sideline. So I'd say that's the biggest thing, you know, and being encouraging as well. You know, tough to be injured during camp, you know, on the field for him once get back on the field. So hopefully, you know, comes here soon, especially when CJ's been healthy. We've seen a bunch of rotation. I think maybe six of you guys have gotten first team reps. What has the the competition and the the camaraderie been like in that room with all you guys fighting for time? It's honestly been pretty dang good. Um, obviously everyone knows this is our job now and everyone wants to start. Um, you know, to provide for their families, you know, so it's deep, man. It's a lot of competition, but that's why you play this game. Um, is to compete with one another. And, you know, with that also comes a brotherhood. We're up here 24/7 preparing, working hard. So, um, I like where we're at right now as a squad. And, you know, it's the brotherhood we can do. >> How does that competition bring out the best in you? It it makes me, you know, have to compete every single day. You know, like coach Lanning used to say to me at Oregon, rent's due every day. Um, you know, in this league, you know, I haven't played one preseason game, but it's pretty evident that rent is due every single day. Um, you know, there's no days off, especially when you're competing for a startup team. >> Bryce, how does the physicality set a tone for the whole defense, you know, when you make a play like that? >> Yeah. Um, I think it runs through us. Energy and effort is the linebacker's job along with communication. Um, so you know that's kind of what I've you know prided myself in my whole whole career is you know being that Energizer battery whether it's a big hit or you know encouraging teammates. You know the other night I came in terms of a big hit which was pretty dang sweet and fired me up. Um, you know I'm just there to do my job for the team. >> There was a series on Thursday where you Austin and and Jaylen made plays each one after another to end a drive and I think force a punt. What does that do for your guys' room when it's all linebackers making the plays to do it? >> It's awesome. you know, it, you know, that hard work is shown off on the field when it matters most, which is great. And like I said too, you know, it runs the defense runs through the linebackers. I feel like, you know, we set the tone whether that's positive or negative. Um, you know, we take accountability for all of it. Um, kind of like quarterback defense. So, it's awesome when we perform that way. >> What it feel like to just play all this like talk about prepping for it and training camp, but just play a game and actually be able to build off of a game. >> Oh, it was so much fun, man. You know, practice is football's fun. Practice is fun, but when you hit the same people for, you know, long enough, it gets a little old. So once you get out on the field in front of some fans, it's, you know, there's nothing like it. You know, didn't have spring ball cuz we're in college this year, so actually being able to play a real game was awesome. A lot of fun. Thanks Bryce.

title: Sean McVay, Ty Simpson & Dean Connors Recap the Rams' 20-12 Preseason Win Against the Chiefs
text: Okay. Um, you know, I thought, uh, today was really cool to see so many guys step up, take advantage of their opportunities. Um, I thought really I thought the coaches did a really good job putting guys in good spots. I thought Nate called a really good game. I thought both GIF and Joe did an excellent job calling a good game as well getting the operation. Thought we were fairly clean, minimized a lot of the penalties and, you know, guys that the style of play was there. Um, really I thought, you know, Stson did a nice job with the two series. We had the first series where, you know, they got their big dogs in there and um we end up having to punt, but I thought he came in, did a nice job of orchestrating a nice drive on the second series. And then I thought Tai had great command all day. He was able to get through good progressions, got a lot of different guys involved. I thought, you know, he and Nate were really in sync. Uh were able to move the launch point. I thought the line did a really good job, especially in some of those later drives that ended up leading to touchdowns. Um where he had good production where he was able to get through some progressions. Um, and that the one sequence where we got the defensive stop, have a big return by Xavier Smith, and then ultimately were able to hit Dean Connors on the screen. I thought that was kind of the momentum flip of the game. But man, it was really cool to be able to see so many guys step up and do a nice job and excited for them. >> Settle in the way Tai did and started getting better. Yeah. >> More confident, driving the ball a little more downfield. What does that tell you about him? Um, and in terms of the moment not being big too big for him and then also just settling >> I think all of those things that you really just asked with the question Vinnie kind of answers it itself where he really settled in did a great job. I think it's a tremendous credit to you know just the way that he's worked you know Dave Ron does such a great job with that room as a whole um and obviously Matthew's leadership and and I thought Nate really did a nice job of putting him in a lot of good spots that accentuate his skill sets but the other 10 guys around him were able to do their job. we were able to kind of sustain, get some first downs, be efficient on early downs that allows some other stuff and you kind of have that, you know, good balance and and Nate stayed aggressive on the early downs which gave Tai an opportunity to deliver and he did that. But, uh, very pleased with him and it's a real credit to a lot of good work and whether today went really great or whether it was a, you know, a great learning opportunity, we continue to move forward, but I thought it was a great step in the right direction for him. Very happy for him. that there's a decision made that's officially been made on a back quarter quarterback. But does this change anything? >> We we continue to evaluate you know I I think you know I think really you have to be considerate of what kind of situations were stats was he placed in and I thought with the circumstances that he was placed in he did a nice job with those parameters. Um obviously Tai had the majority of the game got 25 attempts to be able to throw the football uh but I thought he did a really good job you know overall and I thought Stson with what he had. So, we're going to continue to evaluate it like anything else, but it was fun to be able to see uh, you know, live football, see how guys handled it. We haven't played tackle football in a long time. I mean, shoot, I got to get my I was a little uh rusty myself. I went and started to shower before I came in here. You know, normally I for I was like, "Oh, shoot. I forgot I got to do the press conference." So, uh, it was awesome, though. And really, it's cool to be able to kind of step back and appreciate how many great people that I'm surrounded with with our coaching staff. I thought Bubba and Kyle did a great job with special teams. U you know, Smash Ball with just the communication from up top situationally is awesome and um it was great to be able to get back out here and ultimately just be a good cheerleader for these guys today. >> Max player was reliable throughout the whole >> just that Stu, you know, he had a bunch of catches, had a bunch at the end of the first half and kind of that twominute and um you know, but I thought he did a really good job. He's getting a lot of work right now. Scooter Huff does an excellent job with that room as a whole. It was cool for Valari to be able to get that return on the onside kick at the end of the game, but uh Max did a really nice job. It was a good step for him. >> You know what he told me? He felt his hamstring on the first uh field goal protection. So, he was pretty bummed. I'm hopeful that he'll be okay, Gary, but don't have any updates. He'll get a scan. We'll see. Um but I was bummed out for him for that to have happened. And I think Mario Williams got a hamstring on his kick return. Those were the only guys that I know, you know, got something in the game and didn't return. That can come to mind. Anybody else come to mind for you, artist? Yeah, those are the only guys that come to mind. So hopefully they'll be all right. I hate that part of it. >> Going back to Ty for just a second, what did you like in particular about um you know, the way he picked picked and chose the spots as far as when to push the ball downfield versus taking? >> I thought he took what the defense gave him. You know, I thought he read the plays out, read with his feet. You know, I I thought he did a really good job overall and and I thought even on some of the keepers where maybe the primary isn't there, he attacks with the ball up, you know, even on the first one that he had where he ends up finding Max Clair on kind of the late down flat, but hit a couple low crossing routes. Um, you know, and I thought he kept the ball in play, you know, that's the biggest thing is keeping the ball in play. Um, there was one situation that we'll have a great learning op on a third down where, you know, they kind of play a man coverage. We ended up throwing it to the flat to Max Clare. I gotta see. I think the pocket might have allowed him to be able to progress, but otherwise it was a really good day for him. He just felt like he was in good command and it was cool to see a good smile on his face. >> There was a high snap that he kind of made a pretty nice play on make sure that it didn't turn into a bad play. >> That's what I said. I said way to not make a bad play worse. You know, I couldn't exactly see where that hit him, but it was the first third down that he's in. That was right before he had hit a good job, you know, finding Max Cla on that keeper that I was kind of just mentioning. But, um, sometimes the best play is being able to just throw it away and get and bring the kicking unit on to be able to punt it away. And I thought, you know, that was a good illustration. Um, I thought, you know, he was I thought he made good smart decisions. You know, we always talk about decision, timing, and accuracy, and I thought that was on display. And, and I think the protection allowed him to be able to get through progressions. You know, even on a quick game that we had, he got across the board, found Dean Connors for a good checkdown that Dean ended up having a good catch and run. Then on one, we had a front side combination. and he progressed to be able to hit CJ Daniels on an incut, ended up hitting BP on kind of a crossing route on a three-level throw off the play action. So, there was a lot of really good illustrations of him just being able to play the play and be able to execute it. Um, you know, the way that Dave and and the other guys are coaching him to be able to do it. >> Tell them what Dean showed you. >> I, you know, Dean showed me that, you know, it certainly isn't too big for him. You felt him out there today. You know, I think sometimes that's one of the positives that I could say is you just feel somebody make their presence whether that's a defense or an offensive guy. But, you know, when he got the ball, there was a change of pace and, you know, you felt like, okay, this guy's got a chance to be able to create. Thought he did that in the run game and then obviously um really cool. It was great blocking on the screen that he scored on, but it was a great job by him to be able to set those blocks and then a great job by him on the touchdown catch. Um it was a good good job by him kind of being able to recognize the defender overran it be able to take the end cut on a little option route that we had and um really happy for Dean. It was it's these are fun to see these men, you know, all these guys make a lot of plays that don't get a ton of opportunities in practice and man, it's fun to celebrate them. >> Yep. >> But you guys are getting closer. >> Yeah. >> Do you anticipate? >> You know what? Here's what I would say. It's it's really we've had great dialogue. it's going to be on his timeline, you know, and and when he feels good about having clarity, whether that's a yes or whether that ends up being a no, we've had some tentative discussions behind the scenes, there's a lot of stuff without getting too granular with it. And just out of respect for, you know, the dialogue that he and I have that I do think he's earned the right, I think our guys are doing a great job of focusing on what they can control and that's our, you know, that's our current team as it stands right now. if Aaron does decide he wants to do it, I've been very open that we want to try to be able to explore that opportunity. Um, but I think he has kind of earned the right to be able to say like he knows himself in terms of am I able to stack backto-back days? Am I able to do some of the different things and some of those benchmarks that he set out for himself? Um, and what I don't want to sit here and do is is put a timeline on it and then something comes up where I've got to kind of push it back. What I have said with him, we have some loose things where we've identified, you know, dates that we'd like to be able to hit, but what I don't want to have is any sort of unnecessary pressure on him if there's some unforeseen circumstances. Um, I feel great about our football team as it currently stands, and I know he'll add value if he decides to come. And so, if he's put himself in a position to be able to say yes or no, I think he's earned the right to have clarity on that. We're not at that point quite yet. And um you know I'm hopeful that it'll be sooner than later, but I also want to respect you know when he does feel like that clarity will come. And I think there's a chance that we'll be closer to that than than not. But again, I don't want to I don't want to say too much or put some sort of invisible deadline on something that doesn't exist in my mind for him. >> Okay. Thanks, guys. >> How are you all? Uh, it felt great. Felt great. >> Felt like you got I mean, understandably so, it's your first NFL game. Uh, felt like you got comfortable as the game went on. Did you Did you Is that how you >> Yeah, no doubt. Um, I definitely felt more comfortable than I ever had um in a game. Um, but, you know, I also didn't know what to expect. Uh, first NFL game, first live NFL, you know, against NFL teams. Um but once that first drive kind of you know got done with I was like all right like yeah this is just like playing in the backyard in Martin. Um but you know guys did a great job. So happy for our team. Um and you know on to next week. >> What did you know going in you were going to go in the third series or what was what was the plan? >> Yeah. Um, I knew pretty quickly that I was going to go in. Um, you know, they, uh, communicated that with us. Um, me and Stson. Um, and, uh, you know, I just was making sure that I was ready to go at all times. >> There's a great infrastructure around here and, uh, it kind of leads to a quarterback friendly type of a system. I think you would agree with that probably. Do you feel that in the game like when the plays when when those plays are coming in and the type of plays that you guys are running that this is perfect? >> Absolutely. Um, you know, it starts from the top, starts with Shawn. Um, you know, Nate and the offensive staff did a great job. Um, but you know, also credit to the guys of understanding our game plan. Um, understanding where our lineup um and you know, kind of our uh our um, you know, separators as we can call it there on offense. Um, you know, how we can separate from the other team. Um, and they, you know, hit them hit them all all in the head. Uh, and you know, that was our, you know, big thing going into the game of just hitting our separators. Um, and I think we, you know, did a really good job in that and that's what kind of, you know, led us to, you know, get points on the board. >> That play early snap was high and to your right. You kind of >> did make a bad play worse, but can you take us through kind of what happened on [snorts] that play and what your thinking was? >> Uh, yeah. Um, you know, we had a pass play called of course. Um, but you know, it was a high and hot snap. Um, and you know, just kind of, you know, got to handle the down. Um, you know, last thing you want to do is try to, you know, do too much and turn the ball over and get points for the other team. Um, you know, we have a great punter in Ethan Evans and a great, you know, special teams unit. Um, and our defense was playing great. So, hey, just throw it out of bounds, punt the ball. Any any drive that ends at a kick is a, you know, good drive. So, that's what, you know, I kind of take into the game. >> You have any family members here today? >> Yeah. Uh, made the trip. >> Yeah. So, my mom and my dad made it. My brother made it. Um, one of my dad's former players made it who, uh, who's a, you know, really tight family member me member of ours. Um, I had a uh uh my dad's um strength assistant fly him here. Um, so it was it was really cool. Uh, I saw him, you know, when I was in pregame. Uh, they were young like crazy. Uh, I I waved at him. Um, and so I'm excited to go see him after. >> Did Did your dad uh when the schedule came out realiz >> Oh, yeah. He >> He finesses the situation for sure. I I hate it for the guys at UT Martin. Um but uh um I appreciate the um the sacrifice that he him and the guys do for me. >> What were the conversations like with family before they got here? Like do they have a sense that maybe you would play as much as you did today or were you just kind of off to them that you like I don't know? >> Yeah. No, I I knew I was going to play and I told them I was like hey like I'm going to play um you know a good good portion of the game. Um and you know my dad just talked to me like I was you know four years old again. just, you know, hey, just, um, you know, catch every snap, make the easy ones easy, and go do what you love. Um, and I love you. Um, he sends me a Bible verse every day, uh, every time. Um, and just a quote, um, to give glory back to him. Um, and it's it was just really cool, you know, it's something I felt calm, felt really comfortable, uh, and, you know, especially when I have family members texting me, it's a it's a comforting feeling. >> It seems like you had a good connection with Max Claire today. You explain kind of how that evolved through the game. Um, you know, well, one, I try to get the best players the ball. Uh, and Max is a really good player. Um, and that's why I try to, you know, get the ball out as quick as I can because I know we got a bunch of playmakers. Um, but it was just kind of the situation that happened. Um, you know, Max is a hot hand there. Uh, he he's really worked really hard. Um, you know, especially during camp. Uh, you know, going with, you know, a bunch of the bunch of the offenses. Um, and just, you know, trying to take what the defense gives me. Uh, you know, a lot of times, you know, Max Max does a really good job with his routes. Um, and that's kind of, you know, how it happened really. >> As you said, you knew you were going to play a lot today and hopefully that continues the rest of this preseason, but at some point that picture is going to change a little bit. Um, for obvious reasons because again with Matthew being the starter, how do you compartmentalize that and how do you um do you then approach that whatever the role is going to be moving forward? >> Yeah, my mindset doesn't change at all. Um, I'm still going to, you know, try to prepare like I'm going to play um because you never know what happens. Um, I say that all the time. uh you know just because of you know past experiences with me. Um and you know if anything right like I'm trying to soak up as much knowledge as I can um and what better guy to do it from than you know Matthew. Uh so you know I'm going to try to prepare as best I can um and make sure you know I ask you know all all the questions that I need to to go in there and have confidence because you know if his helmet snaps off or something happens right I got to go in there execute and make sure that our offense doesn't you know take a dip. >> Sean said that they're still [snorts] evaluating the backup role. Do you feel like you are in competition with Stephen for that or do you feel like he's kind of the front runner? >> Yeah. Um, you know, I don't really don't get into that honestly. Uh, I'd really just try to, you know, be the best version of myself I can be, uh, and, you know, compete with myself. You know, a lot of the times I get, you know, people get caught up in, you know, who's better than who and, you know, who who is, you know, going to get this spot and stuff, but at the end of the day, right, like, you know, I'm just trying to, you know, prepare me for the future. um and try to, you know, be sack days and, you know, be progressive and h have progress. So, you know, that's not up to me. That's, you know, a headman decision and, you know, executive decision. Um, but I just know that, you know, I'm happy to be here. Uh, and I'm, you know, working and going to make sure that, you know, I do anything the team needs me to do. >> You guys executed a really great good screen pass for that touchdown. >> How how big was that just just for you to maybe settle down a little bit or just get that thing out of the way? >> Uh, yeah, it was huge. Um, you know, one, it got us, uh, you know, points on the board. So, that's very important. But, you know, what was really cool is that, um, you know, a lot of people don't, you know, really understand, but, like, you know, the guys up front did a really good job. Um, you know, Dylan going out there, uh, and, you know, taking two people out so Dean can hit it up in the hole and, uh, and score. Um, and a great play call by Nate in the red zone where, you know, people don't really expect a screen. Um, it just was allaround great job. Um, and started with the guys up front. Literally, all I did was flick the ball out there. Um but you know it wouldn't have happened without a you know collaborative effort. >> Awesome. Thank you again. >> How did it feel to contribute the way you did today? You know just with the touch catch catches you had and just being out there overall >> felt great. Uh anytime you can help the team it's good feeling and dream come true for someone who you wanted to play in the National Football League. So, just got to keep stacking days and go one day at a time. >> What have you seen from, you know, Tai over, you know, the course of training camp? And, um, you know, just what was it like, you know, connecting with him in particular on those touch? >> Yeah, he work he works hard. You know, I I try to be one of those guys who gets in first and he beats me every time. So, you know, he's he lives in the facility. He's always learning and, you know, trying to absorb as much as he can and you can really see it and he's gotten better. Um, and he's only going to continue to do that. So, it's really inspiring to see someone, you know, who has the ability to not do that, could sit back and relax, but, you know, he he presses the gas and works really hard. And, you know, I'm proud of him and and the way he played. >> Those are two different kinds of touchdowns. One is a screen pass that generally goes to a running back. The other's a crosser in the end. Which one did you like better and which one do you I mean, was cooler to you? >> I don't know if either one was cooler. I thought uh you know we had a heck of a block on the screen by the O line. So I think overall as a football player that was pretty good just to see the fellas get out there and run and you know you know sometimes you don't get to see those big boys run but when you watch screens like that you do and uh you know I wouldn't have done it without them. >> But when you can uh the other touchdown where where it was kind of a wide receiver type of a play just to be able to show that kind of versatility I'm sure pretty >> Yeah, it felt great. You know, I uh try and take pride in being versatile and you know, number one's blocking and you know, running comes next and receiving might be a little dash in there. So, it's always fun. >> You're part of a very key running back group. Um when you're out there, of course, you want to help the Rams win, but you also conscious that you're putting stuff on tape for possibly other teams as well. >> Yeah, I'm I'm trying to be the best Ram I can right now. And we got great guys who who try and make us better. Kron and Blake and Ronnie, those guys help so much and, you know, share so much wisdom to us and, you know, I'm just trying to become a better football player, you know, and then when I can control that, you know, whatever happens happens. So, >> thanks. >> Appreciate it. Thanks. Appreciate it.

title: Aireontae Ersery on Facing Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter Every Day | Full Q&A
text: All right, guys. >> Year two, for you, what are kind of your expectations and what have you kind of felt throughout the course of training camp so far? >> Yeah, I would say for myself, my expectations are always high. You know, just trying to come out each and every day uh and find that one little thing to get better and better at. Um, and like I said before, you know, what better two guys to go against every day, you know, Will and Denil. So, uh, I look forward to the challenge every day. So, just focus on getting better with the technique. >> How big of a resources trend for you and your growth? >> Uh, he's crucial, man. You know, a guy that's seen it all, done it all, been one of the highest paid tackles, you know, he got a real real uh real vet presence, you know. Uh, I always make a joke, call him a master, master sensei because he always stands like this, you know, with his hands behind his back. But, uh, you know, good guy, you know, a good vet to be around and I'm I'm glad that he's here. >> What challenge does Denil specifically provide versus Will? What are some like the differences the way they challenge you? >> Um, Denil, you know, more so he he just he got a lot of different moves, you know, like I said, he got he he is another vet. has been in the league for a long time. So, like I said, he just seen the best of the best uh during his career. And, you know, Will's uh another upandcomer hall of famer, you know, uh great player, great leader, you know, very twitchy, got power, too. So, um he's the other guy I look forward to going to against every day. >> Have you started thinking about going up against Max Crosby coming up in in joint practice? >> Yeah, we already started uh game plan towards that way. Um definitely looking forward to the joint practice to go against somebody somebody else. >> What's it been like having Wyatt next to you on the offensive line? Veteran presence and played a whole lot of football. What can that stability there do for you with him over there? >> Yeah, man. He he's like a a life jacket, you know. Um you know, he he always mentions and says, you know, I got your back. You know, whatever you need, whatever whatever call you call, we go with it and go at 100 miles per hour. you know, we make a make a mistake, we make a mistake together. So, uh, just having a guy like that, you know, Sevet, um, played at a high high level, had high success. Um, just add adds more to the role. >> What have been your early impressions of Ke, you were a rookie just a year ago. Yeah. What have you kind of made of him and his first action here with you guys? >> I like I love the guy, man. I think that uh he definitely came here. He's, you know, a tone setter, um, a difference maker, you know, a guy that you want at left guard, a guy that you want on your O line. Um, love his mentality and I think he got, you know, a bright future ahead of him. >> Last one, Michael. >> What's the biggest difference for you in just the way you're feeling in this training camp? Was it a whirlwind last year comparatively? How do you compare those two years? >> I think uh the heat is probably the biggest battle for real. For real. uh you just got to find ways to, you know, just get through it. You know, it's going it's going to be tough. It's going to happen. So, um and then more so just playing for each other, you know, um knowing there's other guys on the team that's going through the same thing you're going through. So, it's all good. All right, guys. title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media after preseason #MIAvsWAS | Miami Dolphins
text: What was it like to have that opening drive and how did you feel about the offense and what did you think of the offense? >> Yeah, um I love the way our team came out, offense, defense, um especially in a tough situation cuz we were backed up. I thought Bobby had an unbelievable plan coming in. I thought they executed at a high level. The The protection was good. We could run the ball. Um Malik was throwing the ball on time. He was accurate. I mean, that was an awesome drive to watch. Really proud of those guys. Um again, credit to the O line, the wide outs, the tight ends, Malik, really really pleased with the way they started and we got to build on it. And I also thought I thought Bobby did a really good job. >> What did you think of Keilan Douglas' one-handed catch and fighting for the yard? >> I probably haven't seen it on replay like you guys have, but it was pretty incredible and I look forward to watching it on tape. >> What did you What, if anything, specifically stood out No, it was just one drive, but about Malik tonight? >> Um kind of kind of what I had seen in the past, extremely composed, uh very accurate, um just the leadership in the huddle. And then it was also, let's give credit to those guys around him. I thought I thought our O line did a really nice job. I thought the protection was good. I thought the ability to run the ball with ATN early, it was looked like five or six yards plus a carry. That opens up the pass game. So, when you can run it, you can throw it. Then Malik kind of got outside the pocket a few times. Um very clean, very very clean. And that's a really really good first step, um with with obviously a lot to build on. >> What was it like to be a head coach on the sideline for the first time? >> Um you know, it's not about me. I mean, this was about our team tonight and and coming out and a lot of guys having a lot of opportunities to play. I mean, what's cool about the preseason games is we talked about the fast start, really on both sides of the ball. I thought the defense, not just early, I thought the defense came out really hot. We got some pressure on the quarterback. Um we stopped the run, we forced a punt. Then we hit a little bit of a lull, but then it was really cool to see the defense. I think they had six straight stops in the second half and then the sudden change field goal, which was really impressive. Um you know, Shawn [clears throat] called a lot of that and I thought he did a really nice job. And I just give the guys credit for continuing continuing to fight. Um once the headset's on for me, I'm just I'm just coaching football and enjoying being out there with the guys. >> With Chris Johnson, uh we didn't see him participating in the joint practice, but then he plays in the game. Can you tell us what was the situation there? >> Yeah, he had a minor injury where we were just being precautionary and we gave him that day to rest it. Um healed up and we felt confident that he could go on and and get a limited amount of snaps today. But he's good now. Just you know, we were just making sure. >> How did you feel like he performed? >> Yeah, without really watching the tape, you know, I I think there was a dig, which was a tough down for him since it was a condensed split and he probably was outside leverage if I have to replay it in my head just seeing it live. Tough down for him. But then I love the way he responded. Um he made two plays. He had a really really good break on a pivot route in the end zone that was a tough down to put him in and you know, he got his hand on the ball and um that was a big stop for us down there. >> Was that Jordan Brooks just a rest situation? Is he dealing with >> He's dealing with something minor where we felt it was important to um give him the day off. Um you know, we have a lot of time left in the preseason and we just want to be careful there. >> After the first team offense, second and third team struggled today. Um what went wrong for for Quentin Harris, Cam Miller and the rest of the >> Yeah, I think the big thing is again, I mean, I just I got to watch the tape, right? We'll watch it on the plane, we'll watch it tomorrow. Um and and we'll see um what the reads were, what the protection was like. I know there was there was a couple really nice throws that, you know, we got to come down with. And then we had some guys open. Again, I thought I thought Bobby did a good job and you know, I think when we watch this tape, we'll see that there were plays to be made. Um and we just we we got to obviously coach it better and we got to detail it and we got to make those plays when we can. >> What's going He's had a interesting camp. How do you get him to continue to play being confident? >> Keep coaching him. Keep believing in him. Um You're going to go through hard days. You're going to go through hard weeks. You're going to go through hard seasons. I'm not going to change the way I coach these guys and you know, put your arm around him when he needs him. Push it push him when he needs him. Um and all the above. So, we got to get back, watch the tape and and and we have work to do. >> Marco Wilson comes up with an interception and he's playing for his hometown team, so I'm sure he's really passionate about that. Um but what's his camp been like? >> He's had a good camp. Um was really happy to see him make that play. I know that he was really excited. You could see he was pretty cool. All the guys were excited for him, but to make a play down there on that side of the field, it's those usually help you change the game. So, really happy for him. >> I know you said Shawn called some plays. Did What was it like for you to call some plays from the sideline for the >> Yeah. Um I called the first two series. Um I wanted to make sure that both linebackers heard my voice. Um different than being in the booth, for sure. Um but once we got going, it was, you know, I got a great eyes up there from the assistants and Shawn's up there and we got a bunch of other coaches up there, but once once it got going, it it was it was comfortable. Um preseason's good for coaches, too, though. You know, we all had our fair share of mistakes during the game and and we need to coach better and certainly I do myself, as well. >> Is the seven carries in a preseason quarter for A.J. kind of a precursor >> No, it's sort of a precursor of what we can expect on A.J. this year. >> We'll see. I did I hope everybody realizes and listen to the tone in my voice when I said H A was going to get 40 plus carries. I guess I just have to be more careful, but sometimes I like to joke around a little bit, too, and some people really believe that. They can believe that, but seven carries, he did a really good job. I was proud of him, and I was proud of the O line the way they blocked. >> I was watching that JB on the sideline, Jordan Brooks, of course, well, one one series, and he was almost on the field with the way he was attentively watching the backup defenders. First guy to greet them coming off. What does that say about him? >> He's a pro, and that's why you want him around, and that's what all our players need to do. The one thing I was really really happy is because even when I stopped calling it, and I just I got into like I was helping, obviously, coach the game, but then I was observing a lot, and I was watching a lot, and I noticed that, too. And I noticed no one was sitting on the bench. Like guys that weren't in were up, and they were talking, they were going over the calls, they were really excited for their teammates, and they stayed locked in the game. I think that says a lot about the players that we have on this team, cuz I've been places where, you know, guys that are out are kind of chilling on the bench, and it wasn't like that. it was really cool to see the connection some of these guys are making, and, you know, they were rooting for each other, and that's important, cuz, you know, some of these guys are fighting for jobs. Some of these guys are fighting for jobs on our team. Some of these guys are fighting for jobs around the league, and we were we owe it to them to do everything in our power to have them have success, and our players need to help them as well. >> When you said you have to watch the tape, just in terms of vibe that you've got from the rookie class, obviously, it was kind of the first time under the lights, and there's a lot of them. What did you How did you feel? What kind of vibe did you get from the rookies? >> Yeah, I think for some of them it they had anxiety, you know, and I knew they would. It's why you keep doing these. It's why you have the joint practice. It's why you have preseason games. It's why you play those guys. Some of them, instead of trusting their eyes and where they're supposed to be, They just kind of got big eyes and when they're supposed to stay outside they jumped inside. When they're supposed to line up on the left they might So there's some stuff that some of them got to, you know, see this and do it again and then see it and do it again. And I think it's going to be a process with those guys. We need to We need to They need to play. Um and there's no substitute for that and we need to play them. There's some of the guys that it wasn't too big for and I'm excited to watch that but I think going through this together as a team will help, you know. >> How How would you evaluate how Cameron Dillard is playing in practices uh training camp? >> Um he's a guy that I think he's strained. He's giving great effort. He's made some splash plays and you know, he did some good things out there again today. Um you know, I'll dive more into the details. Hard from the sidelines to really hone in on the certain players. You know, a lot of what I'm looking at there is big picture and then you get the iPad and try to figure out what happened with what you want to call what went wrong and I mean, up in the booth I probably could answer all your questions a lot better. That's like playing a video game but down on the field it's more open up my vision and so we'll see but I'm proud of the way the defensive guys strained and I can't emphasize that enough and I think there's needs to be a lot to say about that, right? We challenged them when we didn't play the run well in the end of the second quarter which was disappointing, right? The pile started going backward which that's not good with me. We came in, we challenged them and like I said, I mean, they didn't think they punted six straight times or they kicked the field goal on the sixth possession. It was a sudden change and I'm I'm just proud of the fight with that from the D-line. We had guys we had ends playing inside. We had guys playing everywhere. We had some guys going down but there was a ton of fight from the defense and I'm I'm proud of those guys. >> Mhm.
