And do you have any other sports that you played that kind of help in those situations? >> Um I've been Uh yeah, the so obviously being in the red zone uh just you know, playing football Obviously, this is a game I've been playing a long time. And yeah, and obviously this takes work, so I have worked on this a ton. And uh Yeah, in the end I'm just going out there playing fast, playing physical, and just making sure I put the team in a better position. Of very important. Very important. Um you know, the Philadelphia Eagles is really good football team offensively and defensively. You know, I've gone I've gone against the team, you know, quite some time now. So, I understand the energy that they bring. And I know when it comes down to it, we'll be ready to handle them, so. Um I mean, I speak for the unit. I wouldn't really speak for myself because again, this game takes all 11. It's not just one person. And um like I said I just I appreciate the unit, and I look forward to going to battle each and every day with the dudes, so. Yep, appreciate you guys. What's up? How y'all doing? >> Long time, man. >> It's been a minute. >> Yeah, how'd it feel just being back out there? >> It felt It felt good to get back out there, for sure. Obviously, when you take 2 weeks off, it's like, you know what I'm saying? You got to get back into it. You got to catch the flow of things. You got to get your legs back up under you. So, I'm going through that process, but it felt great to get back out there and you know, compete. Uh he's a great receiver, man. He's got strong hands, quick, quick feet, quick releases. He's going to be a great player for us this year. Uh I mean, yeah. I had a I had a little hammy and just had to rehab it and get back out there. I mean, yeah. It's always good to have the technology to be able to keep up with what's going on and I get the virtual learning going on. Uh so, yeah. I did a lot of that and a lot of rehabbing. No. I mean, this year not for me. I just need to practice. That's all I really need to do it. Get the reps. Oh, yeah. It's going to be a really important week. Uh a lot of momentum going into it. It's a good team coming in here. Um and you know, it's going to be a lot of great competition between us. So, I'm excited for that and those are the type of practices that you need to you know, go out there and compete and I get ready for the season. I don't know. I don't I don't see it like that. Our number two and number one, I feel like when you at corner, um you know, you playing to the best of your abilities and you playing whoever you're in front of depending on the call or the scheme. Um you know, you got to do your job cuz at corner there's nobody saving you. So, like I feel like at corner you got to be able to do your job and uh that's it, for real. I'm not really worried about who I'm sticking. I'm just trying to, you know, stick the guy and play good defense. >> Follow up. Sorry, as as Christian's or you know, kind of drags on, do you see it becoming a distraction >> Uh uh honestly, that has nothing to do with me. and uh you know, I feel like as long as we playing football, the rest and other outside things will take care of itself. I'm just really focused on uh trying to get better and uh getting back to practice. >> Something how do you look at this wide receiver group? >> Yeah. >> AJ Green >> It's a great group. A lot of competition, man. They got a lot of depth. A lot of depth. A lot of those guys could be starters uh anywhere. Uh so, we're lucky to have them on our team. >> From what you said at corner, there's no one there to receive it. Is that something that drew you to the position from a young age as you were coming up? Like that challenge? >> Yeah, I used to play safety in high school and uh it was it was boring. It was boring back there. Just kind of sitting back there. They put me at corner and I just felt the competition. It was like every down, you know, you never know when you're getting the ball or when that ball is going to come your way. You don't know what the offense is going to call that play call. So, uh I just had it's a lot more excitement playing corner. >> You talked about takeaways. You related a conversation that you guys are getting some of the defensive backs have with Kevin Byard. How about you being more getting your hands on the ball, being aggressive to the ball? Then we saw you guys get four takeaways in the >> Has Kevin's approach his leadership style, the way he's gone about his business because he's been so good at taking the ball away in his career >> Yeah, I I mean, you know, that's his individual career. I don't know how much he can Like he can give us leadership and talk about it, but at the end of the day, guys got to go out there and do their job and make the play like, you know, he can only be at one place at one time or you know, affect so many people. Uh so, you know, obviously his presence here, he's going to make his plays for sure. Um but it's going to be on us to, you know, follow his lead. Yeah. >> Carlton, I know you haven't been out here, but you know, this summer, what do you notice that might be different about this year's defense? I don't know. It's been my first day back out here. It seemed like we got a little bit more physical physicality. Uh and just more chemistry. For sure. >> Carlton, how would you gauge your comfort level in year two in this system? >> Yeah, I feel real comfortable. I feel real comfortable with the coaches, with the scheme, with um the organization. So, uh yeah, it's been a good uh start to the year two. All right. No problem. Thank you. What's going on? >> Lamondre, you look pretty uncoverable in a lot of these red zone drills where you're catching the football. Can you give us some insight into how much work you put in as a receiver throughout your career? Cuz it seems like you've done it pretty consistent. you know, I put in a lot of work. Uh you know, just uh you know, the more you can do uh in the NFL, that's the, you know, the better off you are. So, uh I've always been pretty good out the backfield, but the last couple years I put a real emphasis like in off season of running routes and, you know, getting comfortable uh catching the ball out the backfield. >> Lamondre, one of the things that you do well is your alignment versatility, Greg. They can pretty much line you up anywhere. And you can create a match up. Do you take pride in that in terms of having that type of versatility and adding it to this system? >> Yeah, of course. Of course. Especially with in Josh's system. Uh you know, he loves the running back out the backfield. And like you said, just creating mismatches on the linebackers and things like that. So, if I could do that uh on a consistent basis, that'll help uh me and, you know, the whole team. >> Now, he hasn't been here a while, but when Hassan walks into the room, you know, like what what strikes you about him as a player and you've seen him on the field a little bit? >> Uh he's a big guy. Uh he's a bigger running back. Uh you know, he he's smooth out there. Only seen him, you know, a couple couple plays and things like that, but I look forward to making a relationship with him. Uh yeah, he's a good guy though. Great great football player, too. >> How have you seen Traveon develop going into your two now during training camp? >> Uh yeah, he he's a sponge, man. Uh even coming in last year, he's just trying to learn as much as he can. He's doing a great job. Uh fantastic football player, super fast. Um and yeah, I'm just excited for him. Excited to see what he's going to do. >> What are some things you'd like to see him get better at? >> Uh I mean, I think he'll say it himself, just everything. The whole the whole facet of the game. >> Brace was telling us it's a big week. Um what's the message been about this week from him and the coaches about knowing you got six straight days in the field and some joint practices? >> Yeah, it's just a grind. Uh you know, we deep in the camp now. Uh it's going to feel like camp coming up. Uh we're going to get challenged by, you know, this next team coming in here. Uh and you know, I think it's just I think he just I think he just knows camp is like actually started now. Like we're we're in it. >> So, obviously, you're the leader of the running back room. In terms of of that and leading that group, you're now at a point in your career where you can be not just a player but a mentor as well. How much do you talk to these younger backs in particular like Jam? >> Yeah. About playing the position at this level. >> Yeah. Uh anytime they need anytime they need anything, I just remember, you know, having my vets to talk to. James White, Damien Harris, Brandon Bolden. So, I try to just mimic what they did for me. Uh you know, they made the game slow down for me quicker than I think it should have or, you know, running back it slows down for running back. So, I think just talking to the vets and stuff is it does a great deal and, you know, I'm here for them whenever. I try to answer their questions. Try to uh you know, make the game slow down for them. See tell them what I'm seeing. See how they're seeing and things like that. >> Is there anything that more recently, like last year this off season, has slowed down for you? I I say just reading defenses after the ball is snapped. Like I was I was pretty good at it like before the ball is snapped, but you know, getting better at it after the ball is snapped, that's a that's a huge thing. Uh just reading coverages and stuff like that and it could be it could it could help me out the backfield as well. >> With the joint practices, is there a benefit to knowing you're going against a team like oh the the Eagles before the joint practices? Like you're sort of familiar with them. >> Uh I mean yeah, I mean every day is different, every season is different, but uh yeah, we know how they practice. Uh they practice hard just like us. Uh and yeah, they're going to put their best foot forward every every every time we get out there. Mhm. >> How's the body feel? >> I feel I feel good. I actually feel good. >> Yeah? >> Yeah, I actually do. >> better than other years at this time? >> Honestly, I do. Uh and it's kind of just me taking care of my body more. Like yeah, just being more uh proactive about it and you know, just getting in that training room more than I ever have. >> So, how does that like what are you doing in there? >> A lot of things. I got a lot of things at my house, too. I got a big recovery room at my house. >> Okay. >> That that's new? >> Kind of. Like it's probably like a year old now. Uh-huh. Yes, sir. >> Good for you, man. >> Yeah, I appreciate it. Yeah. I appreciate y'all, yeah. >> Thank you. >> What's going on? >> It's good. I'm blessed, you know. Had a nice little preseason game, so I'm happy. >> How did it feel to kind of get out there, get your feet wet? >> Uh it felt good, you know, get the butterflies out, you know, get all the rust off and you know, get hit again. That's what feels good, you know, finally be able to get some contact. So, I'm happy for that. >> That feels good? >> Not really, but to get used to it again yeah, yeah, definitely does. >> How does it feel at this point uh where you are just sort of like mentally and like pace of the game versus where you were at this point a year ago? >> Um I mean for me, I feel like I just got my groove back, you know, just finally having fun. Um not really worried about what I can't control, you know, just so just maxing every opportunity that I get and you know, things have been working out for me, so I'm honestly grateful. >> So, we talked to after practice after the game and he said he couldn't wait to watch your shimmy shake, whatever you want to call it on the touchdown. >> Mhm. >> Is that just reactionary from you, or are you setting him up at various points and then >> Uh I mean, it's a mind game. You know, you set it up from the beginning and everything. You kind of know what's going to work, but it's also a little bit of reaction thing. You know, I could kind of when I the ball is snapped, I kind of understand what his technique and his leverage and then I'm able to make my move based off him. So, it's a little bit of both when you play in the game. >> How do you feel like the competition between the wide receivers and the DBs have been going this camp? It seems like it's like, you know, it's been fun to watch every single >> I mean, it's been back and forth. I mean, our motto is iron sharpens iron. So, when you going against great DBs with great receivers, I mean, it's always going to be a battle. So, I mean, it's been fun. You know, the com- the competition is really what makes this sport. So, without it we'll be a little bored. So, we got to have them, you know, fits going back and forth with each other. So, I enjoy it. >> When you watch Romeo on the field, it seems like he's kind of excelling at those high, you know, jump balls when he goes up. What are you seeing in those plays? >> I'm just seeing the dude float to the moon, for real. Honestly, I mean, it is it's so special to watch, you know, a guy that doesn't really talk too much, but his game does all the talking. So, for him to make those plays and his consistent, I mean, it's just it awes you, but at the same time it's those things that we expect to do in our receiver room. Uh in college, I really wasn't exposed to too many intermediate routes. So, now I'm getting that opportunity to do it. So, year one to year two, you know, it's definitely been night and day. Now, it's just, you know, that ball finding me across the middle and everything. So, I can really showcase what I've been working on. I mean, you give somebody with speed, you just find a way to give them the ball as fast as you can. So, yeah. Uh-huh. Uh I mean, it's been a little bit of both. I mean, I showed little sparks sparks of it, but it's something that I wasn't as consistent on as I am now. So, it's just like something that I keep working on. It's something that I really want to add to my game cuz I feel like that'll make me a complete receiver. A lot, man. Like, I have dreams about releases. You know what I'm saying? It's something that I just do in my sleep. So, I mean, man-to-man and off the line is something that I really pride myself on. I've been pride myself on that from the jump. You know, watching a lot of guys, Devante, Keenan, Doug, Baldwin, Stevie Johnson, like people like that that are really good off the line. I mean, I've always tried to model my game after that. It makes life a lot easier. Um, I don't really think there's any much challenges. I mean, they're all on the same page. We all got a good understanding, good chemistry. I mean, I think it just really prepares you for like certain moments when you know, things go out of left field, you got to replace somebody here. It's just like you already know what that person is coming with. So, it's really little to no expectation for them. I mean, they're two different people, you know, two different personalities. But, I mean, they just bringing that aura, you know, big play receivers, you know, definitely got a lot of game, a lot of knowledge. So, I mean, just a lot of wise, you know, older dudes. Uh, I mean, for me, like, it's just getting open is pretty easy. But, it's a lot of decision-making, you know? So, you got to be able to think on the fly and feel certain things. So, I mean, that's probably the biggest challenge, but I mean, it hasn't really come up for me for real. I mean, the week is important, but you know, you just take it day by day. You know, you just worry about what's in front of you right now. And then when those days come up with the joint practices, we're going to be ready and prepared. >> Speaking on that, it's your second year going through joint practices and preseason games. Is there anything you're taking away differently in this second year than you were as a rookie? that's a good one. I'll probably say for me it's just I'm coming out trying to kill. You know what I'm saying? I'm trying to come out and you know, prove a point, prove myself right. So, any chance I get to go against somebody opposite of my jersey color, I'm trying to make their day hell. >> Uh we saw you out there for the coin toss before the postgame. Can you give us some context as to how that decision was made? >> Say that again? >> We saw you out there for the coin toss before the postgame. Can you give us any insight into how that decision was made? >> Uh I mean, that was with the coaching staff. You know, I really don't know, but I'm grateful that I was able to be >> Thanks, guys. >> Thank you. Thank you. >> Thank you. Appreciate it. >> How you doing? >> What's up? What's up? >> How nice is it to make the play on Thursday and just sort of finally get used to playing football in the league? >> Oh yeah, sure. It felt good. Um just executing the defense and stuff like that. I was able to do my assignment and was able to make a play on the ball and stuff like that. So, uh it felt good to go out there and play some real football in the stadium in front of the fans. So, football is back. >> We've heard that takeaways or turnovers are kind of a message that's being emphasized in the uh DB room. Is that something that was kind of talked about um before this game? >> Oh yeah, for sure. It was talked about to us in sent in April when we reported for phase one and in phase two, just getting the ball, getting the ball, because at the end of the day, if you plus one, two, and three in a turnover margin, your your chances of winning is is extremely high. So, that's that's definitely something that we've been preaching since April. >> Mike Vrabel mentioned that you're very comfortable playing man coverage, but here trying to diversify your responsibilities. What's that process been like for you so far? >> Yeah, it's been a uh smooth transition. Uh I definitely feel like I'm a a man corner. I'd prefer to get my hands on it and stuff like that, but um it's good to be um diverse, you know what I mean? Switch it up, play zone, you You what I'm saying? Just give the um quarterback a different look. >> Do you feel Do you feel more comfortable in the defense than last week as well? >> Uh I I definitely do. I I feel like Count for I feel like I kind of started a little bit slow, just trying to get the defense under my hand and stuff like that. But now I'm getting more comfortable and comf- comfortable um each and every single day and I'm able to show it in practice and even in the games. >> You know, how big of a week is this coming up? Practice versus joint practices, how do you try to use those to your advantage and then preseason game number two? >> Yeah, yeah. I feel like anytime we um step out on the field, man, it's a big opportunity to put good stuff on film, whether it's a joint practice, game, or just practice against us. So, it's it's definitely going to be a a big week for not only me, but the team with the Eagles coming to town, um a good team that's been winning for the past few years under our Nick Sirianni and everything. >> I know you're professional and every rep counts, but does it light a fire under you a little bit when you get more opportunities with the ones? Cuz it seems like when you've gotten them, you've done a great job taking advantage. >> Yeah, yeah. Um I like to consider myself a starter, to be honest, you know what I mean? Like I um played in a lot of games in this league and a lot of meaningful games as well. Some was good, some was bad. So, just being able to have that experience, man, I feel like whenever the opportunity comes, like I'm I'm always ready. >> What do you say about the opportunity to work with a guy like Carlton Davis? >> Oh, yeah. Me and me and Carlton, we we go way back uh in Detroit, you know what I mean? Like we played together in we in Detroit. Um we had a great team there and everything like that. So, um me and Carlton, man, we we we we like this, man. So, that that's my guy. >> What's something you've been able to pick up from him over the course of the >> Um he's super smart, instinctive. I mean, just looking at him last year in in the playoff game, able to get two interceptions on C.J. Stroud and stuff like that. So, and and even when we was in Detroit, he did it. When we was in Detroit, two picks on the same guy. So, me and Carlton, very instinctive, very vision player. I mean, Super Bowl champ. I mean, the list goes on and on for him. >> Getting to going back to the turnover talk in April, I mean, how early was it and what specifically was the message? Cuz every defense, right, wants turnovers. But what was said here? >> Yeah, I mean, for like corner room, because I know I'm not sure, if I'm not mistaken, but I know the corners didn't have like a lot of picks last year, you know what I mean? So, um just a Booker, you know, I'm being a voice of the room. He just preaching and turnover, turnover, turnovers, you know, what I mean? Because at the end of the day, I mean, that's how we going to win games in this league. >> What can you say about the competition in the room? It feels like you've gotten reps with the ones, Iran's gotten reps with the ones. What can you just say about the >> Yeah, it's definitely a deep room. It kind of remind me of my second year in Detroit. We had Carlton, we had first round rookie, second round rookie, and me, Robinson, Emmanuel Moseley, myself, you know, I mean, Khaleel D'Orsay. Like list goes on and on. So, I definitely see a lot of similarities. I mean, we like six, seven deep, you know, what I mean? Even even Chan on a rookie free agency you like he's been amazing this whole camp. So, it it definitely helped. Makes you want to put your best thing on tape each and every single day. I mean, cuz the competition is is legit here right now. >> And as last one, receivers made a lot of big plays today. Does that in any way excite you or do you just walk off the field? >> Yeah, yeah, I mean, I'll be we got a a deep receiver room as well. I mean, Rome out here, I got he's seen coach Mazulla here today and he trying to play basketball and dunk and dunk on people right now. But, I mean, if the list goes on, I mean, Kyle Williams is amazing. I mean, AJ, I mean, it's definitely a group that's deep [cheering] skill positions, offense and defense. >> All right, thanks guys. >> Thanks, Khaleel. >> Khaleel, just some thoughts on your performance the other night. Obviously, the defense played really well. You guys had four picks. How would you assess how you did and the defense collectively? >> I feel like we did pretty good. We held them to seven points, you know, so we did pretty well out there. We forced a lot of turnovers. That's what the coaches harp on. So, it was great going out there forcing turnovers, you know. I feel like I did pretty good, executed my job. Had a couple plays which I could get back, but overall, I did pretty well. >> Coach Campbell said that he was talking to you to maybe practice a little bit harder. What was the message you got from him? >> Oh, man, it was real motivational for me cuz I came in here like halfway through the season and it was just like I didn't realize how hard they practice up here. And then, once he told me that, then I started going a lot harder to make sure to show them that I I belong here and belong in the state. >> When was that? When did he give you that message? >> Uh it was like the third week I was up here, so then it was like, "Okay, I'll show you that in practice." Like I could play way harder. And then he told me to like dial it back a little bit after that. So it was like just good to get that uh feedback and just build from it. >> How much better is it or how much better do you feel on this defense this year compared to when you came in midway through last year? >> Oh man, it feels amazing. Now and we got the second year with the guys, so like the coaches, so and they they know how to teach here. So it's amazing to just learn from them and uh just continue to build each and every day. >> John, can you just take us through your pick in the game? Just what did you see? >> Oh man, I just uh we got the call, you know, we see their formation lineup, and then uh I seen the quarterback drop back. And soon as I see the ball in the air, I just go get the ball. So that's all it was. Keep it simple. >> What were you doing in practice when Vrabel then said to scale back a little bit? >> Oh I was just doing my job to the best of my ability, you know. I was just trying to cause havoc out there cuz once he told me that I was like, "All right, I'll show you I can practice way harder." >> [laughter] >> How comfortable do you feel just playing in the box versus deep and just pretty versatile defense back? >> Yeah. Yeah, I feel pretty comfortable playing in the box. That's something I'mma continue to learn and keep getting better at, but I feel the most comfortable deep, like seeing the quarterback and so I could just go and get the ball, you know, that's really where I feel the most comfortable at. >> When when when it comes to that defensive backs room, you guys have a lot of talent there, a lot of experience as well. How does that benefit a young player like you? >> Oh man, it gives me great people to look up to and learn from. Like now we got Kevin Byard here and it's just great to learn from guys like him, Marcus Jones, Gonzo, uh CD, Carlton Davis. So it's amazing. They're great role models and they they really take us up under their wing and give us insight. Like Kevin Byard is like another coach out there, for real. He gives me a lot of helpful feedback. I'm thankful for it. >> How do you learn going against a wide receiver room that deep like like this team has? >> Oh man, you got to bring it every single rep cuz if it's the twos or the threes, we still got stars out there at receiver. So, that's something that it really makes the whole team better cuz every single rep, you got to be on your Ps and Qs and be in lockdown coverage cuz if you make a wrong step, like we got good quarterbacks, they going to put the ball on the money. So, you know, you got to bring it every rep. >> What was it like going up against Drake Maye every day in practice last year and how do you feel like that maybe helped you get better as a player? >> Oh, man, I was like so grateful for my development. It really helped me a lot just to see him every day and then I could like start to pick up on some of his tendencies. Like I started to try and study him cuz he's one of the best in the league. So, you know, it's just great to go against somebody like that and then keep seeing the offense every day. So, that feel like it really made me a lot better. >> Any tendencies you can share? >> Nah. >> You You played some quarterback in college, right? >> Yeah, for sure. >> Do you think those man coverage skills can still translate against tight ends? >> Yes, sir, for sure. I feel like that helps me a lot, especially with the tight ends who are faster. They remind me of the receivers. They were It's like the same thing cuz they just got to stay square, stay in front of them and all. >> Are you used to being in a system where safeties have so much responsibility, sometimes covering wide receivers, or is that new for you? >> No, I'm used to that, yeah. And it was the same in college pretty much, like you got to be able to cover, you got to be able to communicate, you got to be able to tackle, you got to be able to do everything the defense needs. Good. >> Anyone else? Thank you. >> Good, yeah. Appreciate y'all. You know what I'm saying?

text: Karen, I'm gonna pass on you today. >> Thank you. >> Good. Thank Thank God. >> Good. Riley, how are you? >> I like that dress. >> Do you want to ask a question? >> Riley, you're invited every single day. >> You sit right there. And >> Ben's going to be a few weeks, >> four to six, 8, 10, 12, even numbers, but it'll probably be extensive throughout the rest of the preseason for sure. And will we see any of the injured or physically unable players out there today, namely Christian? >> No, I don't think I would expect Christian. Or should you expect Christian? Uh, working hard. Um, you know, conditioning, you know, but won't won't be practicing. Not ready to get back out there and practice yet. Uh, Ellis may do a little bit. CD would be good to see um him come back. Woods I think will come back again. Just working through protocol, but hopefully he'll be back. He just had a few, I think, appointments here early as we speak. Um, let the PUP guys know. >> Sorry, we all know the contract thing going on. Are you guys on the same page right now? >> I thought Knox was going to ask the questions for you today, Ben. >> Well, then let's see. No, go ahead, Ben. >> Just we all know what's going on. Are you guys on the same page right now? Yeah, absolutely. And um I think that's the important thing. Talked about his professionalism, everybody else's. Um so this this isn't anything that you know it it it was something that happened in practice and I mean he's where he's supposed to be when he needs to be there. treatment, you know, working with Frank and doing those things and that yes, obviously I I that's my job is to be on the same page with with everybody here, players and coaches. Um, and I'm confident that that's what we're doing and everybody has a plan each and every day. >> The volume of this week with four practices and joints and the how do you maximize everything here? >> Well, it's going to look a little, you know, I mean, is Thursday to to Saturday uh Philly coming in. So today will be good work in a red zone two-minute um some situations. Tomorrow will be lighter and we'll come back and then whatever the fourth day is will be lighter and then we'll have two days of Philly. So I mean that's pretty good volume, you know. I mean four four padded practices, two two that we expect to to be really good intensity. I mean, I hope today is really good. If we can find a way to get down to the red zone and hopefully we can be better than we were last year defensively, we'll have to be much better. >> There's really no messages. we all understand, you know, that uh you know, we have um to be able to execute and um I'm confident just like I've always been in Andy that uh that he'll make them. And I was trying to, you know, we went for it a lot of times in those situations last year. And I just with preseason, uh, just trying to see to to be able to work some things and stress him and the the distance and, you know, we just whether we go for them or not, they just have to be ready to go and make those kicks. And, you know, just wanted to try to keep pushing the envelope. title: Saints DE Mike Heldman on two-sack performance in NFL debut against Jacksonville
text: Oh, yeah. That's the boy said my room there were like have a celebration. And I didn't want to like copy anyone's or do something just normal and like I literally thought of it last night. I was also like on Tik Tok before I go to bed just like a couple minutes and I saw some Marvel clips and I'm like that's kind of hard. So I just thought I'd follow that out. So yeah, that's just kind of how it came. So. >> Are you a Doctor Strange fan or is this just like you thought of it randomly? >> Uh it's really just kind of watching Marvel stuff and you know about Brian Burns and all the Spider-Man things. I can't do that. Um and I'm just like no one's ever hit the Doctor Strange. I'm like that'd be kind of cool. You know, I'm a big Marvel fan so it's just like you know pretty cool to hit that in game. So just had to go get the sacks first to do it. So. >> What about those? How did you How did you feel about your uh your >> Man, so like in our joint practice it wasn't my best day. And just kind of like in the league you just kind of got to grow from that and learn. And just coming into the game it was just like I've never had this much excitement going into a game before. Like you know, I had I felt a little bit more nervous in college. Like not like nervous nervous but it's just like I felt excited to get out here. And so it was just like kept hunting kept hunting. When I was ever my opportunity was to get out on the field just go hunt go hunt. And then I got there, you know what I'm saying? So it's just like it's cool to have those like first moments in the league like in the moment you're just in a football game and then when you're on the sidelines you're like wow, I'm in the NFL. Like it's it's super cool. And so you know, I'm just very happy about it and excited about it and you know, excited for the future games that we have. So. >> Um and you got like a a lot of snaps. Do you think that helped you get in a rhythm when you're doing that much playing time and >> Yeah, it it helps. It's nice. Um growing up it's just really taking advantage of the reps you get not counting the reps. And we had John Gordon come in. He's a writer of a great of a lot of great books. He's a good speaker too and he talked about being a hero which is like waiting for the moment to like for the clock to run down so you like the game can be done or be a warrior and just attack every second of the game, not worrying about when it's going in. And I can feel myself doing that in college sometimes and here I'm just like every moment just attack it. And so whenever the reps I had, whether that was on like kickoff, you know, I was I was waiting for my turn to get on special teams and I did. So excited for that. But you know, I just like playing defensive snaps, you know, it was just exciting to get out there and just attack every rep. Um you know, make it mean everything. Um cuz it you know, every play counts in football. So. Yeah, so you know, kind of attacking it we it's more of just like you kind of you know, if you don't have power in this game you you you can't really like get anywhere. You know, and I'm a big guy and like my philosophy is set things up, playing chess with the guy throughout the game. Um several times when I attacked him, um they're really good with like shooting like throwing your hands down when you get pressure and like you stand them up. That's why they like to throw your hands down. And I got like put down on the ground several times. I'm like, man, this is embarrassing. But like, you know what I'm saying? I I felt like I needed to adjust. And so like throughout the game I go when I instead of attacking power, it's show that I'm attacking power, but get off it quick, dip and rip, you know, rip, use my bend, get to the quarterback really. Um and it worked. And one of my TFLs too, like he came at me like super aggressively and I know if I attacked him and I tried to and I would have, you know, stood him up. But like I knew he would have tried to throw me down again. So really I took the liberty of going inside, making a play on the running back. And you know, that's a risk you take. There's a reward and if you don't make the tackle you might be called to sidelines. But you know what I'm saying? It's just really playing the game, you know, within the game, playing chess. And you know, sometimes you got to set up things and guys will We'll that and maybe you'll start out differently at different games. So, it's just really playing that chess match um on the field. >> Does but the confidence found or like that that excitement you're talking about, does that help you kind of take risks in the reality? >> Um I would say not really. It's just more of just like I'm excited to play the game. Um a little bit, but it's just more like even if maybe you're not having the best game or maybe like you are having a good game, but you don't find your like you just find yourself in like you know, got to keep going, got to keep going. It's really just still playing that game, you know, playing chess match with the guy in front of you and just, you know, understanding what they're going to do in that, you know, down and distance, where they are on the field. It's really just continuing to play the game. You know, your highs are your highs, get back to middle. Your lows your lows, get back to middle. It's really just staying in the middle every time and just really attacking it like, yeah. >> How did it feel taking those risks and risks and taking getting that reward and >> Man, it felt good. It felt really good. All the guys are getting hyped on the sidelines. Like I said, I didn't have a good practice 2 days ago. So, like just being out there, the guys were just hyped. Like, "Yeah, Mike." So, money Mike, like it's just cool being out there um and just like like I said, attacking it and just really doing I what I can to help this team win and it just shows what I can do um and it's just great uh and a lot of guys, you know, attacked it too on defense. It was just like being able to help this team win is just really the biggest thing and I think, you know, that's the exciting part is showing what I could do on like basically every phase besides offense. So. >> What are your thoughts kind of going into the game? Like like when you entered in, what was your mindset kind of like? >> This is the biggest stadium I've ever been in. Like >> [laughter] >> I'm from Michigan, so like Ford Field is decently big, but like this just this place is booming. Like the Huda chant, just like everything. It was a surreal moment. Going to warm up, I'm like, "Man, I'm in the NFL. All right, time to attack it." So, that's just kind of how I felt going into it. >> Yeah, I guess when I was asked but what does this opportunity knowing that this is the biggest stadium knowing that you played in the NFL and having this opportunity with the Saints, what did this opportunity mean to you? >> It means a lot. I mean, I'm an undrafted rookie. I got to do everything to make this team. And just putting myself out there, putting, you know, good plays out there. And even if it's not making the tackle or getting the sack, it's just doing my job at like a physical 100% everything just on the line every single day, every single game and really just showing what I can do to make the team and, you know, it's just like growing closer together like every day with the dudes in that locker room, too. It's just huge, you know, learning from Grando, from Chase, from Cam, like you know, it's great to learn from a lot of those guys, too. Tyree coming in as well as Ant, like learning from all those guys, Chris, too. Like it it's just like it's an it's an advantage I'm taking like I'm taking advantage of it, you know what I'm saying? So, like that's just the biggest thing is just living it every day and just enjoying it, man. And so, like I think it's a big opportunity and I'm excited for the next two games and enjoying practices that we have, so. >> We were all supposed to deliver on what you did last night. What was your >> Oh, shoot. Um So, they my coach was like, "Listen, none of the edges have been booed, so you better bring your A game." And they were and I was like, "All right." And I was going to do certain songs and I'm like, "I feel like No Diggity." You know No Diggity with Blackstreet? Yeah. Pull a little Dr. Dre rap at the beginning. I just went out there, just had some good moves. Killing it. Literally was listening to every night after practice just like on the way back to the hotel. Got it memorized and everyone enjoyed it, you know. So, that was just Yeah, definitely killed it for sure. >> We got I don't want to make too much of this, but Asiasi, you were Did you come up with this idea last night? You said >> Yeah, it's just one of those things that like it just came to me and so I went with it. Kind of like, you know, Cam Jordan with his levels. I've never seen anyone do that before. So, it's just like, you know, everyone has their own thing, if that makes sense. So, I thought I'd do that. >> the the the thing I'm curious about is do you do you practice that? Or or is literally >> Literally thought >> it in in a game? >> That was the first time I did it. My first sack was the first time I did it. It's just something I thought of. So, I'm like, all right, if this looks bad, oh well, it can be fixed the next time. >> You didn't have one in college then? >> I had like a couple. Um like I'm a devout Christian, and so, you know, I always point to the sky. Um praise Jesus in everything I do. Um you know, I'm still going to pull that out, and like I still thank him for everything, you know, putting me here. Um but like, you know, I thought it'd be nice to have a little bit of something different. I always did like a high kick. Um you know, baseball bat. But like, I did that like once. So, you know, I thought I'd try to find something other than like You know what I'm saying? I'm in the league now. Um I think I need to have something that's just like something that stands out, I guess, if that makes sense. >> It's like also like manifesting a sack in the preseason game. >> Oh, 100%. Come on now. All the guys are like, "Hey, Mike, it's time to go get some." So, I'm like, "I got you." Like, so that's just kind of how it was. >> The part about the next practice like, why do you feel like you had a bad practice? Like, how did you process that? Like, at what point did you get over it? >> So, kind of going in, I was just excited. But like, you know, it's a new team, and I'm like, "Oh, you know, you know, nerves creeping in a little bit, but I'm still like hyped. I'm ready to go." I go in, and, you know, I have a couple good plays, but there was one, and like, you know, we didn't really know much about him. We just kind of went in blinded a little bit. Um and so, I went in, I went to attack the tackle on one. I thought he was passing, so I was like bull rushing. And I didn't realize the running back ran right in this gap. It was a a run play, and I'm sitting here, and I'm passing through like it's a pass, and it looks so bad on film. I'm looking around, I'm like, "Can we like next next clip, please?" Um and then there was one um Um, I we got a call, and I uh supposed to drop but I didn't. I thought the ball was on one side and I think it was just more of like a I was seeing something and I was just going and locking it in instead of just slowing it down. And that's just like what hurt me the most because I know the playbook and I know where to go. It's just kind of those small things that is just slowing the game down and seeing it and then going and attacking it and today I was able to just be cool and just go in and attack it and I was excited and so that really slowed the game down for me. Seeing you know, did study on them from watching the practice see some like little tails with you know, formations Delta motions being able to see those things and then going in getting the play call and be like, all right. I got to drop on this or I got to rush on this. Cool. All right, now let's see what type of you know, formations they're giving me. So I'm able I was able to like really slow it down but really it like it's embarrassing. When you got those plays it's super embarrassing and like you just want to not have those embarrassing plays. You just want to go out there and play good. So >> So like my yesterday was like kind of past it or like there like whatever point you kind of like you know, I don't know if that happened and you go like >> Well, I was kind of over it when I woke up but I realized we had to still finish our clips in the morning. So I'm like, man I still got several bad plays. So I'm like, all right, you know, got over it and I'm just like, man that that was awful and it was really just praying. I you know, I sat in my hotel I prayed a lot. I talked to my wife um and it was really just one of those things that like you're ready to you know, it's a game tomorrow put it behind you. You know, you got to put plays behind you if they maybe they're not your best. And you just got to keep going, you know, have fun with it. Um, so that's just kind of how it was. I you know, I came in today, you know, stomach felt a little gurgly in the morning but like you know, got over it. You know, I was like, man this is exciting. I came here and I'm like, woo. So I just had a rush and you know, I was out there the whole time and you know, here we are. So this really just kind of I don't know, really just calming down, trusting in the Lord that no matter what I'm still his child and I'm still going I'm still alive and I'm still playing ball. So, I think that's just the biggest thing is just going and playing, doing your job, going 100% and you can't do anything wrong there. >> What kind of feedback did you get from Chase and Cam specifically? >> Really just and Cam really is like he harps on getting out the stack. And if you don't know what that means, instead of stopping if you got to the quarterback or stopping when they threw the ball, you run, right? And I you know, I I was a big guy with that a little bit in college and I started to grow in it and here like I think the heat got to me a little bit and so it was one of those things I'm still growing with as doing that but really the biggest emphasis about effort. Right? And you know, in a game, you know, you got to practice how you play. And so in a game you really want to just keep attacking it and you know, chasing after the quarterback scrambles, maybe it's a screen, you just got to get out and go and I think him harping on that really helps us and helps me to understand to just go and keep going. Even if you're tired, just keep going and going and practicing on that he helps. I'm not going to lie, it felt great in the dome today. So, you know, that's just kind of the experience there and then Chase is really just like go mess stuff up. I'm keeping it PG-13 but like, you know, go mess stuff up, dude. Like you were you're better than them, you're physical, you already you were physical in practice so just go be great. So,

title: Saints CB Jayden Price on taking advantage of opportunities, interception & PBU against Jaguars
text: So how do you feel coming out of that one? >> Feeling great. Uh you know, I was just happy with everything. Happy with how I played. Um you know, limited opportunities in camp, so just tried to go out there and make the most of them. Um and felt like I did that today. Always you know, you're going to go back and watch the film tomorrow and there's going to be some things you want to clean up. Um but so far, so good. I'm happy. Um and and just know I got to continue to get better. >> Can you walk us through what you saw on the on the interception? How it all came together for you? >> Yeah. Um you know, we've been hunting um we knew they were going to uh be throwing those deep daggers. Um and and we've been hunting that since joint practice. Um and knew that I I could manipulate him with with some of my, you know, alignment and um you know, I just saw him staring it down and and went and jumped it and ended up making a good play. >> The uh third down pass breakup even before that, was that just as satisfying cuz of the situation, too? Or or >> Yeah. Yeah. Um anytime you get the opportunity and and capitalize on making a play, it's a good feeling. Um you know, just situation, circumstance. Um you know, it's third down. Um and just executing the call and and just playing at a high level, playing fast, and making a play, and it it it was satisfying, for sure. >> Obviously, you only have so many opportunities when when you're you know, trying to get yourself noticed. But they've been giving you so many opportunities. Has that allowed you to to to get into a comfort zone knowing that they've they've they've shown more and more trust in you? >> Yeah, for sure. Um you know, the more trust, you know, I feel like the more confidence it brings out of me. Um you know, just the more opportunities they give me, the more chances I I I have to, you know, make plays on the ball and stuff like that. And just going out there and trying to maximize those opportunities, take advantage of them. Um and and just do it to the best of my ability. >> Hey, maybe this is like nothing, but like for guys who've been like trying to make an NFL roster for like a year or two or three, do you call them out of the tunnel as a starter today. You get to get that opportunity. Like what what does that mean to you and then put it together for the next game. >> It meant a lot. Um, it's been a long journey. Uh, you know, went went undrafted, went to went to Atlanta, then went to the CFL, went to the UFL, then back here last year. Um, last year was a long year and it's it's been a it's been a long journey. Uh, this past off season was great for me. Um, and it meant a lot for me. Um, you know, just continue to push the envelope and continue to get better each and every day and like I said, continue to take advantage of opportunities and and just know that um, you know, when when you do good things, good things will happen. >> Kelvin said a couple times like you're like the poster child for what the practice squad can do for a player. Like how how much like how much did you benefit from that last year just getting a chance to be around and kind of live this life >> [snorts] >> Absolutely, it was everything. Um, meant everything. I learned a lot from Alontae last year. Um, so getting to kind of grow under him last year was a big benefit to me. Um, just being on the practice squad and going against our one offense every single day got me better as a player and as a person. Um, you know, and I I as an organization as a whole, they travel their practice squad players. So, um, that was a great experience for me. Just game day operations, game day meetings, just going about every single process. Um, just going about it the right way and just knowing how to handle that and and be a professional. Um, helped me get to where I'm at today and meant a lot to me. >> If they like people starting like realize who you are, recognize you more like what you got about? >> Uh, I haven't been out too much. Um, but you know, I hope so. We'll see. We'll see. Um, you know, it's been a great two and a half three weeks of camp so far. Great first preseason game. But just got to continue to get better. Got to continue to build on it. And hopefully by the end of you know, this training camp, this preseason process, then people will start to know who I am and and they can really put a face to a name and stuff like that. >> How cool was it to get the introductions like they did with the whole defensive line? >> It was it was super surreal. It was awesome. I was just talking with some of the media guys where they come through the fog, can't really see anything and then the curtain opens and then it's roaring. So it was great experience. It was a lot of fun and meant a lot to be out there. >> Did you enjoy your opportunity as well as a returner on the day? >> Oh, absolutely. Yes. I That's that's what That was my specialty in college. So it's always good to get back there at returner. You know, I'm sure I'll get a few more opportunities this preseason. But it was good to get back there and have an opportunity and get the ball in my hands again. >> What's that What's that like as a as a defensive guy? You're not often trying to you know, run test your vision in that way. But yet you flip over to returner and you've done that so successfully. What's that sort of transition like? >> Um Honestly, I don't think a whole lot of it. You know, obviously you kind of got to adjust your eyes a little bit. Got to learn how to read read blocks and everything like that. Um Thankfully, I feel like I'm just a natural at it. You know, just coming from high school as a quarterback just and then growing throughout college and being punt returner and everything like that. You know, I've been blessed and I feel like I'm a little bit natural to it. But I mean, you got to adjust a little bit. You know, instead of instead of giving the hit, you got to take the hit and stuff like that. So just adjusting a little bit. But but yeah, it was so far so good. So >> Do you feel like the new I guess it's not new anymore, but the kickoff structure in the NFL, Do you feel like that sets you up for more, better, different? What did your experience with it kind of be in the NFL, really? >> Yeah, yeah. For sure, yeah. I think going through it in the UFL before I came up here last year, um, definitely made me more familiar with it, um, and everything like that. You know, the returns are just going to hit faster and hit harder. Um, you know, you just it's it's 11 on 11. You got to make sure blocks are set up. You got to set up your blocks well, but, um, they're going to hit fast. That hole is going to open, um, and then you're just going to have an opportunity to split it. Um, so you just got to be clean. You got to make one one cut and then hit it. You can't dance and dilly and stuff like that. Um, but definitely the UFL definitely prepared me well for that. >> This game you started with that big return and and estimated touchdown and obviously as a defense you come up with an interception on the first drive. How much has quick starts been emphasized in camp and how cool maybe was that to see it come to fruition uh quickly in the game? >> It's been emphasized pretty much every day. Um, you know, definitely every week we we do situations like that. So we're definitely emphasizing it. It's been just after last year been a big emphasis on starting fast and you know, it was great to see. Especially that opening return it lit the place up. So whenever we can get that energy, get that momentum, it means a lot and it's it's crucial for how the game can go. And it was a big moment and everything like that. But like coach said, we we got to find a way to finish and everything like that. So it was it was positive, but got to keep building.
