So like just grateful for the opportunity. I'm blessed I was able to go out there and make plays and capitalize on opportunities at hand. I hate that we couldn't get a win, but uh we back on the drawing board. Back at it tomorrow I mean back at it Monday. >> How mentally has it been just not being able to get out there? >> Uh mentally it sucks. Like being able just watching my teammates and not being able to go out there and compete with them and and fight with them and go to war with them. So yeah, like last year and not just being not not being able to be out there was real tough for me mentally, but now I'm I'm healed, I'm healthy, I'm going out there, I know what I'm doing, I know my job, I'm making plays. So everything's looking uphill right now. >> We've seen you and Zach connect a lot >> Oh yeah. >> in training camp and that showed up today. Like what do you like about what he's done out there and what >> Um arm talent is amazing. Zach, his arm talent is amazing. And he's he's uh he's a baller for sure. Like he going to take risk. You'll see he going to throw it and he me and him had a connection. We've been building chemistry. I ain't going to say I'm his favorite target, but like I might be his favorite target at this point. So like I know my boy going to feed me and I I'm going to make the plays. We going We going to help each other out. Let's put it that way. We going to make sure we both shining. >> Yes, I think that there was that the near touchdown. >> Yeah. >> And then there's the 37-yard run on the sideline. Can you describe that play and then what happened there? >> Um well, I just got the play call. I knew like the corner's been sitting flat-footed, so I knew if I just got got the corner to basically stop his feet just a little bit like then I can run past him and he just made a great throw and I made a catch. That's that's just kind of a routine play for us though like like I said, we've been building chemistry all camp and since he's been here, so we've had a lot of time to get certain plays and certain tendencies down. >> How does it get it's kind of that every day? >> You feel like you're making the case that you want to make it and you just going to do everything that you set out to do right now? >> Um, yes, sir. I feel like I'm making the best out of every opportunity that I'm granted and I feel like that's the only thing I can do in my position right now. Just I can't complain about the opportunities, but I can do what I can while when the opportunity comes. So, like I said, I'm making plays. I'm going out there and I really don't care what play it is. I'm going 100% effort. Even if I mess up, I'm not really mad that I messed up, but you're going to see if I mess up, I'm messing up at 100 mph. You know what I'm saying? So, like I'm just blessed to be able to be in this position and still get granted opportunities and be able to make plays. >> Where do you feel like you made the most improvements since the last time you were out there on on that field? Uh I feel like more of a I took a more of a mental step. Like physically, I've always been blessed and gifted, but like mentally, I I feel like I slowed the game down this year. Like I understand certain differences more and I understand where I need to be at. I understand the concepts a little better. >> Is it part of like having to sit back and and look at the game? >> When you were hurt and when you were out? >> Yeah. So, like me being able just to be physically gifted and better and faster and being stronger like than most people like I feel like I go out there and before I got hurt, I wasn't a student of the game. So, like after I got hurt and got to looking at I had to really become a student of the game. I had to learn defenses, learn the concepts, learn everything, so like I can go out there and put my talent on display.

title: Saints QB Spencer Rattler on strip-sack and performance against Jaguars in preseason opener
text: Yeah, I mean um good to get out there in the live action again. Um obviously started fast with Ty taking it back and just handing it off on a one-play drive is always nice. Um you know, I thought field position-wise the next two um kind of got stuck back there. Didn't have a great rhythm early on. Um and then got to avoid the the the fumble backed up. I mean trying to get out some pressure, probably just try to dirt it or go down and then move on to the next play. Defense did a great job stopping them, holding them to three. Thought we came out that third or fourth drive in the second quarter with a good rhythm. Uh converting on third down. Thought Barry on made some big catches. Kevin ran some good routes, made some good plays. And then um just kind of stalled it out there in in uh high red and made the field goal. Um but good to get some live action in. Um definitely a lot of stuff to improve on after preseason game one. Um just got to keep getting better as a group. >> The fumble where you was it was just like uh scrambling all people on trying to wait for something to develop or >> Um I mean >> [snorts] >> just hold on to the ball. Hold on a little tighter. You know, they kind of converged and try to get through there. Should have just try to dirt it or go down. >> How nice was it for you to bounce back after that >> Yeah, it was good. You know, I I don't know how many plays that drive was, but it felt like probably a 14-play drive or so. So, it's good to get those reps in, get that conditioning in um in different type of situations and you know, like I said, I thought Barry on made two good contested slant catches for first downs on like third and five. Um Kevin had press man on a I think that was another third down and he just big-bodied the guy, ran a great route, and he got a nice comeback, too, on a little scramble out. Um and then yeah, I mean probably could have been a little more aggressive there in the high red, but I thought overall um thought Nuss called good plays and had it rolling and um it's good to get that those live reps. >> The sack fumble was there last week, I think. >> Um I just try to make a guy miss and then like I said, I probably should have just tried to dirt it at the running backs' feet or just go down. You know, it's tough to get out. You know, I probably should have just thrown it away. Um just got to hold onto the ball tighter. You can't be doing that. >> How do you feel now camp and could be colorful >> Yeah, I mean what I Kellen said, we're still still camp mode for us. We got to keep grinding, keep improving. Um but excited to get out there and have two joint practices and uh you know, two more games coming up. Uh some more good opportunities for us.

title: Postgame Interviews: John Harbaugh, Jaxson Dart, Malachi Fields, Odell Beckham Jr. & more
text: What did you think Jackson took over your feelings at that moment when you saw that happen? >> My feelings in that moment was we need to block better. That's what my feeling was. >> Was there any hesitation in putting him back in? >> No. No, he was fine. >> You went up and looked like talked to him before >> [snorts] >> he went for the check Jackson on the >> No, I don't think so. I don't remember doing that. If I did, I did. I don't remember what I said. I don't think I talked to him. >> Some people obviously went up to him. Did you did >> No, I I did I don't I don't know. >> Did he tell you like that he was fine or >> No, no, that was upstairs. He was Yeah, he was fine. He told me after that he he said after he didn't tell me after, but I heard he said after he just got the wind knocked out of him. So, he was fine. >> Coach, obviously your first time on the sideline I mean like coaching a game being preseason. Just what was what was the feeling like for you big picture? >> Thanks for that question. I appreciate that. Uh I I really I really was I felt I felt you know, you you there's meaning to a lot of things, you know, and you're you're so wrapped up in the game even coming over here this morning and seeing the guys in meeting last night touching the guys during the you know, pre talking the guys before the game, you know, like cuz it's a game, you know? And sometimes you just take a minute my wife texted me a really cool text about that very thing, you know, this is this is it's a moment. You know, understand you know, what this means and enjoy it and and be encouraging and be up beat and and this is this is a this is a big beginning in in your in your in our life, you know? And I feel that way for the organization. I feel that way for the team the guys. And I feel that way for the coaches. I feel that way for our families and then for me personally uh it was a it was a good start. >> John, on Jackson's touchdown throw can that only be made to a receiver who's 6' 4"? >> If if a smaller receiver can really jump, it could probably be made by a smaller receiver if he could jump high if he could jump high enough and get it. >> But you see he you know, you had you had your rookie against the smaller linebacker. >> Well, I mean it to you I think what you're asking is that you know, that the the value of a of a contested catch big contested catch receiver in the red zone, right? And that's really what that is. I mean, that's one of the reasons we drafted him. That's what Malachi One of the things he does exceptionally well. He's getting better at so many things, but I mean, that was a heck of a play. I mean, that's that's played by that most red zone I would I would say argue I'm not sure the stats exactly. Most red zone touchdown passes are not on time. Most red zone touchdown passes are extended and or plus scrambles. And that's you know, you got a quarterback who can move around and find a guy. You got a guy who can make a play. You know, that's that's how you that's how you score a lot of those touchdowns. That was good to see. >> What do you think about Jackson's perspective like the first play to go back in there and then make that play? >> It was great. I mean, I was I I don't know. We were in a heat of battle. I didn't think too much about it. He walked by me, looked at me, and he goes like this, and I went like that, and he ran on the field. You know, that was what it was. So, he he was playing quarterback that series, and it was that was we're going to go two series, and he was back, you know, so we went out there and and did it. But to see him go out there and throw a touchdown pass, I thought it was pretty darn cool. I was excited about that. Made me happy. But really, you're in the back you're in you're coaching a game. You're trying to win the game. You go to the next play, you know, and try to try to make the next play. >> John, you as a player, did you guys ever block better on that play? Is that because of the play call? Is that not his responsibility, Jackson's, to see that pressure coming? >> No, he can assume he's picked up there. I mean, some I think he will feel pressure. He has good pocket presence, you know, and he did it on a he did it on the red zone play. He got himself out, you know, so he thinks he's good at that, but that's one that, you know, should be picked up. >> John, what's the benefit >> Scatback on that drive, too. Like the fact that he was running on that That's obviously his first game since that injury. >> Yeah, I was I was you know, I was excited about it because I I thought I saw the Cam Scatback that you guys all know, you know, and and saw last year. So, I don't I don't know if he's 100% you know, twitchy and explosive yet, but he's getting he's getting there. He's come a long way in the last two three weeks. >> How did Odell look to you, John? >> I thought he looked pretty good. You know, he looked pretty good. Made a couple catches, you know, did some things, some things he could have done better. He'll He'll be the guy first guy to tell you that, you know, but uh thought he looked looked solid, I would say, you know. >> The reception he got from the crowd, you know. >> Yeah, yeah, it was fun. That was fun. I mean, you know, I love Odell. I I do. That was he's what he's doing what he's fighting for, you know, I don't know how it's going to turn out. It's going to turn out the way the way it turns out, you know, based on what happens. But to see his fight, his determination, his humility what he's He's got his son in camp the other day. You know, he's doing it for his son. You know, that just as a friend, you know, that makes me really proud of him. >> Do you have any injury >> ask about the risk reward of starters playing Jackson and the starters. What did they get out of being out there today? >> Uh they got reps in a game. Which they're not going to get until the first game if you don't play them in the preseason. And it's different. You know, they played They played their whole starting defense. You know, uh we played about half our starting defense to start the game. So, I I decided not to play some of those starting defensive guys for that reason. Didn't think that I thought that they would benefit more from not playing. Uh they played their whole starting defense, you know. Um I think we played all of our starting offense except for our left tackle. And uh felt like he didn't need to He would be fine. But felt like the other guys playing together was important, you know, especially with Jackson out there. And our quarterback got two got I don't know 10 15 plays out there of uh of good football. So, he's going to be that much better uh for the regular season that he would have been if he hadn't played those games. And And we got out of it healthy. So, it worked. >> Was going to ask if any injuries or no look like Kayvon had a a wrap on his shin. >> Yeah, he's he's fine. Yeah, nothing serious. Um everything should be good. We should get some guys back this week. Those are kind of those minor things, day-to-day type things. We should get some guys back. >> From overall, how did the operation go in terms of the coaching, the communication, all that. >> Great question. I thought the operation headsets streamlined communication, getting plays in, substitutions were all very good, especially for the first preseason game. We really didn't have any hiccups with that. I just don't like the penalties in the critical moments, you know? I think we had a couple holding penalties, we had we had the I don't know about Arch's penalty. I mean, I you know, we'll see it on tape, but wow, you know, I mean, you know, that's a young that's a young guy who's really, you know, try you know, he's training for the league, so that's fine. I get too upset about it, but um just uh there's an opportunity that the pick the pick play. We have a chance to go win the game. You know, we need to execute that play. In critical moments, you know, throughout the game, when those plays come up, those opportunities come up, and you don't know when they're going to happen, but they're going to happen. You take the ball all the way down the field. Now, we got a third down opportunity. The play has to be executed exactly right. And that's why you practice the way you do. And I told the guys that very thing. That's why you know, don't tell me about how hard practice is. You know, no and our guys don't. You know, lock in when you're a little bit tired because we we we're 10 plays into a drive, and we got to execute this play perfectly. Why? Because it it probably will win us the game if we do. And that's what we're fighting for. Our guys are working for that, and that's where we've got to just keep getting better. >> Joe, were you surprised in any way when Jackson was sent to the blue tent? >> Uh honestly, I was. You know, honestly, I was, but I would say that they you know, their their job is to err on the side of player safety, so I can't argue with that, either. You know. >> What do you make of everything that unfolded from the hit to the tent to the touchdown pass? >> Yeah, um I thought it was a a good drive by, you know, the offense just being resilient. you know, it's big by, you know, even Jameson uh you know, motor just making a play to get us down there, and um you know, us being able to to have a big play in the red zone on a scramble drill, and Malkai just showing what he's been, you know, consistently showing all through camp and through practices of uh continued to to play along with the play and then uh being able to make a contested catch. So, was really proud of of, you know, the protection up front, the resiliency of the whole drive, and um and us ending in a score, which I thought was really cool. As far as the um the blue tent, like I I really respect um the rules and the thought behind, you know, um the NFL has of keeping players healthy and reviewing things, but it at the same time I'm I'm still puzzled by it just feeling like every time that I get hit, you know, I just find I find my way in there. Um which I'm at times I still try to wrap my head around, but um that's all that I'm going to say about that situation. Um you know, I'm I'm really happy with how the the drive ended. >> Is that just your reality at this point? Like do you just have to handle it? >> Is that that or is there anything you can do about it? >> That's all I'm going to say about that situation. >> wind knocked out of you? Was that what happened? >> Yeah, the guy made a good hit on me. >> Did you get the wind knocked out of you? >> Mhm. >> Jackson, how did you end up going back in the game? Most guys wouldn't go back in the game after that. It's the preseason. Did you talk [clears throat] to Harbaugh like, "Hey, I want to go back in after I got cleared?" >> Well, I never thought that I was going to be taken out. >> No. So, I'm going to keep playing until they tell me I'm not playing. Like I want to be out there. >> Jackson, on the play on the play, do you have any responsibilities on the back side or with the play call, are you just assuming that's getting picked up and that's that's part of the play? >> Uh I think that we had just a little maybe miscommunication um in the protection scheme. Um you know, and that and stuff like that happens in preseason where, you know, we're not all all on the same page in in a protection, and um you know, I think that that's that's a a moment that we can really look back on and learn from because you know you have events like that where you know the the group is able to to watch it and experience it and then you know make sure that we don't you know make that mistake move forward. >> Jackson, when you were scrambling and when do you first notice that your rookie receiver has a smaller guy on him and you say okay here's a chance. >> Yeah, I that was a a big thing that I love about Malachi's tape coming out was his ability to go make contested catches. I feel like he's a player that regardless of what route that he's on just from his range and stature and his ability to have really good hands that he's never out of a play. So And and he he loves the game. He competes through the whistle. You see that in the way that not only he runs his routes but also the way that he blocks. So you know I think that you know he's just been doing what he's been doing and and I have a ton of faith in him. >> Jackson, are you also on the scramble drill conscious of the routes that the guys are supposed to be blocking in that situation so you kind of know where he's going to be in the area before you even look down field. >> Yeah, I think that we make like the guys when they're out there they understand their responsibilities during the route and then when you break contain it's it's more of like your instincts take over and he was able to to find a a hole in the defense and he went to exploit it and then when you have you know a defender who's trailing and that you have a guy that's you know as big as him you can just give him a chance and he's going to make the play. >> What did you see on the sack on the third down in the first drive? >> Uh we just had a miscommunication. >> How was the how beneficial was it for you to get these two series in this game? >> I thought it was really good. Um you know I I I really feel like if we were on the on the same page all of us on the first drive we would have scored the first drive. but like I said after like it's it's good for us to have those moments where we're able to come off the field and communicate with each other to make sure that those things don't happen again in a situation that's outside of practice or maybe in practice um it may be the consequence isn't the same as in a game. And so us being able to see that, have that understanding, um and then the second drive is just a resilient drive by by us and um as a whole unit which I was really proud of. >> What do you think of Scat today? >> It was great to have him back out there. Um you know, the energy that he brings, his physicality, his um you know, just will all around um brings a lot of positive and and tough energy into our huddle. So, you know, not only was I happy to have him back out there, but I was just happy for him to um I know recoveries of injuries are are tough. So, when you have the opportunity to be out there on the field, you you take advantage of it and I thought he did. >> Harbaugh said that he can see last year's Scat. Where are you at with that? Like do you think he's all the way back or do you do you see him like still having, you know, somewhere else that he can get to? Like where where do you look at that? >> I think that he's just going to continue to get better. Um I thought that even last year that um you know, it was just his rookie year. So, you know, there's there's improvements that he's going to continue to make and I think that the experience that he had was very valuable and I think going forward now he's just he's just a he's a more mature player. Um he's starting to understand the NFL schemes more and more. And I think that this run game suits him. I think that it's um you know, it's going to be very valuable for our offense to to really establish that. So, I think uh I I I do believe that he's just going to continue to get better. >> Gus, were you glad that Harbaugh decided to play you today? And would you like to play in these other preseason games as well as you kind of work with this new offense towards the regular season? >> Yeah, I'm ready to go out there whenever my my number's called. Um I love this game and I take you know, I want to take full advantage of every opportunity that I have when I'm out there. So, um I love being out there. I love being out there with the guys, with the boys and and just competing. So, um yeah, like I said, whenever my number's called, like I'm I'm excited. >> How different is your preseason this year compared to last year knowing that we're always waiting for that idea of, okay, well, the next time we don't know when Jackson's going to play once the regular season comes. Being able to grow in the in the preseason and get ready for the regular season knowing that this is your job, this is your offense. Is there anything that's different that helps you grow more one week to the next, one week to the next knowing that, you know, you are now prepping for week one and it's not an uncertainty? >> Yeah, I think that you just have to I think what's really nice is now is that I get more reps than I did last year in practices. So, I think that that's really the time where I I try to grow as much as I can. Um you know, I'm definitely not afraid to make mistakes in in those periods and I think that when you get out to a to a game, um like I said earlier, like consequences are different and and that's what you learn from practice of um you know, how much can I test this or test that? How much um you know, can we as an offense do against different looks? And I think that when you're able to have these live action looks that's different from what we're seeing every day, I think that it's very valuable and gets us better. Um but from an approach standpoint, um there's just more reps that I have and uh I just get to take advantage of of those as it goes. >> How did you feel about the first touchdown and connecting? >> Oh, I'm so excited. I'm so excited. I mean, that's what I So, I wanted to do the first drive. So, uh it was good that we were able to go out there in the second drive and do that and um you know, when you have a rookie guy who gets to score his first touchdown like that and and make a really good play, I think that, you know, as us as a whole team was we're really excited and um you know, happy that Malkai was able to get his first >> Why do you think you and likely have developed such a quick chemistry, especially in those conversion downs? It feels like you're always looking for him and it feels like he's open and you're connecting. >> He He a great feel for the game. He is very instinctual and I think that he does a great job of of seeing it through that lens of a quarterback in a way. And um you saw that a ton in his tape in Baltimore of him and Lamar um or maybe it wasn't even drawn up the exact way, but just being able to have conversions and him being able to find empty zones and and to get open. Like I think that that's the title that he has is that he he gets open, he finds a way to get open. So, when you have a guy like that that you can trust to get open, uh definitely gives you a lot of confidence in in those situations and um he works hard. And we have a lot of conversations, you know, late at night in the film room um just going over things. So, all of those things account to to a lot of confidence and I think he's doing a great job. >> So, is that the definition of never giving up on a play and knowing what a quarterback is and keeping it alive? >> Yeah, for sure. Uh you know, we we talk about scramble drill all the time, you know, in red zones like 50% of the touchdown passes are scramble drill. So, we work it all the time and that's kind of what happened. So. >> Can you describe the the catch, how you felt it, and then did you see the replay zone it? >> Yeah, so I I originally had like a shallow crosser and then once I saw Jackson breaking out of the pocket, you know, I'm the low guy, so I turn up and then just trying to make some space and he puts the ball up and I can make a play. >> What what was it like to be out there for your first preseason game in Hard Rock Stadium in the NFL action? >> No, it was amazing um to be back playing football again. Uh pads on, hitting live, it's just it's fun, you know. I had a few insert blocks in there, too. Just just getting my helmet on on a safety was is is fun. >> How crazy was it that kind of series of plays? Jackson takes the sack, big hit goes off, and then you see James running on. I mean, that had to be one of those things where it's like, "Okay, this is if this happens in a real game, got to be ready, doesn't matter what's going on." >> Yeah, for sure. It's that kind of that like next man up, you know, everybody's ready um to go mentality. You know, anything can happen, but we got to see he's okay after that after that hit and then he was able to deliver, you know, a strike for a touchdown. >> Did you even see him coming back into the game and when did you realize when he was back in the huddle? >> I did. >> When they announced it in the press box, they called it a touchdown pass for for James. >> they really? No, I saw him I saw him running on to call the play in the huddle and then I knew he was good to go, knew he was back in. >> Yeah, I assume that is the ball. >> Yes, sir. Yeah, yeah, it's the ball. >> How do you measure the idea of it being preseason, but also being a milestone, being, you know, your first here? >> Um, I think it's awesome. Just one thing, I mean, just take every day like it's your last, like preseason or not. Just go out there and and do what you do. Even if it's practice. I mean, this is just I guess it's a different showcase, different spotlight on it just cuz it's a game, but I mean, preseason or regular season, just make a play. >> Anything surprise you about today? Being the first, walking in the stadium? >> Uh, no, not not really. I was just kind of looking forward to it, excited about it. I knew it was coming, but yeah. Uh, just just going to go and at the house so we all can look at it. So, >> Which which house do you guys grew up in? >> Oh, no, no, back here. Just where I'm at right now. So, me and my family can just see it and just be like, "No, that that was the first one." >> Good. Good. What was the How much improvisation was on that play there? It was kind of a little bit of broken situation, right? >> Uh, yeah, it was probably 50/50. So, it started off, you know, as a regular play and then once you see him scramble and get out of the pocket, you know, it's just scramble rules and we just, you know, try to get open and make a play. >> When did you know you were going to be able to jump up there and get it? >> Um, once I once I started breaking out of the end zone, I saw him kind of looking at me. I figured he was going to try to give me a chance. So, yeah. >> It's kind of a play you're supposed to make, right? >> Yeah, right, right. That's what he wanted me be here for, so. >> On special teams, you also had a big hit. Um how did that feel? And I mean you're putting yourself out on the line already, game one of preseason. And I mean how was it going there and and laying somebody out like that? >> Oh, that was that was awesome. I was telling Chris Horton I was like I was like I got to get a tackle. And he like got to leave me in there on punt, so I was just excited to, you know, just do my job and, you know, I haven't haven't really tackled anybody since like high school back in my safety days, but now it was it was fun just to to be able to make an impact on more than just offense. >> Did you talk your way talk your way into staying out there at all? Is that what you're saying? >> Uh a little bit, but you know, it was kind of kind of the plan anyways. I was supposed to be out there right slot for points anyways, so. Yes, sir. I'm sorry. >> On that play did you see a small linebacker and you right away >> Uh no, so I mean at first it was just like a shallow crosser. I was just the low piece of the of the route tree and then I saw him break the pocket so he was scrambling so I just turned up cuz I was the low guy and then Jackson just gave me a chance, so. >> Um he gave you a chance, but you had to go up I mean it was you had to go up still, you know, you're tall, you know, right? >> Yes, sir. Yeah. Yeah. >> You think how important that play would you say? >> I think so, yeah. Yeah. >> Um some quarterbacks won't make that throw, right? You know what I mean cuz you're not really open. You're just >> Right. I think it was just the you know, the trust and you know, what he wanted me here for just throw it up and 50/50 ball and me make a play on it, so. >> If you could have picked one to get your first one and get it in a preseason game, would it be a contested catch where you can show your strength? >> For sure. Yeah, definitely. >> What do you like about that the best? >> Um just my ability to be able to do so and the quarterback having trust in me, too, cuz you know, it's 50/50 it can go either way, but he trusted me to go to come down with the ball, so. >> Those are kind of the plays that we were kind of talking about the other day as far as you wanted to make those high contested catches and all that stuff like that for you. Is that kind of like hey, this is why they brought me in kind of thing? You just feel that way? >> Yeah, exactly. And then also in the field as well with the with the the third down conversion with the slant and then the the hitch to the field getting the first down out of that and just all the little things but that for sure. >> Even though it was preseason, were there any kind of nerves coming in just for this being like the first like NFL game I guess? >> Uh more just excitement. I was just ready to get out there and ready to play. I was juiced up before. Wouldn't say nerves but just excited to to get out there. >> When Jaxon went down there with uh got hit and had to come out of the game just what was going through your mind there? >> Um I was thinking we still got a game to play. I like to let them figure out and then how to help best serve their game. So uh just happy for him, happy for the guys in our room. Obviously, we didn't win, but you know, just got to get better. I mean I felt good. I feel good being out there. I feel, you know, when you see the tape or at practice, I'm getting open. Um but at the end of the day, receiver always talk about this is the most selfless position on the field. You You wait around all game for everybody to do their job just for five opportunities, maybe. I'm sure you were going to enjoy watching it. >> Somebody got to feel this pain. It's been I've been sitting down for a minute. I got a lot of stuff built up, so somebody got to feel this pain. >> You're a rookie receiver now. I was saying that Coach Harbaugh said last night that the rookies after you played this game, you didn't feel like you belonged. Is that what he said, and do you feel that way now? >> Oh, yeah. That Yeah, after the game he came up to me and he was like, "How do you feel about your first game?" I said, "It was It was It was amazing." then he hit me with a question, "Do you feel like you belong?" And it got me wondering. Um I do honestly feel like I belong, but at the same time I just don't want to belong. I want to dominate the league, obviously. That's the mentality that every kid has, but you know, [snorts] as a rookie, you know, you want to come in and you want to earn that trust, obviously. >> You feel more so now? >> Uh-huh. >> As opposed to yesterday? >> Oh, yeah. >> Did you have any moment on the field where you didn't have tons of snaps, something physical happened, and you kind of looked at the other team and thought to yourself, >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, it was a whole game. I mean, before the game, it was like anxious anxiety. Yeah. Yeah, it was a it was third and extra long. We hit the screen. I was like, "You know what? And then once I I saw a motor get out there and he missed with the blocks, I looked at my guy. I was like, "All right, are you running with me now?" And then I just take it for a ride. >> It looks like you got Jamal in there, too. I mean you took out two guys, no? On the screen? >> On the screen? Uh I wasn't sure. I mean, I had to go look back at the film. All I remember was I was running my guy. >> CC, even though the pressure came from the outside, is there a large part of you that gets angry when you see the quarterback going to the >> Oh yeah. Yeah. I mean, as an offensive lineman, your main priority is protecting your quarterback. And when we see something like that, it was just you know, you want to encourage not only yourself to to do better, but also encourage your your other four guys on the line of scrimmage to, you know, make sure that our quarterback is healthy. >> Nah, I knew he was fine. I mean, he said he was fine. I mean, obviously you get speared, you know, it kind of knocks the wind out of you. So, I've never been speared before, but I'm sure getting speared full speed isn't a good feeling. So, but I mean, he's fine. >> You're a little >> You could take it a little [laughter] better, probably. >> But still getting speared like putting a again, someone's shoulder back putting in your gut like that will affect anyone. It doesn't matter who you are. >> What does it show you when he comes back? So, it's the preseason. He doesn't have to come back into the game. He comes back and throws a touchdown pass. I gather he probably talked his way back into the >> Yeah, man. That's just who he is. You know, he wants to finish what he started. We weren't going to play for too long today. Just kind of get your feet wet, get back out there. So, you know, for him, it's always he wanted to finish the drive because he knew he was done after that. So, that's who what is. >> What did you think of the you guys ran the ball? >> Uh pretty good. I mean, we don't have everything in. >> And um I mean, we ran it pretty good against that type of defense, you know, that defense is um It's It's a lot to prepare for on a weekly basis, you know, played them majority of my career now, like especially playing the floor system. So, you know, I think we did a good job. If I think we had a whole week to game plan them, then I think we'd have a lot of success cuz we have a pretty crazy run game, you know, so but I feel like for the time that we were in there, the run game was pretty damn good. >> Scott, particularly, I mean, it's the first time we've seen him in a game since that horrible scene. >> Yeah. No, I mean, he's getting his feet under him, too, you know, I mean, that's what the preseason is for. Get your feet under you, get, you know, dip your toes in the water a little bit, get wet, and just um you know, get things ready for the opener. >> I'm part of all What was it like, you you know, in here after the game, on the sideline? That was the first Hard Rock game, so >> I mean, nothing crazy, just however you expect it to be, you know, it's the preseason. I was like, all right, we're going back to West Virginia for camp next year. Um and we even put a a note on our calendars like, all right, this is the earliest we're able to book uh the house that we want to stay >> While we're talking West Virginia, I did I said this to you before. What is the biggest thing you've learned through now three weeks of practice uh for the twen- you know, for the 2026 Giants or John Harbaugh or whatever? >> I'm still very curious how this offense is going to come together. The the clock is ticking. But, I think you're going to see, as we get closer to the season, they're going to have to hone in on the things that either A, he's good at, and B, they're good at. You say, "All right, we got to take that concept out, that page out of the playbook," whatever you want to say. title: POSTGAME LIVE: Who stood out in Giants' preseason opener vs. Vikings?
text: All right, everybody. As Jonathan Pride says, Pat, let's effing go. Pat Leonard here from the New York Daily News and the Talking Ball with Pat Leonard podcast. I know I said it was going to start at 5:00. It is 5:38 p.m. and have a special dinner to attend tonight. So, we're not going to go very long. So, if you have comments or questions you definitely want answered from what I saw on the field or what I heard in the locker room or in the press conferences, please dump them into super chats to guarantee that you will have them answered, heard, and seen. But thank you all for being here. Thank you for being patient. We are of course here at Metife Stadium after the Giants 13-10 preseason opening loss to the Minnesota Vikings. And the headline of course is Jackson Dart. It's always going to be about Jackson Dart, especially early this season with the quarterback in his second year trying to ascend, trying to further develop, learning the position under a new offensive staff, new offense. And I think what we were looking for today coming in, although the head injuries and the hits that Dart has taken has been a huge part of his story and narrative so far in the NFL, I think we were all just looking at this game, not even through that lens. We were just walking into Metife Stadium today thinking, is Jackson Dart going to play better than he and the offense have in the training camp so far through three weeks between West Virginia and East Rutherford, New Jersey. And we were going to evaluate some football. We knew it was going to be a small sample size. And as I told you guys, I expected Dart to play. I expected a lot of the starters to play. Um, on the first team offense, the only people who did not play were Andrew Thomas, who was healthy, and Malik Neighbors, who was still rehabbing the knee. Neighbors was on the sideline, so it was Thomas. But, um, otherwise, this was the full go, full first team offense, and you saw two drives, namely because usually they have snap counts in their minds as far as what they want the quarterback and players to get, not necessarily from a series number standpoint. And the first series just wasn't very long. It was five or six plays, six plays I believe. And um so you know the headline comes out of this is that the Jackson Dart full experience is already on display. And what does that mean? Well, we know what that means. It means injury and blue tent and it also means some playmaking. That's what we've grown to know and expect from Jackson Dart. So we saw him take that monster hit on the blitz. He was sacked twice on six drop backs and Dart had two third down conversions to Isaiah likely. You saw it in real time. He loves number nine. He and number nine finding really good chemistry. Dart saying that Likely knows how to get open. He knows how to find those windows in the zone. They really like uh that connection. The Giants do. And clearly Dart and Likely have something going there. He even said they're watching tape late at night together talking about different things. and he thinks that likely sees the game through the quarterback's eyes. So, that's great to hear. And Cam Scataboo looked pretty good running the ball. Had four carries. And with Thomas out, no surprise they were running the ball more to the right side. And I thought it was encouraging between CC Maui Noah and Germaine Aluminor over there on the right side with Brian Hudson at center. I thought you saw them moving the pile a little bit. You know, that was interesting and exciting to see. And also, I think a lot of the things that I've told you I'm seeing in practice every day from a physical standpoint showed up on offense. You saw Pat Ricard, the fullback, making a clear difference in bringing that physicality and um creating a push and punishing the defense and not just blocking them. And then Arl Ree, even though the run defense from the quote unquote defensive starters wasn't perfect by any means, you saw some of Reese's physicality and speed. He filled a hole on one play for a nice run stop where he shed his blocker as he was coming downhill and still made the one-on-one tackle. Um, you know, the Giants did not start all of their defensive starters. They did not start DJ Reer, Shelby Harris on the interior. Brian Burns did not play. Javon Holland at safety did not either. And they were missing Paul Adibbo, Greg Nuome, and Drew Phillips due to injuries there nursing and just protecting their bodies. But, you know, something to clean up for Dinard Wilson to take into the film room is on that first drive, uh, I believe it was six carries for 44 yards by the Vikings starting offense, including an 18-yer for Aaron Jones right off the bat pass Kavon Tibido and Deontay Banks on the left side of the offense and then a Jordan Mason 15yard run kind of up the gut there. So, plenty for them to work on. Um, but they did get the red zone stop. Mike McFaten and our Darius Washington in on that. And so that was good to see. So plenty of positives, plenty of interesting things developing. We'll talk about Odell Beckham Jr. as well. As I said, uh time constraints today here at Metife Stadium. Sorry, a little technical difficulties there. What's going on? It's preseason mode here for Talking Ball with Pat Leonard. All right, so we're going to get into your questions and the queue, guys. I'm probably running right up until 6 and then either a little before 600 or a little after 6, we're going to wrap up. So, this will be a quick one. We will come back again on Monday evening and plan on our normal schedule now, Mondays and Thursday nights on most weeks, followed by the postgame lives. Early afternoon, probably Eastern time. Um, so that'll be exciting as well. That'll be their their next test for Jackson Dart and them getting on the field. Um, what I'm going to jump in with, I'm going to tell you about Dart's response to being sent to the Blue Tent and his comments and Harbaugh's comments on that. And then we will get into your questions and right around 6:00, maybe a little bit before we will jump and we will see you next time. You can find my coverage on the Daily News website as well as also on social media. So, really quickly on Dart, Dart said he is still puzzled that he keeps getting sent to the blue tent every time he gets hit. Now, of course, it wasn't every time he did get sacked twice. The first time he was tackled, he did not. The second time he did, he got absolutely smoked on that play. Uh, John Harbaugh said flat out, "We need to block better." He seemed to be pinning it directly on Tyrone Tracy, the running back. Harbaugh also said, you know, Dart's awareness usually is pretty good. He felt like they just need to have it blocked up. I'm watching it live and it looked to me like the quarterback, if he's looking and scanning the full field, should have been able to see where the pressure was coming from, but also where his out was if he saw it out of the corner of his eye, uh, you know, out of the peripheral vision. Now, the play was definitely designed to go to the left. I asked Dart about did he have any backside responsibilities. Dart said that they had some miscommunication in their protection scheme on that play. So, the way I view it is at the very least the quarterback and center along with the rest of the offense, they're in charge of getting everybody lined up and figuring out what's coming and making the correct adjustments. Now, maybe the Giants aren't there yet with Dart in this offense with those play calls as far as tacking those things on there, but I'll just say like if I'm if I'm standing there behind an offensive line and I'm one of 11 guys on the field and I'm seeing and I'm and and I'm standing there scanning the full field, even if the play is going to the left, you do have the responsibility of understanding what the full field looks like and maybe they're single coverage with no safety on the right to Calvin Austin and maybe you find a different uh solution there. Now, obviously Tyrone Tracy Jr. completely whiffing almost looked like maybe the protection breakdown was either nobody assigned Tracy to that and therefore he didn't have the responsibility because it almost looks like he starts to run out onto his right um to try to you know be a pass catcher and then he sees the blitz coming and kind of jumps back inside. So maybe the adjustment or the problem there was that Dart and Hudson or andor Hudson did not assign Tracy to that protection and therefore that's the breakdown. But I just think overall this is not what you want to see obviously right from Dart and from this offense. It's sloppy. Um especially when it comes to getting your first team quarterback hit this significantly, this directly, this hard. Um, Dart obviously upset that he's getting sent to the tent and says that he feels like it happens every time. He's still trying to wrap his head around it. But if you saw it live and Dart's physical reaction to the play, you know, Harbaugh said he had his win knocked out of him. Dart was asked if he had the win knocked out of him. He didn't really answer in the affirmative. He kind of just said, "The guy hit me hard." Um, so you know, I think the Giants, what they have to look at here is you still clearly need this offense and this quarterback to get more work, especially in the passing game, but you have to be smart about how you do it. And obviously, they need to uh put themselves Dart needs to put himself into better position. Now, you saw the other side of the Jackson Dart experience, which we like, which is he comes back onto the field. Harbaugh said he had no second-guing or hesitance putting him back on because he said he he was quote fine. And then Dart on that third down in the red zone, makes that 15 yard touchdown pass to Malachi Fields. Um, you know, holds the ball again, feels the pressure, but escapes out to the left, throws it up to his big bodied um wide receiver out of Notre Dame who makes goes up and makes the catch over a linebacker. Um, you know, that was against the second team defense. The first uh series was against the first team defense and the Giants got down there due to a 40 yard screen pass from Jameus Winston to Devin Singleary. I didn't see it in the first couple plays. I saw once or twice, but it's really important to see him in the run game and see how he fares from that standpoint, especially against their first team. Is is that what you're leaning towards right now heading into this this week? No joint practices with the Chiefs obviously, but will you uh will you sprinkle in some starters or maybe give them a series or two? >> Yeah, I've been saying that the last 2 weeks the healthy starters are going to play in week two. >> Do you know about how long? >> Not yet, no. >> Greg Auman. >> Hey Todd, I I know in preseason so much is is when you come in and who you're with, who you're up against. With with Browning in his back, is there a reasonable think he might be in play to to play at home against the Chiefs or is that something you're you're more concerned about? >> We're hopeful. I'll see I'll see how he comes along during the week. >> Okay, Todd, thank you. >> Yeah. >> Anyone else? Good. Okay, that's all. Thanks, coach.

Yeah. >> Can you take me through the touchdown? Don, >> you got a smile to you tonight. title: Nick Sirianni on Preseason Loss to Baltimore Raven
