title: Robert Saleh on the Pass Game, Carmona & Injury Updates | Press Conference
text: Yeah, so we have every day. Today was a little bit more extended just because we're the time of practice gave an opportunity to get in the chill box cool their core temperatures down so we could finish our practice strong. >> Is there value to practicing in game time type of heat and humidity? >> I think there is, you know, acclimate yourself to this weather. We I mean the first couple weeks of September you don't know what the heck you're going to get. It could be 90° with 90% humidity. Could be a cool fall day in the upper Midwest. So um you just don't know. >> What what about the practice situation? I don't want to use the word panic but maybe concern do you think that there could be a a better performance by them? >> What? >> Specifically your >> Yeah, you know, that's just it's just continuing the rep rep what we're asking them to to accomplish understanding formations. You know, you're not game planning so you're not really recognizing formations, recognizing tendencies as we go but but at the same time um uh just from a man coverage standpoint being able to win your one-on-ones when those one-on-ones are presented. Um you know, I'm there's never panic but is there urgency? There's always urgency from the from the second we stepped on the football field till the day the season's over there's going to be urgency to try to get better. >> What what you've seen as of late would you say the urgency needs to >> It's all it's If if you're waiting till now to pick up your urgency you're already late. So our guys have been working relentlessly. I know we do drills every week every day. Um it's just taking the drill work to the practice field from indoor to teamwork to the game day and uh just trying to find a ways to hone in on your craft. >> After maybe having more time to kind of look back at the film and the work that the 49ers did what do you feel like you held up across the board against a good team like that? >> Uh for the week? >> Right. >> Yeah, I you know, I've said it I think I said it the last time. I'm I'm I thought we had a a really productive week. Um I I felt like the game was a continuation of what we we we we accomplished on the line of scrimmages. Um when we practice against them Tuesday we felt like the run game both offensively and defensively were very very good. And it continued into the game. I thought we dominated the run game on both sides of the ball and uh and so that was a very encouraging thing. Now from a from a pass game standpoint, the efficiency on offense, the um the production on defense, that needs to improve. >> How does your fast and violent manifest itself in the passing game? If that's the philosophy, how do you use that to get better on your offense and defense this year? >> Um you know what? It's from a from a speed standpoint, it's operating at a very high level in terms of your uh getting getting up getting off the ball. Um getting to the top of your routes. Uh quarterback working through his progressions. Uh and operating at a speed that uh that that is unmatched in terms of uh the way everyone is operating. And then violently, obviously when you got the ball in your hands, the easy thing to say is you drop step, you run through tackles, you do all that good stuff, but you know, it's violently jumping off the ball as a receiver to to to make a a DB feel your speed. It's violently getting to the top of your route and putting your foot in the ground and coming back to the ball. It's there's there it's violently getting your hands out there to go catch the football. There's there's violence just isn't about contact. It's about the urgency and the strain at which you operate and uh um so that's how it applies to offense. Uh little by little, you know, like I said, it's got to get better. I felt like we saw it in both run games offensively and defensively off the line of scrimmage, the strain in our double teams, the strain getting off blocks, uh jumping off the ball both offensively and defensively and uh uh uh operating on the opponent's side of the line of scrimmage, but uh in the pass game on both sides of the ball it needs to get better. >> You used to see offensive line coaches utilize sleds with their guys a lot. Carmen talked about uh for one thing it makes them inefficient and he can do a lot more, but also guys with their hands on other guys it's it's a lot more realistic in a lot of ways. Um >> How uncommon do you think that is around the league where you've been with other guys? Um and and what do you think of his philosophy in it? >> Um I think anytime I don't know if you've noticed like the structure of our practices, we we try to structure practice to to create as many real situations as possible. Very little seven-on-seven, even though we did a quick nine-play seven-on-seven period today. Very little one-on-ones, very little It's but it's a lot of move You see the clock is moving. You see us in first, second, third down being very random uh with our practice and how we operate. And it's all by design because that's what football is. Football is very random. Football is very unpredictable. And there it's not uncommon on the second half of practice to for me to just throw the guys out there in a random situation and say, "Let's go play football." Uh and deviate from the from the uh uh script. But, to answer your question, all our drills I encourage all our coaches to constantly put them in real situations that are more football-like. It's not we're not running a combine and individual. We're running you know, you're you know you're playing a team that's going to B-block on the backside and work up a double team. Then as a linebacker, I should be recognizing those B-blocks. As a D-lineman, I should be playing those B-blocks in individual. You should be practicing what you're about to go get. And the best way to simulate that is with people. >> I know you're not game planning, you know, in any of the preseason games. You're just kind of holding your stuff. But, how much do you practice and the tendencies of what the opponent will do while you're out there? >> Tendencies, no. Uh but structure, you know, like you like Seattle's going to come in. We're just going to familiarize our guys with regards to the structure that they're going to see. But, as far as D&D tendencies and and all that stuff, it's uh we're still working on us. We're still working on our fundamentals. And and to be honest, once we get the kickoff like um on game day, it was probably the most vanilla offense and defense that you're going to get. Try not to show our hand with regards to what we can what we're capable of on on both sides of the ball. >> Carmona on the rise so to speak. Can you tell us a little bit about where Wilson and Slater stand and what they're doing? >> They're they're still part of the competition. Does Carmona Carmona has he grabbed the inside track? I'd say he has. But at the same time it's it's nowhere near over. Carmona's done a great job like I said with communicating, playing with great violence, great strain. Is he still a rookie making rookie mistakes, rookie fundamentals? Sure, but but at the same time he's doing everything he can to like I said last time we spoke he's he put his foot in the door and he's doing everything he can to throw a shoulder through it. >> A couple more seasons of Hard Knocks coming out this year. What do you most remember from your time with that show? Did you enjoy that? >> I love Hard Knocks. >> [laughter] >> You know, they were it was [clears throat] good. You know, it's I I kicked and screamed like a baby trying to keep them out but but at the same time once they got there they're they're awesome to work with. They really are and I'm not just saying that. They they were not invasive. They tried to work with you and they tried to show your team in a great light and so having done it before you know, it's it's really it gets to the point you don't even notice that they're there. >> Last two Paul and Terry. >> Any update on some of the guys that had injuries out of the game like Harold or Cannick? >> Yeah, Harold and Cannick unfortunately will be done for the season. Harold with his ACL, Cannick Cannick with torn pec. Everyone else just minor aches and bruises. Tony didn't practice today just dealing with a sore foot. Hopefully get him back Monday. Same thing with Nick Singleton. Jacob Martin same thing. So there was a couple of guys that were having a little bit of a little bit of soreness plus the travel. Just felt like it'd be good to give them a give them a quick break and get them back going on Monday. >> The I didn't see that happen. He played against >> That was on special teams. >> Okay. >> It was like his only rep. >> Just a fluky play. >> Yeah, just a fluky play. >> Yeah. >> Got his arm out there and it ripped on him. >> We've had officials out a ton. Are they all NFL guys and have the rules changed as to how much access you get to them? >> No, you know what? So, the the NFL guys are we'll have them here for Seattle. We'll also have them here for Chicago, but the the gentlemen you see out here are kind of in-line guys. So, college, high school here to just work on their craft and so we just have them out here. They throw their flags, they jot down what they see, and then we get a report every day to try to try to educate our guys. >> Does the league help facilitate that or is that all you guys? >> That's that's our that's the organization.

title: Kevin Winston Jr., Austin Schlottmann & Cody Barton at Titans Camp | Tennessee Titans
text: It was really good. You know, we got presented a lot of things from the 49ers offense, a lot of different looks, a lot of different motions, things like that, and we got to see where we were where we are at this point right now. And I think we learned a lot of things from that game, and I think we're going to be good heading forward. >> What do you feel like you are What do you feel like you guys are at this moment? >> Uh I think what we wanted to go out there and play fast and physical. I think we did that. Obviously, we got to clean up some areas within the secondary, clean up the things some things, but I'm pretty really happy where we're at, but we got a lot of things to improve, and we expected that, but we got to make sure we we nip it in the bud and all those things. >> How do you feel the communication is coming between yourself and one of the back of the place and relaying the signals? >> I think we're really good on that aspect. Uh come to Every time I come out here, what I hear in the meeting room, I make sure to deliver it to Flat and Taylor every time we get out here. So, I make sure even on the field, I alert things ahead of time to them to make sure that's what the corner wants. You know, they really want to just want to make sure to depend on the safety to make sure we can get them aligned and play fast. So, me and Imani Hooker put that on our plate, and we make sure to take care of them in that aspect. >> What's the challenge playing fast and physical when your job title is just playing safety? You're supposed to be the last line of defense. How do you not over pursue to what you're doing out there? >> I mean, it's reading your keys. A lot of times, if Malcolm Manny always If you have your eyes in the right spot right place, you know, you can read run pass easy, and you know, you do that then from there, do your job and do it fast and physical. And that's how It's really just knowing within your job, knowing where your people are all around you, and then reading your right keys, and that allows you to just play as fast as you want. >> How's Cordell uh in in the middle of that? A lot of the scrimmage stuff was with him. How How is he reacting to that, and how is he kind of been sensitive? >> Yeah, he he's great. You know, nothing changed with him. He was You know, he's very poised in the moment, you know. Cordell's a great player, and he's a vet. He's been doing it for a long time, and he You know, I'm I'm excited for Cordell, and he's only going to get better from now on. >> The staff said you guys have been working or continuing to work on the point of attack defensive plays. What What is working that? How How do you work that? >> I mean, you could work it on the sideline with in the individuals, but it's really just in practice when we get a chance to make a play on the ball, make sure we finish through, see through the hands, finish it whether that's interception or getting the ball out. And that's That's where we got to work at it. We get live times, it gets our wide receivers who are going to give us good looks great looks on, you know, making plays on the ball and we got to make sure we finish through the through the hands every time. >> When you're in a position where you can get a lot of contact, how difficult is it when you're used to practicing where you're not having a background and all of a sudden >> Yeah, it's difficult, you know, going from, you know, thudding to live. I mean, everybody talks about how how different it really is and it is, but I think when you train yourself with your angles and how you pursue guys, having the right leverage on guys and just getting used to communicating that is when you get out there and you're going full speed, and you know, from what I've experienced, you kind of allow it to be second nature because you've been training your body, put yourself in the right position, but when you get out there and get live, that's why I'm glad we're all playing in the preseason games cuz we're getting those live looks, knocking off the dust on our tackling, and that's where, you know, come game one, we should be ready to go full in and make all our tackles. >> How much did you see the battle up for Jaylen and what did you kind of tell him as he But Jaylen here, how much did you take to see the battle walk and then what did you tell him as far as what's ahead? >> Yeah, yeah, I'm praying for Jaylen. I talked to him about, you know, having went through the same thing. I told him, you know, he's going to be just fine. You know, I know he's a I know Jaylen as a person. I told him, you know, I'm praying for him and best of luck with anything. I talked to him even before anything happened, you know, I just just wishing the best and making sure he keeps his head high. We'll have him around all the time, but he's going to come back better than ever. You know, a lot of times with these ACL injuries, when you're dealing with guys that really care about their bodies and take care of themselves, they always come back stronger and I'm feeling that myself, so I'm excited for Jaylen and I'm praying for him as well. >> What do you think about Josh who's wearing don't hit me jersey and delivering the biggest hit of practice? >> You know, I mean, I I can't I don't know what to say about it, but I, you know, he's physical. You know, we know that about Josh and we know that with all due respect. I mean, if he he he wanted to hit, so clearly he's doing just fine, but I'm excited for Josh and I feel like he's, you know, he's getting to the point where he's getting real healthy, clearly delivering that hit, but I'm excited for Josh, great player. >> What do you think the offense thought? >> I'm not I'm not sure what they thought about it. I mean, they, you know, they like the physicality as well, so I'm like they're probably happy that Jaylen Josh was getting back and hit hitting people. >> Is it sometimes I mean, sometimes though where it's letting letting them everybody know you're there without delivering, I guess, too much of a hit. >> Yeah, I mean, it it's it's hard it's hard. You know, you talking about just how you how you hit guys? In practice, it's hard, you know, trying to train yourself to pull back pull off, but I think in certain areas when you're playing fast, it's hard to, you know, find the fine area, but as a as, you know, as a team we got to take care of our guys and make sure we don't hurt anybody in practice, but Uh when I play I mean, I was I was reading front side. Cam seen him turn on the other side. I played ball the whole time. I didn't even see we me and Alec talked about it. Soon as the as soon as practice was over, I ran in to find him to make sure he was fine, but we both talked about it. He was actually in the in the building watching the clip to see what happened. So, you know, he's hard on himself, but I was actually seeing ball the whole time. I played ball, went to go for the interception, came down with it, but, you know, I don't I don't want to see Alec go down like that, but I didn't see him on that play, but, you know, I'm glad Alec's doing just fine now. >> Saleh had mentioned how he builds the practices to resemble more like game-like situations. How much do you feel that's benefited you so far? I mean, as a DB, I know one-on-ones, the traditional ones, are kind of stacked against you, but I would imagine when you get your work in. What do you think of not having as many one-on-ones? >> Uh I think when you talk about one-on-ones, I think we get Saleh makes sure we get that we get that in 7-on-7. We get that in in when you you get one-on-ones all the time when you're actually going live in 11-on-11. We man coverage is wherever that is and we're getting the feel of playing to our leverage, playing to where knowing where our help is. If we have a low hole, if we don't, and we learn we get a lot of one-on-ones through that, but we have periods where we're doing straight one-on-ones and straight man coverage. So, I think we get that in there regardless of, you know, whether we have the actual period of one-on-ones and we get it all at once cuz a lot of times you do one-on-ones, it's only one guy going at a time, two guys going at a time, but when we make sure we get those man plays, we got a whole defense going all all together. >> And and how about the way he structures practice to resemble game situations? >> Yeah, it's been great for us. I mean, a lot of guys have been very healthy to this point and we know we've been focused on building a callus for the season and making sure we're ready to be healthy throughout the season and everybody's built for the you know the hard beat up that the season will have on you and I think it's been great for us. >> What do you think Nick's done so far? Singleton? >> Yeah, he's been great. You know, I've known I've known Nick I've known him since we you know first got to Penn State, but he's been doing really good and I'm I'm happy to see him out there making these big runs and you know doing what he does, but it's it's good to see him back out there and I'm happy I'm happy for Nick and excited to have him on the team. >> I've been able to go through an extra scoring drive or not. >> Um yeah, I think that's always good. That's always like my mindset. It's always like let's go put a 95-yard drive together. Like nobody like you're not supposed to do that. Like we might as well we might as well go out here and do it. Like let's go. That's kind of what I always say when we go in the huddle when we're in that situation and uh I mean it just it starts with getting the first down and then you get a first down and you're in the field and your whole playbook kind of opens up and um you just got to execute. >> I know he's not been declared the winner yet, but what are you seeing out of Carmota that gives you a good good feeling that he may be ready to go? >> Yeah, um Fernando's been doing a good job. He's uh he plays with a lot of a lot of intensity, a lot of good effort. Um him along with all of us we can all clean up some technique stuff. Um that's always the case especially this time of year. Um but yeah, I think he's been doing a good job. >> To clarify, did you guys use more sleds in OTAs than >> Uh we didn't No, we didn't use any sleds. >> If you put in in college and I don't know if you had somebody before Carmody >> Yeah. >> with the Giants. Did you use more or anything in the philosophy of not using them? >> Um yes in college. Um my rookie year um with Denver back in 2018 we used them a little bit. Um but since then I haven't I've been with coaches that that don't don't really care to use them. I think there's a certain aspect like blocking guys when it's a real body who's moving uh as opposed to like a sled that's fixed and sitting still. Um I think it's It's bit different. It's good for like foot drive and being able to just fit it and and run run off the ball. Um but I think there's there's definitely benefits to both. Um I kind of like the idea of blocking a moving person where they're like we have pads on, they don't have to hold a bag, they can just like get in a D-line stance and come off the ball. >> Are you guys ready to go pull them out for for solo work or do you just not >> Sleds? Um I don't think so. Yeah. >> Appreciate it. You uh you haven't been around uh Pete that long, but uh he got an extension I guess last week. >> How happy were you to see that and what maybe like the kind of What's the conversation like in the O-line room when a guy gets pulled over like >> Yeah. Um I thought that was awesome. I think he's super deserving of of everything he got and probably more. Um Pete's a great dude, a great player. Um really fun to play next to. Um And like he doesn't like to talk about it. He's super humble guy. He's just like we he doesn't want to bring it up in the O-line room. It's just we're moving on and we're we're on to football just like any normal day, but uh we were definitely fired up for him. >> Looking forward to them in Dallas on >> Looking forward to the Lions. Going to be fun. Uh big competition, you know, they're the former world champs, so um you know, the joint practice and I think it's in a week or a little over a week or no, less than a week, excuse me. It's going to be fun. >> What's What's uh what What kind of a shift is there after you [snorts] play a game or after a week with uh competing against another team as far as how you know what you got to do this, got to do this to keep getting better? How do you gauge a shift in in thinking here after after a week of that? >> Yeah, I mean it's just look at the film, you look at it from joint practice, right? It's It's different too cuz you go from a joint practice and then 48 hours later you're playing a game versus in season it's you're not going to go to a hard practice on a Friday like that and play Sunday. But anyway, you just look at the film from joint practice, see the things they like to do, um make your corrections there, and then going into the game, same thing, you know what I mean? After watching the tape, we watched it this morning. And uh you know, you make some tweaks here and there and then today practice is for those those kind of things, you know what I mean? Some adjustments you make or or whatever it is. >> What's the With this defense, you know, you played in it before. Is it unique like how much stress it puts on you guys as far as the coverage perspective is concerned, you guys meaning the linebackers? >> Yeah, but that's also why the rush and coverage go hand-in-hand, you know what I mean? When those front four rush and hum, the ball's got to come out a little quicker, but um you know, there is some stress particularly on the outsides. Um and that's just when the when the quarterback throws it up, you want those the corners to make the 50/50 balls. >> What's happened for you guys >> Say it again. >> linebackers >> Yeah, there's there's certain certain calls that we make where the linebackers have, you know, care responsibility and you could be matched up on a on a receiver who's fast, you know what I mean? So, there's When you go into each call, if you know your issue and you're ahead of it, it's not as bad, but if you're if you're late on your issues or late on your pre-snap stuff, then you're going to be, you know, caught behind chasing. You can give a big play. >> What was the tone from coaches about coverage generally giving up 12 or 14 to to a third-string quarterback? I think you guys probably expected to play better. >> Yeah, just we got to tighten it up. You know, there's there's certain certain I mean, depending on what call we're in, there's certain techniques we can do better and um you know, whatever it was, there's just just overall we just got to tighten it up. >> What does that Can you be a little more specific on what you mean by "tightening up" means >> I mean, it comes down to your to your footwork, your technique depending on the call, like I said, and just you know, doing your 1/11th in that call and then the plays come to you. That's what What I mean when I tighten up, I just mean it kind of covers all of it, you know.

title: Mike Macdonald: "We're Going To Learn A Lot From This Game" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Okay. Um, first of all, I want to shout out the twelves. I mean, that's the most people I ever seen at a preseason game. So, uh, we owe we owe them a better performance to say the least. But, uh, I just told I told the team it's, um, we're going to learn a lot from this game. Whether, you know, take the result out of it. Obviously, it's disappointing to lose the game. Anytime you line up in anything competitively, we're trying to win. But, um, right now, our process needs to improve. That's really the biggest takeaway is um on really in both phases on offense and defense our operation is uh not up to par and how we're finishing plays is not up to par. So uh that'll be a focus moving forward, but it's it's good to know. You know, I'm glad we know now on the things we need to be able to do to take our uh our team to the next level. And um and we have a great opportunity to go to go figure it out. You know, we got a big week coming up. uh couple couple great practices opportunities and then um and then off to Tennessee we go have a great practice and and play another great game and and uh take you know and move forward. So that's where we're at. >> You see the operation wasn't up to your standard. What do you mean? Um just all all the things how you know how we get calls in, how we take the line, uh how we motion, how we shift, how we get lined up on defense, how we communicate, uh all those things need to take a uh a very big jump very quickly. So, uh but it's good to know now we know it. So, let's go get it. >> Just ask you about Ste contract. I mean, obviously we all know he's a great player, but what why is he so important to what you have done and what you want to do in the future? Well, I mean, Spoon Spoon is all the things. He's a He's a great person. He's a great football player. Uh he's a great teammate. He's a great leader. Those are the guys we want to be here. It's it's kind of similar to Jack. It's like these are these are foundational people to to our to our to our team. And I'm I'm extremely excited to get that um foundation laid, you know, where we know Spoon's going to be here for the long haul. and and and we're also excited for the opportunity to to reward him. You know, that this is a contract that we feel like he's earned and we should celebrate it as well. But it's also really exciting to know that we've we have foundational players that are going to be part of our team here for a long time. >> He was one of the guys when you said, you know, the first phase of OTAAS, some of the veteran guys didn't need to be there. He was there day one. >> Yeah. >> He's out practicing like a maniac while he's still waiting to get a deal done. Like what does that tell you about him? >> Oh, well that's that paints a great picture, John. like he um he's just infectious and he loves the game. You know, we were talking today and he's just, you know, people would hopefully he doesn't mind me sharing this, but people would talk to him about um you know, ask him why he does what why he's doing what he's doing. He's like, "Yeah, I love I love the game of football and there's a season to get ready for, you know, he kind of keeps the main thing the main thing without getting distracted by all the the extra stuff." Uh he also probably feels, you know, he's also a great teammate. you know, he just wants to be there for the guys and and uh how our team plays is important to him, which is which is uh really cool. >> He closes out the NFC championship game, those two pass breakups and then the slot blitzes were just insane in the Super Bowl. >> What how like certain players just have a knack for coming up the biggest moments? What is it about him that allows him to do that? >> Well, I think it's his relentless attitude about like the details. doesn't matter the situation, he's playing it at at, you know, at at top speed, top intent. That's how we want our football team to operate, you know. I mean, uh there are plays in earlier in the game in the NFC game that Spoon um probably could have played better, but like the mentality to just attack the next play all the time is uh is probably what makes it so special. And then in both those plays, you know, they're both are extended plays where, you know, I think we're in man coverage on both of them to be able to, you know, to guard your man for that amount of time relentlessly is is uh I mean, it's legendary type stuff. And then, you know, in terms of how he plays nickel position on early downs and the things he did in the Super Bowl are are some of the some of the things that make him special as well. >> I think you may have had a comment on the radio after the Super Bowl about like the impact he had on the Super Bowl as a Blitzer. like does that make you feel like maybe you should use him more in that role? >> Yes. >> Yes. Yeah. It's it's uh he's a he's a great corner and he's a great nickel and when when Nick's available, Nick's also a great nickel and so, you know, it's it's a great it's a great problem to have as a as a coach that, you know, how do you deploy your people to have success? But, um, Spoon is very, I mean, all all those instincts about timing and, you know, even even beating guards, you know, setting them up and beating backs and one-on-one pass situations is uh, you know, it's not it's not common for those for that skill set. >> Looked like he jumped about 8 ft in the air to celebrate after the long punt return. >> Yeah. Today, >> yeah, >> we were trying to get a penalty. We were trying to get a celebration penalty, but I was a little disappointed that, you know, we could be we could bring some more uh some energy to to the celebrations. >> To Bob's point, like Ernest Jones was out celebrating. A lot of guys weren't playing seemed very into the game. Does that tell you something about those guys? >> Yeah, I was excited. You know, and and the guys playing like you know, we we got to we have to play with more urgency. take take the from the when the ball was snapped to like when the ball is over the play is over but like how we finish the play to the op the whole operation needs to improve and the players are responsible for that as well. It's not this isn't like a a comment on our coaches or anything. It's it's the whole team and so and to do that that provides energy. That's how you stack plays you know that's how you kind of get out of a rut is by you know falling back on those on those like core fundamentals those core principles of how we're going to operate as a football team. So that didn't happen today. That's probably the most disappointing thing. >> Would you really want a penalty? >> Uh, kind of. Yeah. >> Why? >> I mean that I just wanted the guy I wanted the guys to feel the energy and kind of like we did last year like it was I think we got an interception or something and I think everybody was in uniform that maybe I don't I don't know. I probably should know the rules better. >> Mike with um Tyrie. You said early in camp that, you know, you'd like to find a way to get him involved a little bit more and it seemed like he had one of those games that shows he's ever >> Yeah, we're a little banged up at inside backer right now. So, Tide uh played probably more than we bargain for, but um played a probably he he's the best player on the field on defense today for sure. So, that was uh that was cool to see. >> What initial thought on how the two quarterbacks played? >> Um good enough to put up seven points. you know, got to put up more points. We need to operate better. Uh there's some good things. There's there's going to be a lot of there's going to be like it's so great to have tape against another team now like in in a real in a different type of setting where the pass rush is live, you know, um you're up against the play clock, you know, there's there's penalty, all these different things that you'd have to be able to play out uh are great learning experiences for everybody, quarterbacks included. >> Ju talked to us a couple days about being more decisive as his key. Yeah. >> How do you think he was tonight? He seemed to hold on to the ball. >> Uh there were spots, you know, I got we got to see if you know what the things that he that he was seeing, but um I think the whole thing just needs just whole thing just let's go take another step, you know. Um you know, was it there? Let's let's encourage him to go rip it. I think that I think some great things that Jaylen did was extend plays with his legs. Um something that uh has been a point of emphasis with him that he's just that he's really uh it's great to see him do that today. That really helped us. >> Well, Tory Foster's a guy has had a strong camp. Good to see when a player can do that and carry it in. >> Yeah. Yeah, for sure. Yeah. Happy for Montoy. Um all the things you felt in camp, you felt uh felt today during the game. >> We haven't seen Jaylen take off and run a whole lot like this summer in practices. It sounds like that's some Are you saying that's something you wanted to encourage him to do more? >> Yeah. And like it's Hey, you know, there's the play doesn't have to end if you're if there's nobody to throw in with your progressions. Like >> you're allowed to extend the play. You know, it's up to you on how long the play goes. You had Adam and Dury doing the play calling tonight. >> Yeah, AD called the game, did a good job. Um, >> what did that afford you? What did you see differently or what are you able to glean from a >> Um, you know, I think it was best for us right now for him for him to call. It's great experience for AD. Uh, he's called the majority of camp up to this point. Um, he's done a phenomenal job throughout camp. He really has. He's he's we've had a ton of call up periods. Um he's on the details. He's thinking thinking um just doing a lot of great stuff honestly. So um but at some point I got I got to get ready to call game two. So I think I think I'll probably call next week. >> Clark, do you get a chance call plays to see him running? >> Did some good things. Did some good things. um some things off the top of my head that I know that we want to talk about and improve, but uh again, he he's he's a great example of, hey, this is your first experience playing a game, you know, in a loud environment where we have to communicate, you know, the communication needs to improve on. Dave, I think that's a wakeup call to our guys of, you know, examples of So, shout out to the 12 for being loud and showing our guys that we got to be able to communicate better, but um great great first experience for him. He's going to learn from it. >> Anything else? >> Okay. Thank you. Encourage you.

title: Jalen Milroe: "There Are So Many Opportunities To Grow" | Seattle Seahawks
text: What's up? It was good to be back on the field, especially at home to start the the year off being around the guys and especially for us, you know, going through the training camp, competing against each other. It's an opportunity for us to go and compete against somebody else. So, it's it's a lot of fun. >> [snorts] >> Um it's good to feel the the energy from our fans, especially just being game one of preseason. So, I'm excited for the season to keep on rolling and we're getting closer to our first game. >> You told us a couple days ago your decisiveness is the key to you being decisive to you. How do you think that went for you tonight? >> Yeah, I think every play that I have the ball in my hands is all about being decisive, um trusting in in the game plan, trusting in um coach Flurry or whatever play call he has and putting our offense in the best position to be successful. And so, I think that was key throughout the whole game. And of course, like this is a preseason game number one is for, like there's always things we can clean up, there's always things we can do positive and even if we came out victorious, there's things that we can improve on, get better at. And so, that's the exciting part about preseason and getting our opportunity to play um today. And so, uh the biggest thing just to build on today and build on and going into our next opponent. >> Especially in the first half, you took off running a few times, you got some good gains. Was that Was that kind of an emphasis to want to try to do that in this game at all or just >> Not necessarily. I think every time I have the ball in my hands it's all about putting our offense in the best position to win. And whether it's passing, whether it's running, whether it's handing the ball off, so many areas to our offense that uh can can beat the defense. And so, um every opportunity we have to move the chains, we're going to do it in unique ways and um that was just one one way to do it. >> What's Brian Flurry like in a game? How does he give you feedback? >> Yeah, um I think what's unique about having your play call on the field you can get direct um dialogue as far as what he's saying, um plays that are going to set up during a drive, you know, of course we have the iPads where able to see exactly what coverage, you know, structure and things that they can have and then the set up plays and so it's the communication of moving forward, right? Like you of course you watch the tape of what exactly went down on that drive. So now it's the moving forward aspect of looking at how we can attack the defense. >> How did the speed of the game feel today versus last year and were you pleased with how you were able to use your legs to scramble? >> Um never pleased, you know, of course. Um there's so many opportunities to grow um as a quarterback um in this league and so um I think for all of us in the locker room it's like how can we be better than we were this weekend and um today was a great opportunity for us to put in a display um uh the hard work that we've been doing during the week and it's so of course we were going to learn and grow and get better. >> What role can a quarterback take in terms of the team finishing in the red zone without pressing? >> Yeah. Um I think that's key. I think when you're in the red zone we need to come out with points, you know, whether it's a field goal or whether it's a touchdown. Coming out with points is so important, especially helping our defense out um and putting putting points on the board is so important, you know, it's going to be a critical when we play tougher opponents, you know, when we're um trailing in the game whether we're uh in in the lead. It's just really just finishing drives. So I think that's another emphasis for us is finishing drives. >> Montrell Foster has been a really good player in camp all summer. Now he's leading receiver in this game. Just what have you seen from him since you got here? >> I think a growth mindset. Um a mindset to grow each and every day that he has opportunity to be on the field. Um I think also the approach that he takes whether it's preparing, um whether it's playing different positions, X to Z, at F, like being versatile so coach can use him on the field. And so I think that's something that um I applaud him on is that he's been versatile around the field and playing all positions. >> Jay, have you ever played in a game like that where the quarterbacks were rotating that way rather than it just being one guy playing for a certain amount of time [snorts] and then the other one coming in? And what were your thoughts on that? >> Um I think as a backup you have to be prepared and ready to go at at any at any point. Um, this is not my first time being a backup and so I think reps are so important for me and Drew. Um, and for any guy that's a backup because in the league, you know, the starter gets majority of the reps. So as many reps that we can get as much as possible is going to prepare us and help us out for whenever the opportunity comes that we play in the game and so um, I don't see it as a negative. I think this is an opportunity for us to get reps and preseason is big for us because during the season once you have established starter, you know, your your your reps are cut short. >> You told us the other day how close you are with Terryon and you hoped he was going to come here and now now it looks like it's going to happen. Have you been able to talk to him since then at all and what are your thoughts on that? >> Of course. Yeah, of course. That's that's my dog and I'm very happy that he's going to be a Seahawk. Um, I think now it's just showing him the way of how we do things and I think that's now the move forward process, you know, the process was trying to figure out where he was going to go. So now he's a Hawk and so we're just going to emphasize what we do as you know, as being here in Seattle and emphasizing our theme, our mottoes and our team mission and goals and so now it's a running forward mentality with having him a part of our team. >> Jaylen, what do you think people should know about Terryon? >> I think >> [sighs] >> I think number one is that he's committed. Um, when he has goals set for him he wants to achieve them and he's going to put his all into everything he puts into it. Um, this is someone that's really care about his teammates. Um, he's really unique as far as what he can do on the field. Um, and he's going to really love the culture that we have here because it's similar to the vibe that we had when we was in college. >> How is he going through all this? >> Doing good. He's doing good. Um, he's excited for the opportunity and he's really going to seize it when he gets here. >> Anything else? >> Thank you, sir. >> Thanks, Jaylen.

title: Montorie Foster Jr.: "Every Time I Play, I Play To A Standard" | Seattle Seahawks
text: On that touchdown, did you know when you turned around the ball was going to be right on you like that? >> Yeah, I did actually. Um, you know, it was kind of tight coverage a little bit, so and it was a tight window, too. Uh, shout out to Drew, but um, you know, on that plant, I knew the ball was going to be right there, so I was just ready for it. >> Did that linebacker tip it? Did it change direction at all? >> He almost tipped it. It was It was super close, but you know, I was just ready for the moment and then made the play, so definitely. >> You've had a good camp up to this point. How like rewarding is it to then have it carry over into game action and then show you can do it in the game? >> Yeah, definitely, man. It's been great. Um, every time I play, I play to a standard and it don't matter if I'm, you know, playing good or bad. Like my standard is my standard. I go out there every day and just try to put my best foot forward every day and put forth the effort, go block, do the little things and, you know, let everything else take care of itself. >> How close were you to that second one that Drew just over threw on on the sideline? >> Yeah, I was close, man. I feel like, um, you know, watching the tape on the sideline, um, I could have did a better part of just digging out my route. Um, I looked a little bit too early, so you know, that's something that I can clean up in my game, um, which I will do next game. >> How much are these next couple weeks you feel like special teams will be big for you to try to get a chance to show what you can do there as well? >> Yeah, definitely, man. Like every time I go out on that field, like whatever's on my plate, you know, I'm just going to take care of whatever I got to do, so um, I can't wait to get more opportunities in special teams to show that I can do that, too, as well. >> I'm curious, you you get dropped in here late last year joining the practice squad and following along for the run and everything. I know you had the social media stuff kind of following your journey with everything to now all of a sudden be out there contributing a little bit. What does that kind of mean to you? >> Yeah, it means everything, man. Um, you know, I was back at home, shoot, for 16 weeks and, you know, it was it was tough, man. It was times where, you know, I wanted to give up and just, you know, get a regular job, but um, I stayed at it. Um, my dad told me cream always rise to the top and just to stay faithful and I just kept working and you know, I'm now I'm I'm here today. Yeah, I was I was doing a lot of things, man. I was teaching substitute teaching at my high school. I actually got my real estate license too while I was back at home and then I was training little kids in football too as well just to give back to the game. >> As a undrafted guy coming in it's a tough road to go. When you got hurt in camp and got on injured list like did you wonder was that your only opportunity? >> Um, yeah, I had no idea, man. You know, I know I had some teams, you know, in the past that you know, before the pre-draft process call me and stuff, but you know, you never know in this business because you know, it's the 1% of the 1% so you know, it's all about faith and timing and you know, luckily I was on God's timing. >> When did When were you teaching and doing real estate? >> Uh, when I went back home. So, I would say probably in like September. >> Okay. Okay, I'm sorry. >> Yeah, September of last year. >> And what were you teaching? >> Subjects as a substitute teacher just filling in really. I had I want to say freshmen and juniors in high school. So, that's what I was dealing with so far. Um, I had a Latin class. So, I went to Saint Anne's. So, we I didn't I don't know any Latin so at all. So, you know, I was just like, man, do y'all homework and I'll just be here and watching y'all and you know, they was all good from there. >> No lesson plan. >> Yeah, no lesson plan not at all. >> You got it. >> Thanks for the interview. >> All right, thank you. Yeah.

title: Drew Lock: "The Key Takeaway Is To Finish In The Red Zone" | Seattle Seahawks
text: what's going on. >> Drew, what did you like about the opening drive? >> Um, yeah. Uh, finishing in the red zone was probably the plus there. Um, good put together, good set of plays. Um, move the ball well, ran the ball well. Guys got the ball in their hands, they made plays with it. Montour had a great catch in the end zone and, uh, just we we finished. Um, I think that's the key takeaway or what we need to work on is just finishing in the red zone. >> There had to be a lot of trust in that throw. He didn't turn around and see that ball. So, it's almost gone. >> Yeah. Um, when you're that, you know, when you're that tight, um, down there in the red zone, there's, you know, not a lot of time for, you know, patting the ball and seeing guys come out of breaks. Um, you know, we've obviously practiced that play before and um built some built some good chemistry on it and you know, I trust him on Tori and he made a great catch. >> Seems like he makes at least one play every day. What have you thought of this summer? He said, >> "Yeah, he should have made two today if I don't overthrow him on that uh ball on the left sideline. Um, he's had a great summer." He's had a great summer. I think I said it, I forgot who I was saying it to, but you know, the journey he's been on from the previous year till now, man, he's he's light years away from where he was, and he's been fantastic for us. Makes great plays, explosive with the ball in his hand, reliable, he's going to catch the ball. Um, yeah, I know nothing but nothing but compliments for him. Mike, uh Mike was saying kind of the operation wasn't great at times today. What I guess any any reason you could feel for that at all or? >> Yeah. Um you know, working through some working through some kinks early. Um you know, we we expect perfection in the operation side. That's something that we preach and uh that obviously wasn't there tonight. Um something we need to continue to press through training camp. Um, and I think, you know, obviously the quarterback room can lead that and and we're going to >> You've been hearing all plays through your new offensive coordinator all through camp and whatnot, but anything different tonight? Anything different and new about that? >> No, I thought it was great. Um, we mixed in the wristband a little bit. Um, no, I I I it was actually it was actually seamless. Um, first time first time really hearing him call wristband and flipping in and out from a wristband call a non- wristband call. Um, I thought the communication was great and um, you know, it's it's been worked on over camp and to be able to mix in the wristband, mix in a real call um, for the first time tonight live bullets. It was it was great. >> Did you use the wristband at all last season, preseason? >> Uh, I don't remember about preseason. I know I know we did regular season. Uh yeah, just about every one of them on there. Um sometimes they can get a little wordy and um it's just I know there's multiple different beliefs on wristbands, non- wristbands, whatever whatever makes it easiest. It's I think it's for the better. >> Is that usually the quarterbacks or the coordinator's preference or a combination of the two? >> I'd say it's a combination of the two. Um I've been in multiple different systems and some put the whole game plan on there. somewhere just third down in red zone. We didn't use it a couple years when I was in Denver. Um I think it's just a preference thing. >> Was it mostly? You said it was mostly on the wristband last week. >> Uh yeah, mostly if not all of them on the wristband. Actually, that's false. It was not all of them. It was mostly now that I'm thinking about it more. It was not all of them. We would do a meeting every night on a Saturday and go through all the ones that were non- wristbanded to call them out and keep practicing those. >> Mike opened his comments today. about the crowd for a preseason game being like as big as a loud team. Did you sense a difference from >> Yeah, it was awesome. It was awesome. Even like, you know, when when you finally get told the day is done, you kind of absorb a little more and just looking around late in the third, early fourth, it's like, wow, this place is actually packed. It's super cool. Again, nothing that we don't know, but shout out to the twelves. Best fan base ever. It's super cool that they'd come out and support us tonight. What were your thoughts on the way that the quarterback rotation was today? Like Mike said that there's a switch up in the past where like you might have played like the whole first half and then Jaylen comes in. Uh how does that impact rhythm? >> Yeah. Um know it's definitely new. Um I had done a lot of different ways. This is my first time doing it this way. I feel like honestly it is a uh it's a good way as a as a backup guys. Obviously me and Jaylen aren't going to be the starters this year. kind of being able to go to get pulled out, sit a little bit. Kind of feels like a normal Sunday where you're just getting thrown in. If something were to happen, you kind of feel that way about how the rotation went tonight. It's a good thing to practice for us, I think. >> To get to this point where you're finally playing against somebody else, next week you go on the road, you know, what's that journey been like in camp as you take these steps forward now as it gets closer to being real, so to speak? >> Yeah, I we've had a great camp. Um, we've came to work every single day. every room has. Honestly, it's been it's been really impressive to watch the guys work and um I know it's always exciting to go on your first road trip as a team. You got everybody, you've got however many players we have all going on this trip and get to get to build the brotherhood a little bit and hang out and go to somebody else's place. Feel that energy. It it it feels different than being at home and going against each other all the time. Being able to go do a little practice uh with the Titans would be cool. And um yeah, it's awesome to get on the road and you know, feel like you're not wanted. >> Anything else, guys? >> Thanks, guys.

title: Tyrice Knight: "We Always Have The Next Man Up Mentality" | Seattle Seahawks
text: How did it feel to be back out there and actually get to tackle? >> It felt good being back on Lumen, you know, all the twelves came out to support us. But, you know, for my defense it just felt good being healthy and being back on the field. >> Mike talked earlier in camp about you being a player that's like even if you're not right now in the starting lineup, you're pushing for playing time and they'll find ways to get you involved. Is that the way they coach is that a motivation that you know, there's always opportunity for they'll find ways to get you on the field? >> Yeah, pretty much just, you know, we always got next man up mentality. So, really just everybody always just kind of work every day and just for me I just been having a great camp and just trying to stack days. I just let the chips to play out how they supposed to play out. >> What do you expect Ben Leedy to have in a great camp? >> Um, probably just getting the confidence back, being more decisive, just just getting back to how I was before everything happened. >> Not that you haven't done it before, but what did it kind of run the defense out there today with the group and kind of have What did you kind of take away from that? >> Um, you know, it felt good just I don't really get to call the defense, but it felt good today just getting the calls and everybody lined up and just getting everybody really ready to go for every snap, everybody looking at me waiting for me to get a command. That just gave me a good feeling today. >> Did you have the the green dot? >> Yeah. >> Have you done that before? >> Uh, my rookie year preseason. >> How did you do it? You made all the calls, right? >> Yeah, I did. >> How was that different than Mike Nolan making the calls? >> Oh, you know, they got a different play style, different voice, all that. You just got to lock in and be ready to go wherever whenever you get a call. >> Tyrel, you've seen you off the edge a fair amount in training camp and out of preseason. You did that some at UTEP as well. Do you foresee that being a way that maybe you could get some snaps on Sundays this year? >> Yeah, you know, versatility is it should be a big part in everybody's game. So, just showing that I can pass rush and still defend, coverage off the line, that should give me pretty much aces in my game. >> Tyrel, so the last time we saw you in significantly against Arizona last year, you had those two forced fumbles that led to the touchdowns and everything. Where do you feel your game has taken a step forward, you know, both from rookie year to then and and from then to now? >> Um probably the biggest stepping for me probably just be, like I said, just more decisive, just how it was at Utah, just bringing the same game to the NFL and that just playing downhill more, just, you know, being ahead of the play. >> When you were in the game, you have to process the play as done, get ready for the next play much quicker since you're going to call the play, or is it kind of the same case? >> Uh you got to get I'm got to get ready for the next play, like you got to hurry up and hurry up and get back to the um middle of the huddle and get everybody back locked down. So, you don't really don't got no time to lollygag and just think about other stuff. You just got to put the next play behind you and get ready for the next. >> Anything else, guys? >> Thanks, Darius. Thank you. >> Thank you. Thank you.
