Um, probably just getting a confidence back, being more decisive, just just getting back to how it was before everything happened. >> Not that you haven't done it before, but what did it kind of run the defense out there today with the group kind of what did you kind of take away from that? >> Um, you know, it felt good just I don't really get a call to the defense, but it felt good today just getting a call, get everybody lined up, and just get everybody really ready to go for every snap. Everybody looking at me, waiting for me to get a command. That just gave him a good feeling today. >> You had the the green. Yeah. >> Have you done that before? >> Uh my rookie year preseason Dirty made all the calls, right? >> Yeah. >> How was that different than Mike? >> Oh, you know, they got a different play style, different voice, all that. You just got to lock in, be ready to go wherever whenever get the call. >> Tyres, you've seen you off the edge a fair amount in training camp and preseason. You did that some at UT as well. Do you foresee that being a way that maybe you can get some snaps on Sundays this year? >> Yeah, you know, um versatility is it should be a big part of every everybody game. So, um, just showing I could pass rush and still defend coverage off the line, that should give me pretty much aces in my game. >> Tar, last time we saw you play significantly against Arizona last year, you had the two force fumbles that led the touchdowns and everything. Where do you feel your game has taken a step forward, you know, both from rookie year to then and from then to now? >> Um, probably the biggest step for me probably just be, like I said, just more decisive. just how it was at Utah, just bringing that same game to the NFL and that just playing downhill more, just you know, being ahead of the plate >> when you were in the green. Uh, you have to process the plays done, get ready for the next play much quicker since you're going to call the play or is it kind of the same case? >> Uh, you got to get you got to get ready for the next play. Like you got to hurry get back to the middle of the huddle, get everybody back locked in. So, you really don't got no time to lo guy and just think about other stuff. You just got to put a nest plate behind you and get ready for the next. >> Anything else? Okay. Um, first of all, I want to shout out the twelves. I mean, that's the most people I ever seen at a preseason game. So, uh, we owe we owe them a better performance to say the least. But uh I just told I told the team it's um we're going to learn a lot from this game whether you know take the result out of it. Obviously it's disappointing to lose the game. Anytime you line up and anything competitively we're trying to win. But um right now our process needs to improve. That's really the biggest takeaway is um on really in both phases on offense and defense our operation is uh not up to par and how we're finishing plays is not up to par. So uh that'll be a focus moving forward. But it's it's good to know. you know, I'm glad we know now on the things we need to be able to do to take our uh our team to the next level. And um and we have a great opportunity to go to go figure it out. You know, we got a big week coming up. Uh couple couple great practices opportunities and then um and then off to Tennessee we go have a great practice and and play another great game and and uh take, you know, and move forward. So that's where we're at. >> You say the operation wasn't up to your standard. What do you mean? Um just all all the things [snorts] how we you know how we get calls in, how we take the line, uh how we motion, how we shift, how we get lined up on defense, how we communicate. Uh all those things need to take a uh a very big jump very quickly. So uh but it's good to know now we know it. So let's go get it. >> Just ask you about student contract. I mean obviously we all know he's a great player, but what why is he so important to what you have done and what you want to do in the future? Well, I mean, Spoon Spoon is all the things. He's a He's a great person. He's a great football player. Uh he's a great teammate. He's a great leader. Those are the guys we want to be here. It's it's kind of similar to Jack. It's like these are these are foundational people to to our to our to our team. And I'm I'm extremely excited to get that um foundation laid, you know, where we know Spoon's going to be here for the long haul. and and and we're also excited for the opportunity to to reward him, you know, that this is a contract that we feel like he's earned and we should celebrate it as well. But it's also really exciting to know that we've we have foundational players that are going to be part of our team here for a long time. >> He was one of the guys when you said, you know, the first phase of OTAAS, some of the veteran guys didn't need to be there. He was there day one. >> He's out practicing like a maniac while he's still waiting to get a deal done. Like what does that tell you about him? >> Oh, well that's that paints a great picture, John. like he um he's just infectious and he loves the game. You know, we were talking today. He's just, you know, people would hopefully he doesn't mind me sharing this, but people would talk to him about um you know, ask him why he does what why he's doing what he's doing. He's like, "Yeah, I love I love the game of football and there's a season to get ready for." You know, he kind of keeps the main thing the main thing without getting distracted by all the the extra stuff. U he also probably feels, you know, he's also a great teammate. you know, he just wants to be there for the guys and and uh how our team plays is important to him, which is which is uh really cool. >> He closes out the NFC championship game those two pass breakups and then the slot bles were just insane in the Super Bowl. >> What how like certain players just have a knack for coming up with the biggest moments? What is it about him that allows him to do that? >> Well, I think it's his relentless attitude about like the details. doesn't matter the situation, he's playing it at, you know, at at top speed, top intent. That's how we want our football team to operate, you know. I mean, there are plays in earlier in the game in the NFC game that Spoon um probably could have played better, but like the mentality to just attack the next play all the time is uh is probably what makes it so special. And then in both those plays, you know, they're both are extended plays where, you know, I think we're in man coverage on both of them to be able to, you know, to guard your man for that amount of time relentlessly is is uh I mean, it's legendary type stuff. And then, you know, in terms of how he plays nickel position on early downs and the things he did in the Super Bowl are are some of the some of the things that make him special as well. >> I think you may have had a comment on the radio after the Super Bowl about like the impact he had on the Super Bowl as a Blitzer. like does that make you feel like maybe you should use him more in that role? >> Yes. >> Yes. Yeah. It's it's uh he's a he's a great corner and he's a great nickel and when when Nick's available, Nick's also a great nickel and so you know it's it's a great it's a great problem to have as a as a coach that you know how do you deploy your people to have success? But, um, Spoon is very, I mean, all all those instincts about timing and, you know, even even beating guards, you know, setting them up and beating backs and one-on-one pass situations is uh, you know, it's not it's not common for those for that skill set. >> Looked like he jumped about 8 ft in the air to celebrate after the long puck return. >> Yeah. Today, >> yeah, >> we were trying to get a penalty. We were trying to get a celebration penalty, but I was a little disappointed that, you know, we could be we could bring some more uh some energy to to the celebrations. >> To Bob's point, like Ernest Jones was out celebrating. A lot of guys weren't playing seemed very into the game. Does that tell you something about those guys? >> Yeah, I was excited. You know, and and the guys playing like, you know, we we got to we have to play with more urgency. take take the from the when the ball was snapped to like when the ball is over the play is over but like how we finish the play to the op the whole operation needs to improve and the players are responsible for that as well. It's not this isn't like a a comment on our coaches or anything. It's it's the whole team and so and to do that that provides energy. That's how you stack plays you know that's how you kind of get out of a rut is by you know falling back on those on those like core fundamentals those core principles of how we're going to operate as a football team. So that didn't happen today. That's probably the most disappointing thing. >> Did you really want the penalty? >> Uh, kind of. Yeah. >> Why? >> I mean, that I just wanted the guy I wanted the guys to feel the energy and and kind of like we did last year like this is I think we got an interception or something and I think everybody was in uniform that maybe I don't I don't know. I probably should know the rules better. Mike, with um Tyrie, you said early in camp that you know you'd like to find a way to get him involved a little bit more and it seemed like he had one of those games that shows he's ever >> Yeah, we're a little banged up at inside backer right now. So, Tai uh played probably more than we bargain for, but >> um played a probably he he's the best player on the field on defense today for sure. So, that was uh that was cool to see. >> What the initial thought on how the two quarterbacks played? um good enough to put up seven points, you know, got to put up more points. We need to operate better. Uh there's some good things. There's there's going to be a lot of there's going to be like it's so great to have tape against another team now like in in a real in a different type of setting where the pass rush is live, you know, um you're up against the play clock, you know, there's there's penalty. All these different things that you'd have to be able to play out uh are great learning experiences for everybody, quarterbacks included. Jaylen Mo talked to us a couple days about being more decisive is his key. >> How do you think he was tonight? He seemed to hold on to the ball. >> Uh there were spots, you know, I got we got to see if you know what the things that he that he was seeing, but um >> I think the whole thing just needs just whole thing just let's go take another step, you know. Um you know, was it there? Let's let's encourage him to go rip it. I think that I think some great things that Jaylen did was extend plays with his legs. um something that uh has been a point of emphasis with him that he's just that he's really uh it's great to see him do that today. That really helped us. >> Tory Foster's a guy who's had a strong camp. Is it good to see when a player can do that and carry it in? >> Yeah. Yeah, for sure. Yeah. Happy for montory. Um all the things you felt in camp, you felt uh felt today during the game. >> We haven't seen Jaylen take off and run a whole lot like this summer in practices. It sounds like that's some Are you saying that's something you wanted to encourage him to do more? Yeah. And like it's hey, you know, there's the play doesn't have to end if you're if there's nobody to throw in with your progressions. Like you're allowed to extend the play. You know, it's up to you on how long the play goes. >> You had Dury doing the play calling tonight. >> Yeah, AD called the game, did a good job. Um, >> what did that afford you? What did you see differently or what are you able to glean from a >> Um, you know, I think it was best for us right now for him for him to call. It's great experience for AD. Uh, he's called the majority of camp up to this point. Um, he's done a phenomenal job throughout camp. He really has. He's he's we've had a ton of call up periods. Um, he's on the details. He's thinking thinking um just doing a lot of great stuff, honestly. So, um, but at some point I gota I gotta get ready to call game two. So, I think I think I'll probably call next week. >> Bud Clark, do you get a chance with Jordan Hall plays to see him run away? >> Did some good things. Did some good things. Um, some things off the top of my head that I know that we want to talk about and improve. But, uh, again, he he's he's a great example of, hey, this is your first experience playing a game, you know, in a loud environment where we have to communicate. You know, the communication needs to improve on Dave. I think that's a wakeup call to our guys of, you know, examples of So, shout out to the twelves for being loud and showing our guys that we got to be able to communicate better. But, um, great great first experience for him. He's going to learn from it. >> Okay. Thank you. >> Thank you. What's going on? >> Drew, what did you like about the opening drive? >> Um, yeah. Uh, finishing in the red zone was probably the plus there. Um, good put together good set of plays. Um, move the ball well, ran the ball well. guys got the ball in their hands, they made plays with it. Montoy had a great catch in the end zone and uh just we we finished. Um I think that's the key takeaway or what we need to work on is just finishing in the red zone. >> There had to be a lot of trust in that throw. He didn't turn around and see that ball was almost on. >> Yeah. Um when you're that, you know, when you're that tight um down there in the red zone, there's not a lot of time for, you know, patting the ball and seeing guys come out of breaks. Um, you know, we've obviously practiced that play before and um, built some built some good chemistry on it and, you know, I trust him on Tory and he made a great catch. >> Sounds like he makes at least one play every day. What have you thought of this summer, he said? >> Yeah, he should have made two today if I don't overthrow him on that uh, ball on the left sideline. Um, he's had a great summer. He's had a great summer. I think I said it, forgot who I was saying it to, but you know, the journey he's been on from the previous year till now, man, he's he's light years away from where he was, and he's been fantastic for us. Makes great plays, explosive with the ball in his hand, reliable, he's going to catch the ball. Um, yeah, I know nothing but nothing but compliments for him. Uh Mike was saying kind of the operation wasn't great at times today. What I guess any reason you could feel for that at all or >> Yeah. Um you know working through some working through some kinks early. Um you know we we expect perfection in the operation side. That's something that we preach and uh that obviously wasn't there tonight. Um something we need to continue to press through training camp. Um, and I think, you know, obviously the quarterback room can lead that and and we're going to. >> You've been hearing all plays through your new offensive coordinator all through camp and whatnot, but anything different tonight? Anything different or new about that? >> No, I thought it was great. Um, we mixed in the wristband a little bit. Um, no, I I I it was actually it was actually seamless. Um, first time first time really hearing him call wristband and flipping in and out from a wristband call, a non- wristband call. Um, I thought the communication was great and um, you know, it's it's been worked on over camp and to be able to mix in the wristband, mix in a real call um, for the first time tonight live bullets. It was it was great. >> Did you use the wristband at all last season, preseason? >> Uh, I don't remember about preseason. I know I know we did regular season. Uh yeah, just about every one of them on there. Um sometimes they can get a little wordy and um it's just I know there's multiple different beliefs on wristbands, non- wristbands, whatever whatever makes it easiest. It's I think it's for the better. >> Is that usually the quarterbacks or the coordinator's preference or a combination of the two? >> I'd say it's a combination of the two. Um I've been in multiple different systems and some put the whole game plan on there. somewhere just third down in red zone. We didn't use it a couple years when I was in Denver. Um I think it's just a preference thing. >> Was it mostly You said it was mostly on the wristband last year. >> Uh yeah, mostly if not all of them on the wristband. Actually, that's false. It was not all of them. It was mostly now that I'm thinking about it more. It was not all of them. We would do a meeting every night on a Saturday and go through all the ones that were non- wristbanded to call them out and keep practicing those. >> Mike opened his comments today. You talk about the crowd for a preseason game being like as big as a loud team. Did you sense a difference from >> Yeah, it was awesome. It was awesome. Even like, you know, when when you finally get told the day is done, you kind of absorb a little more and just looking around late in the third, early fourth, it's like, wow, this place is actually packed. It's super cool. Again, nothing that we don't know, but shout out to the twelves. Best fan base ever. It's super cool that they'd come out and support us tonight. What were your thoughts on the way that the quarterback rotation was today? Like Mike said that there's a switch up in the past where like you might have played like the whole first half and then Jaylen comes in. Uh how does that impact rhythm? >> Yeah. Um you know it's definitely new. Um I had done a lot of different ways. This is my first time doing it this way. I feel like honestly it is a uh it's a good way as a as a backup guys. Obviously me and Jaylen aren't going to be the starters this year. kind of being able to go to get pulled out, sit a little bit. Kind of feels like a normal Sunday where you're just getting thrown in. If something were to happen, you kind of feel that way about how the rotation went tonight. It's a good thing to practice for us, I think. >> To get to this point where you're finally playing against somebody else, next week you go on the road, you know, what's that journey been like at camp as you take these steps forward now as it gets closer to being real, so to speak? >> Yeah, I we've had a great camp. Um, we've came to work every single day. every room has. Honestly, it's been it's been really impressive to watch the guys work and um I know it's always exciting to go on your first road trip as a team. You got everybody, you've got however many players we have all going on this trip and get to get to build the brotherhood a little bit and hang out and go to somebody else's place. Feel that energy. It it it feels different than being at home and going against each other all the time. Being able to go do a little practice uh with the Titans will be cool. And um yeah, it's awesome to get on the road and you know, feel like you're not wanted. >> Anything else, guys? >> Thanks, guys. that touchdown. Did you know when you turn around the ball was going to be right on you like that? >> Yeah, I did actually. Um, you know, it was kind of tight coverage a little bit so and it was a tight window too. shout out to Drew, but um you know on that plant I knew the ball was going to be right there so I was just ready for it. >> Did that linebacker tip it? Did he change direction at all? >> He almost tipped it. It was super close, but you know I was just ready for the moment and then made the play. So definitely >> you've had a good camp up to this point. How like rewarding is it to then have it carry over into game action and show what you can do on the game? >> Yeah, definitely man. It's been great. Um every time I play I play to a standard and it don't matter if I'm, you know, playing good or bad. like my standard is my standard. I go out there every day and just try to put my best foot forward every day and put forth the effort. Go block, do the little things, and you know, let everything else take care of itself. >> How close were you to that second one that drew just over three down the sideline? >> Yeah, I I was close, man. I feel like, um, you know, watching the tape on the sideline, I could have did a better part of just digging out my route. Um, I looked a little bit too early, so you know, that's something that I can clean up in my game. Um, which I will do next How much over these next couple weeks you feel like special teams will be big for you to try to get a chance to show it. You can be there as well. >> Yeah, definitely, man. Like every time I go out on that field, like whatever's on my plate, you know, I'm just going to take care of whatever I got to do. So, um I can't wait to get more opportunities in special teams to show that I can do that too as well. >> You get dropped in here late last year joining the practice squad and following along for the run and everything. I know you had the social media stuff kind of following your journey with everything to now all of a sudden be out there contributing a little bit. So, what does that kind of mean to you? >> Yeah, it means everything, man. Um, you know, I was back at home, shoot, for 16 weeks. And, you know, it was it was tough, man. It was times where, you know, I wanted to give up and just, you know, get a regular job, but, um, I stayed at it. Um, my dad told me cream always rise to the top and just to stay faithful and I just kept working and, you know, I'm now I'm here today. >> You were teaching back then, right? >> Yeah, I was I was doing a lot of things, man. Um, I was teaching, substitute teaching at my high school. Um, I actually got my real estate license too while I was back at home and then I was training little kids in football too as well just to give back to the game. >> As a, you know, undrafted guys coming in, it's a tough road to go. When you got hurt in camp and got on injured list, like did you wonder was that your only opportunity? >> Um, yeah, I had no idea, man. Uh, you know, I know I had some teams, you know, in the past that, you know, before the pre-draft process call me and stuff, but, you know, you never know in this business because, you know, it's the 1% of the 1%. So, you know, it's all about faith and timing and, you know, luckily I was on God's timing. >> When did When were you teaching and doing real estate? >> Uh, when I went back home. So, I would say probably in like September. >> Okay. >> Yeah. September of last year. >> And what were you teaching? So, I was just a substitute teacher just filling in really. Um, I had I want to say freshman's and juniors in high school. So, that's what I was dealing with so far. >> Um, I had a Latin class. So, I went to St. Ed so we I didn't I don't know any Latin so at all. So, you know, I was just like, man, do y'all homework and I'll just be here and watching y'all. And, you know, they was all good from there. >> No lesson plan? >> Yeah. No lesson plan. Not at all. [laughter] Thank you. What's up? >> How'd it go? >> It was good to be back on the field, especially at home to start the the year off. um being around the guys and especially for us, you know, going through training camp competing against each other. It was the opportunity for us to go compete against somebody else. So, it's it's a lot of fun. Um it's good to feel the the energy from our fans, especially just being game one of preseason. So, I'm excited for the season to keep on rolling and we're getting closer to our first game. >> You told us you told us a couple days ago, decisiveness is the key to you. Being decisive. How do you think that went for you tonight? Yeah, I think every play that I have the ball in my hands, it's all about being decisive. Um trusting in in the game plan, trusting in um Coach Flurry or whatever play call he has and putting our offense in the best position to be successful. And so I think that was key out the whole game. And of course, like this is what preseason game number one is for. Like there's always things we can clean up. There's always things we can do positive. And even if we came out victorious, there things that we can improve on, get better at. And so that's the exciting part about preseason and getting um opportunity to play um today. And so uh the biggest thing just to build on today and build on and going into our next opponent, >> especially the first half you took off running a few times, you got some big games. Was that was that kind of an emphasis to want to try to do that in this game at all or >> Not necessarily. I think every time I had the ball in my hands, it's all about putting our offense in the best position to win. And whether it's passing, whether it's running, whether it's handing the ball off, so many areas to our offense that uh can can beat a defense. And so, um, every opportunity we have to move the chains, um, we're going to do it in unique ways. And, uh, that was just one one way to do it. >> What's Brian Flurry like in a game? How does he give you feedback? >> Yeah. Um, I think what's unique about having your play call on the field, you can get direct u dialogue as far as what he's seeing. Um, plays that are going to set up during a drive. You know, of course, we have the iPads. We're able to see exactly what coverage, you know, structure and things that they can have and then to set up plays. And so it's the communication of moving forward, right? Like of course you watch the tape of what exactly went down on that drive. So now it's the moving forward aspect of uh looking at how we can attack the defense. >> How did the speed of the game feel today versus last year? And were you pleased with how you were able to use your legs to scramble? >> Um never pleased, you know, of course. Um there's so many opportunity to grow um as a quarterback um in this league. And so um I think for all of us in the locker room, it's like how can we be better than we were this weekend? And um today was a great opportunity for us to put in display um the hard work that we've been doing during the week. And so of course we're going to learn and grow and get better. >> What role can a quarterback take in terms of the team finishing in the red zone without pressing? >> Yeah. Um I think that's key. Yeah, I think when you're in the red zone, we need to come out with points. You know, whether it's a field goal, whether it's a touchdown, coming out with points is so important, especially helping our defense out. Um, and putting putting points on the board is so important. You know, it's going to being critical when we play tough opponents, you know, when we're um trailing in the game, whether we're in in the lead, it just really just finishing drives. So, I think that's another emphasis for us is finishing drives. >> Cory Foster been a really good player in camp all summer. Now, he's lead receiver in this game. What have you seen from him since he got here? >> I think a growth mindset. Um a mindset to grow each and every day that he has opportunity to be on the field. Um I think also the approach that he takes whether it's preparing um whether it's playing different position X to Z F like being versatile so coach can use on the field. And so I think that's something that um I applaud him on is that he's been versatile around the field to play all positions. Jayen, have you ever played in a game like that where the quarterbacks were rotating that way rather than just being one guy playing for a certain amount of [snorts] time and then the other one coming in? What were your thoughts on that? >> Um, I think as a backup you have to be prepared and ready to go at any at any at any point. Um, this is not my first time being a backup and so, uh, I think reps are so important for me, Andrew. Um, and for any guy that's a backup because in the league, you know, the starter gets majority of the reps. So, as many reps that we can get, as much as possible is going to prepare us and help us out for whenever the opportunity comes that we play in the game. And so, um, I don't see as a negative. I think this is an opportunity for us to get reps and preseason is big for us because during the season, um, once you have established starter, you know, your your your reps are cut short. >> You told us the other day how close you are with Terry Arnold and you hope it was come here now. Now, it looks like it's going to happen. Have you been able to talk to him since then at all? What are your thoughts on that? >> Of course. Yeah, of course. That's that's my dog and I'm very happy that he's going to be a Seahawk. Um, I think now it's just showing him the way of how we do things. And I think that's not a move forward process. You know, the process was trying to figure out where he was going to go. So now he's a Hawk. And so we're just going to emphasize what we do as, you know, as being here in Seattle and u emphasizing our theme, our mods, and our team mission and goals. And so now it's a running forward mentality with having him a part of our team. >> Jay, what do you think people should know about Terion? >> I think I [sighs] think number one is that he's committed. um when he has goals set for him, he wants to achieve them and he's going to put his all into everything he puts into it. Um this is someone that's uh really care about his teammates. Um he's really unique as far as what he can do on the field. Um and uh he's grown to really love the culture that we have here because it's similar to the vibe that we had when we was in college. >> How is he going through all this? >> Doing good. He's doing good. Um he's excited for the opportunity and uh he's really going to seize it when he gets here. Anything else?

title: Something Is Up With the Devon Witherspoon Extension...
text: Williams' contract extension, which they've kept really quiet. And he kind of jumps out from behind a desk and signs his name. That would [laughter] be nice. >> That's not a That's not a terrible idea. Brady, is there any information on any of the contract extension situations with the Seahawks that we should know? Any updates there? >> I mean, we know that they've been working on Leonard Williams, and they've had I guess some discussions with with Devon Witherspoon. I mean, that is a strange one cuz I know that after they extended Jackson Smith-Njigba in late March, they immediately turned their attention to Witherspoon and trying to get that deal done. And they made him an initial offer not long after that. So, we're talking about well, April, May, June, July, you know, four plus months now where they've been working on it, and it hasn't happened yet. And I I don't I don't even know if they know exactly why it hasn't happened yet or when it's going to happen. We can certainly come up with plenty of theories, and I I would venture to guess that it it probably has something to do with the fact that is this microphone creeps closer to my mouth. There we go. Probably I think it's We we could say there's a good chance it has something to do with the fact that Devon Witherspoon's agent also represents Christian Gonzalez, who is in line for a top of the market extension himself. Now, whether that is the agent is the one who's dragging his feet or whether it's maybe the players who are waiting each other out knowing that typically in situations like this one guy goes, the next guy tops that. So, maybe those guys are both, you know, waiting for the other guy to go first. I don't really know. I I had a theory at one point, and and I don't know if I believe this as much as I did, but that maybe the agent was waiting, you know, maybe just long enough for this situation to play out on Hard Knocks knowing that that would be a quite the promotional tool to let the entire world know who made Devon Witherspoon the highest paid quarterback in football. title: Keeanu Benton, Elandon Roberts & Nick Herbig Press Conference (August 15) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Uh, yeah, first of all, I just want to say I'm excited. Um, it's a dream come true for me and my family. Um, I want to thank Mr. Rooney, uh, uh, Omar. I'm going to thank Mike T. I want to thank my parents, my family, the whole Steelers organization. Uh, my beautiful girlfriend, um, all my boys who I put in the work with to get to this point. Um, I'm just forever grateful. Uh, God putting me in these positions to overcome obstacles and come out on top each and every time. So, um, I just want to thank all those people and can't wait to see what the future holds. >> Keanu, a couple months ago you were the one standing in the back of the room for Nick when he got his, uh, when he got his extension. What does it mean to you that both of you guys, as long as you've been friends, both now have good extensions and are playing here for so much longer? >> Yeah, you know, it's a dream come true. This is our seventh, eighth year playing together, uh, consecutively. Um, I I think it means the world. Um, you know, I was back there, I was celebrating for him, but then at the same time getting that itch like when is my turn going to come? But now, we both we both got our contract done and we can kind of take this thing to the next level. >> Keanu, can you kind of take me back to, uh, Mobile during the Senior Bowl during your draft process? I remember being down there and then speaking with some of the Steelers people that were there and they were just really impressed with you during that time. From that point on through your entire draft process, can you remember just your interactions with the Steelers and could you have imagined getting to this point now where you didn't weren't just drafted by them, but now getting a second contract? >> Yeah, you know, um, it was it was pretty brief at the Senior Bowl. Um, it it was kind of crazy cuz, you know, you see Mike T on television and stuff like that, but he just came up on the side note after a pass rush and told me I was something special. So, um, him him actually going through with his words and and picking me up in the draft in the second round uh meant the world to me. Um and then now I'm with PG who was my head coach at the Senior Bowl. It's just you know this whole thing just goes full circle and you never know who you'll be playing for. Just respecting everybody and making the most of every situation you're in. >> Cali, you're the third guy from your draft class to get a contract extension. Seems like possibly there could be more. How early on did you guys realize that the group of you together were going to be pretty special for this team? >> Yeah, I think we knew it right off rip. Um we had a we had this bond that that was untouchable and I feel like that's important especially going into the league um because you know you got that bond in college because you know everybody is still young, you know. You meet new people, you get that brotherhood, but when you get to the league it kind of leaks off a little bit. Everybody got families and stuff like that, but we kind of made a promise to our class that we're going to stay close and stay at it. So I feel like we had we had a uh hold each other accountable and it just became contagious. >> Same time, seems like you guys are building a uh young defensive line movement. Well, you still have Cam in the room, you, Derrick, Wyatt, guys like Gabriel, guys like David. You guys have all kind of What does it mean that you what you guys have been able to build in just your couple of years together figuring each other out? >> Yeah, I think this is just a stepping stone um to something special. Uh I feel like all those guys, including myself, you know, you just find little things to get better at each day um each week and just figuring each other out is it comes along with just playing playing with each other over period of time and I think this is going to come naturally and and we're going to be a pretty good group up front. >> When did you know this contract was kind of kind of beyond the horizon? I'm sure your agents and the team talked, but when did you kind of start dialing in knowing maybe it might be today not last Saturday hypothetically it was coming. >> Yeah, you know, I knew it was coming eventually, but just didn't know when. See, I still ain't got a haircut today. If I if I knew uh it was today, uh I would definitely get cleaned up a little bit, but I was just trying to focus on um making the most of these last few days of camp um and let my agent figure out the whole contract situation. >> A lot of people have talked about you not playing as much nose and playing a little bit more either in passing situations or more of, you know, outside more-ish. Is that Is that happening this year some and is that what you want? Producing sacks and things, is that something that you you want to >> I feel like I can play all over the D-line. Um where I'm going to play and how much I'm going to play in each position is up to my coach, so I'm ready for whatever at this point. >> Mike McCarthy said that there is definitely more there when it comes to your game and I think this extension probably also kind of speaks to that. How do you feel like there's more there? What do you feel like you need to do more, whether that's your own performance, how you might fit into this particular scheme? What do you need to do to to get to that next level for >> Um I think it's just the the utilizing me in different places on the D-line. Um I feel like that's something I have I haven't had the opportunity to do as much to this point, but I I'm I'm feeling that that's what I'm going to be doing this year, just moving around, being that that Army Swiss knife that can plug in left, right, middle, um just playing all those positions and getting after the quarterback for sure. >> Who was the first person How did you find out last night that the deal was done and who was the first person you told? >> Yeah, so I was in my bed actually. Uh then my agent told me to call him and I assumed cuz if you not about to tell me to call you for no reason when I'm about to go to bed, but um we actually added Nick to the call first and then I was able to tell my my uh girlfriend and then my my parents. >> What and what was that call like? Like did you know that he was going to tell you like hey, it's done when you added Nick to the call? >> I mean, I assumed when Like he added him after he told me but uh I assume just because you're not telling me to call you at 10:00 for no reason after I told you I'm in bed. So it got it better be something. >> You sleep after that? >> Not really. Me and Nick stayed up for a little bit just talking and you know reflecting on how far we came for real. You know the 7 years done went by kind of fast but made a lot of progress within it. >> Keanu we've heard a lot from players in the defense talking about how Patrick Graham has worked so much closer with the D-line as the D coordinator. What has he been like when he focuses extra in on with you guys along with you know Demarvion and what you guys already have? >> I think it's been awesome. He's a old D-line coach and he not afraid to show it. He he not afraid to speak his mind and I love that about him. He he brings a different edge to us and it's always nice to have another person's like opinion on like on your staff on what's going on and having having multiple minds working on the same thing but I think he brings a lot to us and just making it a lot easier for us. >> Is there a difference in how he coaches you guys to maybe hold up offensive lineman a bit more to keep the linebackers clean? That was something that I was talking to some of the linebackers and he said like you know especially that first preseason game how clean they were versus you know you guys focusing on attacking. It seems like there might be a different emphasis this year. Is that a different emphasis for you guys as a D-line or is that something you guys always did? >> I mean I feel like he's he's almost doing the opposite. Like he's he's telling the linebackers to keep us clean when they're pressing gaps and making sure they're kind of getting downhill and not letting them double team stay on us. Um but I I think he's doing a great job of that. >> Well Steve Keanu congratulations. What's the first thing you're going to get? You have anything in mind yet? >> Um no. I got pretty much everything I want for real. I'm not ready to spend it all yet but we're going to have some fun for sure. >> Guys good? All right. Thank you. >> Thank you. Keanu. That feel good. It feel good. Feel good being out here in Latrobe. You know, I was in the dorm room last night and I was just kind of looking up at the walls and I was just like I it was just you know I was I was enjoying it. You know, sometimes uh being in in in certain places, you know, I was here for 2 years. So, I'm like, "Ah, man, we got to be in the dorms." When I got back, I was like, "Yeah." You know, this time I left the overalls at home though. >> What's it like to reunite not just with the Steelers, but also with Patrick Graham? >> Ah, it's really good. Uh PG, man, very smart. Uh always going to put us in the right situation. Very detailed. Uh you probably got that from him, you know, just talking to him. He's uh He's just a football nerd. He know the history of the game. You know, uh he's been around not just, you know, the New England system, but you know, a lot of great defensive systems to where he's able to soak in so much knowledge to where he can make it come to life, you know, and uh that's a great thing to have in him. >> How different is this defense with him running it and just what you've seen the last couple days? >> I've only been here for 1 day, really. You know, uh defensively, uh just today I see like the nuances are are different concepts and and little little little changes subtle changes that the way he may be running a certain call now and stuff like that. So, yeah. >> Patrick Queen Patrick Queen talked about he was happy to have his OG back. What what was like your first interaction knowing you were back in with him in his in his linebacker room? >> Nah, it was it was exciting, you know, uh me and PQ been talking the whole off season. Uh you know, before the news broke, you know, he was one of the first persons that knew. You know, I dialed in with him. We talked. We had a pretty lengthy conversation, you know, and stuff like that and you know, uh he and myself and you know, he was big on you know, from me even like that brother who him not just PQ him Peyton Cole. I know I played with all of them. You know, and stuff like that. So that was just a huge big thing for me. You know, being able to come back and play and and and and enjoy you know, enjoying where you play enjoying knowing there the the the position you putting yourself into you know what I'm saying? It's not comfortable but at the same time you ready to go and and and you familiar with the landscape. >> What excites you most about this defense? >> Uh everything everything man. Man, you see them big old big old boys up front? Man, they huge. I said whoa y'all got bigger since I left. You know, and uh that's just a uh a big huge uh you know, hat's off to the upstairs. You know, getting that D line constructed the way it is and and even obviously the guys that's that's been here being the pillar of this defense uh Cam and TJ. Uh you know, I haven't been able to really really get around the defensive backs you know, like like I would want to yet. You know, so I can only kind of talk about the front seven but like I said man my my first two days here is is is been good to be home. >> Why did you want to come back here? >> Um you know, this is just different playing for the Steelers. You know, I wanted to be back though. I wanted to be. >> What does Patrick Graham do to help linebackers like like yourself off ball linebackers communicate and be maybe in better control of the defense? Now that you know his system and I know that these guys are really excited to work with you. >> I think just because uh from a linebackers standpoint he was a D line at heart. You know, so the D line you know, he he's big into that gritty. You know, obviously he want them guys to make plays but he like hey I don't want my backers to be touched and whatnot like that. So it it's a it's a lot of that to where now it frees up the linebackers and open up our eyes sometimes too. You know, when you coming downhill it's it's real easy cuz it's like I know you got to be tough. Like, let's let's do this, you know? And cuz if you're not putting two hands on these full hands on these guys, it's a problem, you know? So, you know, it's time to get busy. But other than that, man, uh them guys don't give you time, you know? And and and we're not like that to dissect plays, and it it's just huge. And uh I think that's what the freedom from a linebacker come in as. It's not it's not second-guessing. With them big old jokers, you don't know when it's play action. You don't know when it's boot. You're going to get people going to be getting pushed back fast. And and also, too, with them just being so big and massive and him being a D-line coach, it's easy to identify run pass because, you know, like I said, man, hands going to be put on them big ones up front. >> How much of the same Landon Roberts are we seeing this year? >> Say what? you bringing back? >> From a physicality standpoint? >> From the old Landon Roberts that we saw 2 years ago. >> Yeah, I try not to change. I don't I don't think I changed much, you know? Uh I think uh man, probably the only thing that's changed, man, I got a little smarter, a little from a from a football standpoint. The more years I'm in it, I'm more able to get around, you know, a lot of uh uh good coaches, good defenses to be able to learn different systems, and and seeing different things. So, that's the only thing. But from a physicality standpoint, I'm always be me. >> Bobby Wagner keeps bringing it back every year. >> Mhm. >> Is that you? >> I want Oh, you're talking about >> That kind of as you get older, and he keeps getting better, it seems. [music] >> I mean, hey, I'm not going to lie. Right now, I'm just being on my feet at. But me excelling is is not in not in my thoughts no time soon. So, I got to let you leave it there. >> How did you get number 50, O'Jay Smith? >> Uh me and Jamin were teammates in the Raiders last year. and 57 was available, and uh me and Jamin had a conversation, and we was able to make it happen. >> Yeah. >> Very cool. Good luck to you, man. >> Say it again? >> What are you expecting for a role? >> Right now, man, I'm just doing whatever they ask me to do. You know, and uh whatever role comes to that comes to that. You know, that's all I can do, you know, uh make the make the reps count that I'm in on and be a good teammate, good leader, and uh just come out here every day ready to go. >> I remember when you took the podium about your extension, he was right in the back cheering cheering you on. How excited are you to go cheer him on as he gets to talk to >> I can't wait. I can't wait. It's going to be a special moment, for sure. What's happening with you, brother? Love that guy. Big general back in town. >> What What made you guys respond so special over the years? Like, how did you guys connect like off the field as friends? >> I think when you meet somebody like him who's just a great person, a great human, um and he has that same mindset as you. Uh like we both came into college with the same mindset like this is our goal, like we wanted to play in the NFL. Um and just sharing that and, you know, it kind of trickled into things off the field like you're you're not going out and partying and doing stuff like everything you do is towards that similar goal. So, just sharing that connection and having that bond, especially playing on the line together, like it's just nothing but strength in that. Like that's really my brother. Um I I can't even tell you, man, how I feel for him. >> Your draft class is the draft class of the last four years. This year, what does that mean to you? You're all you guys are staying together there. >> I mean, I think that's a testament to the people that drafted us, too, you know, being able to recognize good football players and have them come here the opportunity. What an honor to be a Steeler and, you know, what an what an honor to be a Steeler for another four years. >> Was there a point in the process where you maybe realized, "Hey, this draft class is pretty special. These guys around me are are pretty good"? >> I mean, I think you kind of knew that throughout the year. Uh you saw the impact everybody had. and I'm still waiting on one more. So, yeah, you know, the the impact our our class has had, I think it's been good so far and I think it's going to be nothing but better. >> You guys are the first draft class the Steelers have had where they've had three guys sign extensions with the team since 2011. [cheering] Back when Cam was drafted, if you if you if a fourth guy like Joey or whoever, that's going to be the first since 2002. What do you think that means [cheering] for this franchise to have all that continuity across the board? >> Yeah, like I said, I think it's a testament to the [cheering] people that drafted us, you know, putting in that time, putting in that work on their end. You know, it's a job for solid, quality players. Um obviously, we still got to show up, put the work in, uh be consistent, be a Steeler. Um but you know, the >> [screaming] >> the fact that they gave us an opportunity and to be in this position, uh not only to play football, but you know, set up our family. Um at the end of the day, it's just a game we love, so I'm just blessed. >> What do you like about Coach McCarthy's style? >> I like that he's very uh detail-oriented, um and everything is kind of moving, you know. There's not really any lax time. It's just go, go, go. >> And do you think spending more time in individual units, like linebackers together, or offensive linemen together, builds a more cohesive unit with linebackers and everybody in their positions? >> Yes and no. I think the way you build chemistry is on the field. Uh so, any chance we get to go 11 on 11, I think that's really, really good for that team chemistry. >> We talked to E-Rob, but one thing he said he loved already seeing just on Thursday, the size and strength of the D-line and how Patrick Graham is having the D-line put hands on guys. How does that help you guys outside linebackers, too, as far as how physical they are, to help keep you guys clean? >> Yeah, I mean, they set the line of scrimmage, you know, and we're all about that. You know, I'm sitting the edge, but if he's sitting the edge right next to me, then I can fall off or go make a play. You know, together we eat. One of us eat, we all eat. >> Do you have a good feeling about the last one getting signed, Joey? >> Are you sure it's going >> I hope so. I hope so. He's a dog.

title: Coach Mike McCarthy Press Conference (August 15) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Mike, I know you talked about signing your own and you know, getting that done. What's it like for you to walk into a new situation and know you have some young guys to build your team. >> I mean, I've always felt this way and it's it's a it's a great day when you're when one of your players gets a second contract. Um you know, when KB walked into the team meeting, everybody applauded. So, I think that tells you right there how everybody feels about him. So, um as I've said before, if you know, if I was in charge of the money, I'd I'd pay them all and we wouldn't have any money. But, I think it's important you know, I believe in drafting develop. I mean, that's that's been the >> [snorts] >> mode of operation that I've worked under, you know, my whole time as a head coach and and it's important. It's so important to this year. It's important to moving forward. So, um it's uh you know, it's new for me cuz you know, I'm I'm the coach. You know, and and and my opinion is the is probably the shortest because of you know, just the limited time I've had with these guys. But, you know, Keanu Benton getting that contract today, I think it's it's huge for him. You know, I had a chance to visit with him last night and just you know, how happy he is for you know, him and his family and that's a that's that's a big day for those you know, anytime those guys get that contract. So, very happy for him. >> Mike, in your time around him, what stuck out to you about Benton and what kind of player he is? >> Well, I think the way I would describe him when his smile, you know, his smile reflects the energy that he plays with. You know, he's a he's a big guy. He's his twitch, uh you know, his his athletic ability, I think there's definitely you know, there's more there as far as his ceiling. So, that that's you know, that's my personal opinion on on him. I think there's a lot of football in front of him, too. So, I I I think that's exciting. You know, you look at the dynamics of our of our defensive line room. I mean, boy, you know, we have a a really good blend of veteran and and guys and you know, and obviously >> having a rookie in there, too. So, uh um and then that's that's that that's something that, you know, bodes well for us, you know, today and moving forward. >> Mike, looking back at the tape, uh what did you like about your quarterbacks' performance all three of them? >> Well, I'll say this. I I thought all three quarterbacks commanded the huddle. They commanded the operation. I thought our operation we got off to a good start. I mean, there wasn't, you know, any hiccups. You know, I I you know, we we continued to really strive to be better in the pre-snap. You know, and that was really part of what today's practice was to go back and correct it. So, but I think for the first game, um I I thought they did a really good job of of managing the game, you know, play in the play, uh not getting outside themselves. So, I I liked their time clock when they activated the scrambles rule. You know, they didn't come out too soon. Uh they hung in there and tried to step up in the A-B gaps. Uh so, we had some, you know, good play extension production. Um and then, you know, and I thought that their ball placement decision-making was was was strong for the first time out. So, and, you know, so much of preseason football is number one, you know, uh particularly young guys that get out there that get down their assignment strong. And uh but you also, as a quarterback, you got to you got to know how to react when the guy doesn't run the the right route. And you know, Will had one and I I thought he did a good job getting, you know, getting on to the to the second receiver and trying to get to the check down. So, uh those are all positive little They're all They're all positive little little things that uh you know, just through experience you learn to see how they handle handle that, too. So, but uh number one was the ball security. That's, you know, that's the first thing we always talk about. And the you know, and the correction component of it. title: The Good and Not So Good from Day 12 of 49ers Training Camp
text: The 49ers just finished day 12 of training camp. Here's who stood out. The good. Wide receiver Trenton Irwin. After De'Shawn Shivers stellar performance in his preseason debut a few days ago, it was reasonable to expect the Niners to reward him by giving him some opportunities with the starters today. They didn't. Instead, they gave those opportunities to Trenton Irwin, a 30-year-old wide receiver who caught two passes for 25 yards against the Titans on Thursday night. Apparently, the Niners really like what they see from him. Today, he caught a 30-yard pass and a 15-yard pass over the middle from Brock Purdy and later dropped a pass in the end zone. I'm guessing head coach Kyle Shanahan wanted to send Shivers a message that he hasn't arrived yet. What a silly message. He should be starting from now on and he shouldn't play any more in the preseason. He's too important. The Niners better not get him injured before the season starts. Wide receiver De'Shawn Shivers, he spent a few minutes at the beginning of practice working on catching passes that were thrown behind him because he dropped one of those on Thursday night. I guess the Niners weren't pleased about that mistake. Shanahan was decidedly lukewarm about Shivers in his postgame press conference. Today, Shanahan essentially demoted Shivers to the second string offense. He ran some routes with the starters, but Purdy never threw him the ball. Instead, Shivers caught passes from Mac Jones. I haven't seen a 49ers wide receiver unfairly punished like this since Brandon Aiyuk was in the doghouse 5 years ago. Free De'Shawn. Wide receiver Jacob Cowing, he returned from injury and beat Jack Jones to catch a 30-yard pass up the right sideline on a pass from Mac Jones. Cowing needs to stay healthy for the rest of camp and play like he did today in both preseason games. Otherwise, he probably won't make the team because he's not 30 like Irwin. Unfortunately for Cowing, he's merely 25, which is far younger than Shanahan would prefer. Wide receiver Deebo Samuel, another 30-year-old wide receiver the Niners just love. Today, he caught a 20-yard pass from Adrian Martinez over the middle. With the starters, Samuel didn't catch any passes, but he did carry the ball a couple times because all the top running backs are injured. Give Samuel credit. He's He's the best shape possible and he shows up every day as opposed to lots of other veterans on the team. He's one of the Iron Mans of camp so far, which is incredible. Unfortunately for him, he's 30, which means he's not as fast as he once was. Good thing Shanahan loves him. Tight end Luke Farrell, he caught three passes from Purdy during a move the ball drill. Purdy seems to trust him, which is surprising considering Farrell was awful last year. He's having a solid camp. Cornerback Renardo Green, he nearly intercepted a deep pass Brock Purdy intended for Mike Evans. Evans had a step on Green, but the trajectory of Purdy's pass was low and caused Evan to slow down, which allowed Green to recover and knock the pass away. Ideally, it would have been nice to see Green intercept that pass because it hit both of his hands. Unfortunately, he doesn't have good hands, but he still is a good cornerback. Cornerback Jack Jones, he injured his hand early on Thursday night against the Titans, but practiced today and recovered a fumble. He takes the ball away from the offense seemingly every other practice, but his coverage isn't exactly sticky. He's an enigma. Linebacker Jaden Dogger, he started at strong side linebacker, then moved to weak side linebacker next to Fred Warner in the nickel defense because Dre Greenlaw had the day off. The 9ers clearly love Dogger, and I'm guessing he'll start at SAM in week one. If Greenlaw ever misses significant time, I expect Dogger will replace him at will and play 100% of the snaps. His stock is soaring. Offensive tackle Trent Williams, he shows up every day and practices even though he's a 38-year-old future Hall of Famer who doesn't really need the work. I've never seen him lead like this before. I'm guessing he's positively reinforcing the 9ers for extending his contract this off season, which is smart. The not so good. Brock Purdy's connection with Mike Evans, it's a work in progress. To be fair, Evans missed at least a week with a quad strain, and today was his first full day back. And he made a nice sliding catch over the middle on a pass from Purdy. But later, Purdy misjudged Evan's speed, underthrew him, and nearly got picked off. Finally, Purdy fired a deep throw toward the sideline before Evans made his break, and the pass landed out of bounds. Purdy loves throwing anticipatory passes to receivers before they've turned their head, but he can't do that just yet with Evans because they haven't played together much. Right now Purdy has a much stronger connection with Trenton Irwin who shouldn't make the team. Quarterback Mac Jones, I don't think I've said anything nice about him yet in camp. I wanted to praise him today, but then he threw an interception right to Jalen Shermond, another player who won't make the team. It'll be nice to see Jones in the preseason game against the Chargers on Thursday considering he didn't play against the Titans and has yet to impress in camp. Chris Wrock has played much better than Jones so far. Left guard Connor Colbie. He was promoted to starting left guard after playing backup right guard for the past week. That's the good news. The not so good news is that Colbie was awful and routinely gave up penetration on runs and passes to Osa Odighizuwa. The Niners simply don't have a starting caliber left guard. Robert Jones certainly doesn't qualify. He's worse than Colbie. Perhaps rookie Carver Willis can take his job eventually, but he has a long way to go.

All the Niners best moves under Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch have been big trades. This should be the next one.
